title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
山東鄉試錄序
嘉靖乙酉春監察御史張〔英〕
來按東土貞肅憲度首謂先
任左布政使林〔琦〕曰維茲秋
逢鄉試之期事莫重焉盍慎
諸乃循舊典延聘文儒董茲
試事以至百爾執事罔不遴
===
選以充既慎以詳也届期〔鋼〕
暨教諭安〔常〕鄧〔林〕秦〔行〕賔徐
儁訓導吳〔山〕黃〔敏〕劉〔怡〕陳〔鈞〕
胥應聘而至罔敢不欽用協
厥職于時巡撫都御史王〔堯〕
封作則敦化已克底績而愛
賢下士則又有鎮守太監王
punctuated:
山東鄉試錄序

嘉靖乙酉春，監察御史張〔英〕來按東土，貞肅憲度，首謂先任左布政使林〔琦〕曰：「維茲秋逢鄉試之期，事莫重焉，盍慎諸？」乃循舊典，延聘文儒，董茲試事，以至百爾執事，罔不遴選以充，既慎以詳也。届期，〔鋼〕暨教諭安〔常〕、鄧〔林〕、秦〔行〕賔、徐儁，訓導吳〔山〕、黃〔敏〕、劉〔怡〕、陳〔鈞〕，胥應聘而至，罔敢不欽，用協厥職。于時，巡撫都御史王〔堯〕封作則敦化，已克底績；而愛賢下士，則又有鎮守太監王
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Shandong Provincial Examination

In the spring of the yiyou year of Jiajing [1525], Investigating Censor Zhang Ying came to inspect Shandong and uphold the disciplinary standards with strict rectitude. He first addressed the former Left Provincial Administration Commissioner, Lin Qi: “This autumn is the appointed time for the Provincial Examination. Nothing is more important. Should we not attend to it with care?” Accordingly, following established precedents, they invited learned scholars to oversee the examination. All those serving in its various capacities were likewise carefully selected to fill their posts. The preparations were both cautious and thorough.

When the appointed time arrived, I, Gang [surname not supplied], together with the Instructors An Chang, Deng Lin, Qin Xingbin [?], and Xu Jun, and the Assistant Instructors Wu Shan, Huang Min, Liu Yi, and Chen Jun, all came in response to the invitations. None dared to be other than reverent, and together we fulfilled our duties. At that time, Wang Yaofeng, Grand Coordinator and Censor-in-Chief, had already achieved results by setting an example and strengthening moral instruction. In cherishing worthy men and treating scholars with humility, there was also the Defender, Grand Eunuch Wang …

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
思〔競〕雅德崇文則又有總理
河道都御史章〔拯〕而清戎監
察御史杜〔民表〕巡鹽監察御
史鄧〔顯麒〕亦相與振作之以
部事至而觀厥成則郎中錢
〔瀾〕員外郎郭〔日休〕主事黃一
道高〔汝行〕丘〔其仁〕陳〔良謨〕董
===
漢〔策〕蕭〔璆〕白〔沛〕提調則右布
政使潘〔塤〕左參政江〔曉〕監試
則按察使潘〔珍〕副使錢〔宏〕若
左布政使郭〔韶〕左參政常〔道〕
右參政王〔潮〕左參議劉〔淑相〕
右參議方〔楷〕侯〔位〕副使馬〔應〕
〔龍〕熊〔相〕馮〔時雍〕趙〔春〕屠〔垚〕牛
punctuated: 思〔競〕。雅德崇文，則又有總理河道都御史章〔拯〕，而清戎監察御史杜〔民表〕、巡鹽監察御史鄧〔顯麒〕亦相與振作之。以部事至而觀厥成，則郎中錢〔瀾〕、員外郎郭〔日休〕、主事黃一道、高〔汝行〕、丘〔其仁〕、陳〔良謨〕、董漢〔策〕、蕭〔璆〕、白〔沛〕。提調則右布政使潘〔塤〕、左參政江〔曉〕；監試則按察使潘〔珍〕、副使錢〔宏〕。若左布政使郭〔韶〕、左參政常〔道〕、右參政王〔潮〕、左參議劉〔淑相〕、右參議方〔楷〕、侯〔位〕、副使馬〔應〕〔龍〕、熊〔相〕、馮〔時雍〕、趙〔春〕、屠〔垚〕、牛
translation_en: …[Wang] Sijing 思競. For refined virtue and esteem for literary learning, there was also Zhang Zheng 章拯, Censor-in-chief and Director-general of River Conservancy. Du Minbiao 杜民表, Investigating Censor responsible for inspecting military affairs, and Deng Xianqi 鄧顯麒, Investigating Censor for Salt Inspection, likewise joined in promoting the undertaking. Those who arrived on ministry business and witnessed its completion were Qian Lan 錢瀾, Bureau Director; Guo Rixiu 郭日休, Vice Director; and the Secretaries Huang Yidao 黃一道, Gao Ruxing 高汝行, Qiu Qiren 丘其仁, Chen Liangmo 陳良謨, Dong Hance 董漢策, Xiao Qiu 蕭璆, and Bai Pei 白沛. Serving as Proctors were Pan Xun 潘塤, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner, and Jiang Xiao 江曉, Left Administration Vice Commissioner. Supervising the examination were Pan Zhen 潘珍, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner, and Qian Hong 錢宏, Surveillance Vice Commissioner. As for Guo Shao 郭韶, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner; Chang Dao 常道, Left Administration Vice Commissioner; Wang Chao 王潮, Right Administration Vice Commissioner; Liu Shuxiang 劉淑相, Left Administration Assistant Commissioner; Fang Kai 方楷 and Hou Wei 侯位, Right Administration Assistant Commissioners; and the Surveillance Vice Commissioners Ma Yinglong 馬應龍, Xiong Xiang 熊相, Feng Shiyong 馮時雍, Zhao Chun 趙春, Tu Yao 屠垚, and Niu…

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
鸞王〔騰〕王〔言〕僉事謝〔芝〕陳〔個〕
韓〔璒〕李〔崧〕〔祥〕邊〔寧〕陳〔德〕〔鳴〕顧
〔璪〕又僉與先後贊襄都指揮
僉事何〔浩〕馬〔縉〕李〔麒〕周〔南〕又
皆效力防範乃合遼東巡按
監察御史王〔正〕〔宗〕山東提學
僉事高〔尚〕〔賢〕所選士一千八
===
百有奇三試之拔其尤者七
十有五錄成〔鋼〕屬當序諸首
竊惟文王興周化先汝漢故
召南稱首列國干城好仇之
才生焉孟子論夷惠之風興
起後人孔孟可知矣至若申
甫生於崧嶽夫子降於尼山
punctuated:
鸞、王〔騰〕、王〔言〕、僉事謝〔芝〕、陳〔個〕、韓〔璒〕、李〔崧〕〔祥〕、邊〔寧〕、陳〔德〕〔鳴〕、顧〔璪〕，又僉與先後贊襄。都指揮僉事何〔浩〕、馬〔縉〕、李〔麒〕、周〔南〕，又皆效力防範。乃合遼東巡按監察御史王〔正〕〔宗〕、山東提學僉事高〔尚〕〔賢〕所選士一千八百有奇，三試之，拔其尤者七十有五。錄成，〔鋼〕屬當序諸首。

竊惟文王興周，化先汝漢，故召南稱首列國，干城好仇之才生焉。孟子論夷惠之風，興起後人，孔孟可知矣。至若申甫生於崧嶽，夫子降於尼山，
translation_en:
…Niu Luan, Wang Teng, and Wang Yan, together with Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Xie Zhi, Chen Ge, Han Deng, Li Songxiang, Bian Ning, Chen Deming, and Gu Zao, all likewise assisted at successive stages. Assistant Regional Military Commissioners He Hao, Ma Jin, Li Qi, and Zhou Nan also devoted their efforts to security and precautions. The candidates selected by Wang Zhengzong, Investigating Censor on a巡按 inspection tour of Liaodong, and Gao Shangxian, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner responsible for education in Shandong, were then assembled, numbering more than eighteen hundred. They were examined in three sessions, and seventy-five of the most outstanding were selected. When the record was completed, I, Gang, was charged with writing a preface to place at its beginning.

I humbly reflect that when King Wen brought Zhou to prominence, his transforming influence first reached the Ru and Han regions. Thus the Airs of Shao ranked foremost among the states, and men capable of serving as shields and walls of the realm and as worthy partners arose there. Mencius discussed how the moral influence of Bo Yi and Liu Xiahui inspired later generations; from this, the influence of Confucius and Mencius may be understood. As for Shen and Fu being born through the power of Mount Song, and the Master being born at Mount Ni…

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
地靈人傑之說又今昔以爲
信然是王者之化聖賢之澤
山川之秀皆賢才之所自也
我
朝定鼎北畿維山東爲首化之
區亦今之江漢汝墳也孔孟
鄉邑風澤未斬視海內爲矣
而滄海泰山宗表天下其秀
===
而靈也莫大焉夫
聖化有感而必變矧其先焉師澤
有聞而必興矧其厚焉地靈
有萃而必秀矧其大焉三者
籍一可矣又矧乎其備也哉
士生此邦固宜迥拔秀出而
punctuated:
地靈人傑之說，又今昔以爲信然。是王者之化、聖賢之澤、山川之秀，皆賢才之所自也。
我朝定鼎北畿，維山東爲首化之區，亦今之江漢汝墳也。孔孟鄉邑，風澤未斬，視海內爲矣。而滄海泰山，宗表天下，其秀而靈也莫大焉。夫聖化有感而必變，矧其先焉；師澤有聞而必興，矧其厚焉；地靈有萃而必秀，矧其大焉。三者籍一可矣，又矧乎其備也哉！士生此邦，固宜迥拔秀出而
translation_en:
…the saying that a land’s numinous potency produces outstanding people has likewise been held true in both ancient and modern times. Thus the transforming influence of kings, the beneficent legacy of sages and worthies, and the finest influences of mountains and rivers are all sources from which worthy talent arises.
Our dynasty established its capital in the northern metropolitan region. Shandong was among the first regions to receive its transforming influence: it is the Jiang and Han river region and the banks of the Ru of our own day. In the home country of Confucius and Mencius, their influence and beneficent legacy have not been cut off; compared with the rest of the realm, it is [?]. Moreover, the vast sea and Mount Tai stand as exemplars for all under Heaven; nothing surpasses the excellence and numinous potency of their influences. Wherever the sage ruler’s transforming influence is felt, change must follow—how much more so where it was received first! Wherever the teachers’ beneficent legacy is heard of, people must be stirred to emulation—how much more so where that legacy is profound! Wherever the land’s numinous potency gathers, outstanding talent must emerge—how much more so where that potency is great! To draw upon any one of these three would suffice; how much more, then, when all are present! Scholars born in this land surely ought to distinguish themselves far beyond others and excel, and…

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
倍視諸藩也夫生也有自而
成也有本宜思所以不負矣
是故化者道之倡也風者韻
之流也秀者氣之凝也是皆
有理而無迹有可會而無可
執焉者也夫無迹則易忽無
可執則易怠苟怠而忽則等
===
之人耳其何稟之足多是以
君子貴夫習也窮焉而愼所
養達焉而愼所爲不恃其所
稟而勉其所圖其始也有以
異乎吾之生其終也有以異
乎吾之成生定則事天成已
則盡性性命立而萬善備矣
punctuated: 倍視諸藩也。夫生也有自，而成也有本，宜思所以不負矣。是故化者，道之倡也；風者，韻之流也；秀者，氣之凝也。是皆有理而無迹，有可會而無可執焉者也。夫無迹則易忽，無可執則易怠。苟怠而忽，則等之人耳，其何稟之足多？是以君子貴夫習也。窮焉而愼所養，達焉而愼所爲，不恃其所稟，而勉其所圖。其始也，有以異乎吾之生；其終也，有以異乎吾之成。生定則事天，成已則盡性，性命立而萬善備矣。
translation_en:
…and stand twice as high in comparison with the other provinces. Birth has its source, and achievement its foundation; one should therefore consider how to live up to them. Thus, transforming influence gives the lead to the Way; inherited custom carries forward its resonance; outstanding talent is the concentrated essence of vital energy. All these have underlying principle but no visible trace: they can be apprehended, but cannot be grasped. What leaves no trace is easily overlooked; what cannot be grasped easily invites indifference. If one is indifferent and neglectful, one is merely an ordinary person: what is there to praise in one’s endowment?

For this reason, the gentleman values sustained practice. In obscurity, he takes care over what he cultivates; in prominence, he takes care over what he does. He does not rely on his endowment but strives toward his aims. At the outset, he thereby gives distinction to the life into which he was born; in the end, he thereby gives distinction to what he achieves. Once the foundation of life is established, he serves Heaven; once cultivation is accomplished, he fully realizes his nature. With his nature and Heaven’s mandate established, every virtue is complete.

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
由是
聖朝之化不為徒被而吾將有以
贊之孔孟之澤不為徒灸而
吾將有以衍之海嶽之秀不
為徒鍾而吾將有以重之茲
於是為不負矣夫試士以文
所出才緒餘耳士非盡在此
===
也即其所未盡而求其所當
盡文焉有以為之實肢焉有
以為之體由孔孟之途以識
聖明之化而成為海嶽之英斯幾
矣嗚呼二三子其思所以不
負是邦也哉
河南開封府鈞州新鄭縣儒
punctuated:
由是，聖朝之化不為徒被，而吾將有以贊之；孔孟之澤不為徒灸，而吾將有以衍之；海嶽之秀不為徒鍾，而吾將有以重之。茲於是為不負矣。夫試士以文，所出才緒餘耳，士非盡在此也。即其所未盡，而求其所當盡，文焉有以為之實，肢焉有以為之體，由孔孟之途以識聖明之化，而成為海嶽之英，斯幾矣。嗚呼！二三子其思所以不負是邦也哉！

河南開封府鈞州新鄭縣儒
translation_en:
… Thus, the transforming influence of the sagely dynasty will not merely extend to us: we shall have the means to assist it. The beneficent legacy of Confucius and Mencius will not merely warm us [?]: we shall have the means to carry it forward. The finest essence of the seas and mountains will not merely gather within us: we shall have the means to enhance it. Only then shall we have lived up to what we have received. Now, when men are examined through their writing, what they produce is merely the remnants of their talent; a man’s worth is not wholly contained therein. Starting from what their writing has not fully expressed, we seek what they ought fully to realize. Their writing will then have something to give it substance, and their limbs something to constitute their body [?]. Following the path of Confucius and Mencius, they will recognize the transforming influence of the sagely sovereign and become outstanding men of this land of seas and mountains. Then they will be close to the ideal. Ah! You gentlemen should consider how to live up to this region!

Henan, Kaifeng Prefecture, Junzhou, Xinzheng County, Confucian …

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text: 學教諭白綱謹序
punctuated: 學教諭白綱謹序。
translation_en: …Bai Gang, School Instructor, respectfully composed this preface.

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
嘉靖四年山東鄉試
監臨官
巡按山東監察御史張英〔伯含金吾右衛官籍通州三河縣人戊辰進士〕
提調官
山東等處承宣布政使司右布政使潘塤〔伯和直隸山陽縣人戊辰進士〕
山東等處承宣布政使司左參政江曉〔景熙浙江仁和縣人戊辰進士〕
監試官
山東等處提刑按察司按察使潘珍〔玉卿直隸婺源縣人壬戌進士〕
山東等處提刑按察司副使錢宏〔可容太醫院籍浙江錢塘縣人戊辰進士〕
===
考試官
河南開封府鈞州新鄭縣儒學教諭白鋼〔世堅陜西儀衛司人丙子貢士〕
直隸鎮江府丹徒縣儒學教諭安常〔德懿湖廣襄陽縣人壬午貢士〕
同考試官
河南開封府通許縣儒學教諭鄧材〔達卿湖廣武昌護衛人己卯貢士〕
浙江寧波府鄞縣儒學教諭秦行賓〔體觀福建候官縣人癸酉貢士〕
河南南陽府鄧州淅川縣儒學教諭徐儁〔子用廣西護衛人癸酉貢士〕
直隸松江府上海縣儒學訓導吳山〔仁重江西安福縣人丁卯貢士〕
直隸揚州府高郵州寶應縣儒學訓導黃敏〔本仁貴州興隆衛人甲子貢士〕
punctuated:
嘉靖四年山東鄉試

監臨官
巡按山東監察御史張英〔伯含，金吾右衛官籍，通州三河縣人，戊辰進士〕。

提調官
山東等處承宣布政使司右布政使潘塤〔伯和，直隸山陽縣人，戊辰進士〕。
山東等處承宣布政使司左參政江曉〔景熙，浙江仁和縣人，戊辰進士〕。

監試官
山東等處提刑按察司按察使潘珍〔玉卿，直隸婺源縣人，壬戌進士〕。
山東等處提刑按察司副使錢宏〔可容，太醫院籍，浙江錢塘縣人，戊辰進士〕。

考試官
河南開封府鈞州新鄭縣儒學教諭白鋼〔世堅，陜西儀衛司人，丙子貢士〕。
直隸鎮江府丹徒縣儒學教諭安常〔德懿，湖廣襄陽縣人，壬午貢士〕。

同考試官
河南開封府通許縣儒學教諭鄧材〔達卿，湖廣武昌護衛人，己卯貢士〕。
浙江寧波府鄞縣儒學教諭秦行賓〔體觀，福建候官縣人，癸酉貢士〕。
河南南陽府鄧州淅川縣儒學教諭徐儁〔子用，廣西護衛人，癸酉貢士〕。
直隸松江府上海縣儒學訓導吳山〔仁重，江西安福縣人，丁卯貢士〕。
直隸揚州府高郵州寶應縣儒學訓導黃敏〔本仁，貴州興隆衛人，甲子貢士〕。
translation_en:
Shandong Provincial Examination, Fourth Year of Jiajing (1525)

Supervising Official
Zhang Ying, Investigating Censor on a surveillance tour of Shandong; courtesy name Bohan. He was registered in an official household of the Jinwu Right Guard and was a native of Sanhe County, Tongzhou; metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the wuchen year.

Proctors
Pan Xun, Right Administration Commissioner of the Shandong Provincial Administration Commission; courtesy name Bohe. He was a native of Shanyang County, Zhili; metropolitan graduate of the wuchen year.
Jiang Xiao, Left Administration Vice Commissioner of the Shandong Provincial Administration Commission; courtesy name Jingxi. He was a native of Renhe County, Zhejiang; metropolitan graduate of the wuchen year.

Examination Monitors
Pan Zhen, Surveillance Commissioner of the Shandong Provincial Surveillance Commission; courtesy name Yuqing. He was a native of Wuyuan County, Zhili; metropolitan graduate of the renxu year.
Qian Hong, Surveillance Vice Commissioner of the Shandong Provincial Surveillance Commission; courtesy name Kerong. He was registered with the Imperial Medical Institute and was a native of Qiantang County, Zhejiang; metropolitan graduate of the wuchen year.

Examiners
Bai Gang, Instructor at the Confucian school of Xinzheng County, Junzhou, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan; courtesy name Shijian. He was from the Ceremonial Guard Office in Shaanxi; tribute scholar (gongshi) of the bingzi year.

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
君子務本本立而道生孝弟也者其為仁
之本與
莫見乎隱莫顯乎微故君子慎其獨也
諫行言聽膏澤下於民
易
大有元亨
六二不耕穫不菑畬則利有攸往
以言乎遠則不禦以言乎邇則靜而正
戰乎乾勞乎坎
===
書
予欲左右有民汝翼予欲宣力四方汝為
庶土交正厎慎財賦咸則三壤成賦中邦
百穀用成乂用明俊民用章家用平康
自古商人亦越我周文王立政立事牧夫
準人則克宅之克由繹之茲乃俾乂
詩
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書
君子務本，本立而道生。孝弟也者，其為仁之本與！
莫見乎隱，莫顯乎微，故君子慎其獨也。
諫行言聽，膏澤下於民。

易
大有，元亨。
六二，不耕穫，不菑畬，則利有攸往。
以言乎遠，則不禦；以言乎邇，則靜而正。
戰乎乾，勞乎坎。

書
予欲左右有民，汝翼；予欲宣力四方，汝為。
庶土交正，厎慎財賦，咸則三壤，成賦中邦。
百穀用成，乂用明，俊民用章，家用平康。
自古商人，亦越我周文王，立政、立事、牧夫、準人，則克宅之，克由繹之，茲乃俾乂。

詩
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books
The gentleman devotes himself to the root. Once the root is established, the Way grows from it. Surely filial devotion and respect for elder brothers are the root of practicing benevolence!
Nothing is more manifest than what is hidden, and nothing more evident than what is minute. Therefore the gentleman is watchful over himself when alone.
His remonstrances are acted upon and his words heeded, so that beneficence reaches the people.

Book of Changes (Yijing)
Great Possession: supreme success.
Six in the second place: reaping without plowing, obtaining cultivated fields without first clearing them—then it is favorable to have somewhere to go.
Speaking of what is distant, it knows no bounds; speaking of what is near, it is still and correct.
They contend in Qian and toil in Kan.

Book of Documents (Shujing)
When I wish to assist and guide the people, you are to aid me; when I wish to exert my strength throughout the four quarters, you are to act.
The various lands were properly assessed in relation to one another. Careful attention was given to their revenues and levies; all followed the three grades of soil, establishing the levies of the central realm.
Thus the grains ripen, government is enlightened, men of outstanding ability become distinguished, and households enjoy peace and well-being.
From ancient times, the men of Shang, and likewise King Wen of our Zhou, were able to place in office those responsible for government, those responsible for affairs, the shepherds of the people, and the officers of justice. They could follow and examine their conduct, and thus entrusted them with governing.

Book of Odes (Shijing)

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
七月流火八月萑葦蠶月條桑取彼斧斨
以伐遠揚猗彼女桑七月鳴鵙八月
載績載玄載黄我朱孔陽為公子裳
我有嘉賓德音孔昭視民不恌君子是則
是傚
古訓是式威儀是力
於皇来牟將受厥明明昭上帝迄用康年
春秋
冬齊人来歸衛俘〔莊公六年〕六月齊侯来
獻戎捷〔莊公三十有一年〕
諸侯遂救許〔僖公六年〕公孫敖帥師及諸
侯之大夫救徐〔僖公十有五年〕
六月公會宋公陳侯衛侯鄭伯許男曹伯
晉趙盾癸酉同盟于新城〔文公十有〕
四年
秋晉荀吳帥師伐鮮虞〔昭公十有五年〕八月
晉荀吳帥師滅陸渾之戎〔昭公十有〕
七年
punctuated:
七月流火，八月萑葦。蠶月條桑，取彼斧斨，以伐遠揚，猗彼女桑。七月鳴鵙，八月載績。載玄載黄，我朱孔陽，為公子裳。
我有嘉賓，德音孔昭。視民不恌，君子是則是傚。
古訓是式，威儀是力。
於皇来牟，將受厥明。明昭上帝，迄用康年。
春秋
冬，齊人来歸衛俘。〔莊公六年〕六月，齊侯来獻戎捷。〔莊公三十有一年〕
諸侯遂救許。〔僖公六年〕公孫敖帥師及諸侯之大夫救徐。〔僖公十有五年〕
六月，公會宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯、晉趙盾，癸酉，同盟于新城。〔文公十有〕四年。
秋，晉荀吳帥師伐鮮虞。〔昭公十有五年〕八月，晉荀吳帥師滅陸渾之戎。〔昭公十有〕七年。
translation_en:
In the seventh month, the Fire Star descends; in the eighth month, reeds and rushes are gathered. In the silkworm month, we prune the mulberries, taking axes and hatchets to cut the high, spreading branches, and bending down the young mulberries. In the seventh month, the shrike calls; in the eighth month, we begin spinning. We dye the threads black and yellow; our vermilion is brilliant indeed, to make skirts for the lord’s sons.

I have worthy guests, whose virtuous reputation shines brightly. They show the people no frivolity; gentlemen take them as their rule and example.

Take the ancient teachings as your model; devote yourself to dignified deportment.

Ah, splendid are the wheat and barley! We shall receive this bright gift. The radiant Lord on High has thus granted a year of plenty.

Spring and Autumn Annals

In winter, men of Qi came to deliver captives taken from Wei. 〔Sixth year of Duke Zhuang.〕 In the sixth month, the Marquis of Qi came to present spoils from his victory over the Rong. 〔Thirty-first year of Duke Zhuang.〕

The assembled lords thereupon went to the aid of Xu 許. 〔Sixth year of Duke Xi.〕 Gongsun Ao led an army and joined the grandees of the assembled lords in aiding Xu 徐. 〔Fifteenth year of Duke Xi.〕

In the sixth month, the duke met with the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, the Earl of Cao, and Zhao Dun of Jin. On the guiyou day, they jointly concluded a covenant at Xincheng. 〔Fourteenth year of Duke Wen.〕

In autumn, Xun Wu of Jin led an army to attack Xianyu. 〔Fifteenth year of Duke Zhao.〕 In the eighth month, Xun Wu of Jin led an army and destroyed the Rong of Luhun. 〔Seventeenth year of Duke Zhao.〕

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
禮記
禮樂之情同故明王以相沿也故事與時
並名與功偕
著存不忘乎心夫安得不敬乎
貴其不已如日月東西相從而不已也是
天道也不閉其久是天道也無為而
物成是天道也已成而明是天道也
故君子信讓以涖百姓則民之報禮重
第貳場
===
論
虛心以為天下
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢舉賢良方正能直言極諫者詔〔文帝〕
二年
擬唐以韓休同平章事誥〔開元二十一年〕
擬宋崇政殿說書趙師民獻勸講箴表〔慶〕
曆四年
判語〔五條〕
punctuated:
禮記
禮樂之情同，故明王以相沿也。故事與時並，名與功偕。
著存，不忘乎心，夫安得不敬乎？
貴其不已，如日月東西相從而不已也，是天道也；不閉其久，是天道也；無為而物成，是天道也；已成而明，是天道也。
故君子信讓以涖百姓，則民之報禮重。
第貳場
論
虛心以為天下。
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢舉賢良方正能直言極諫者詔〔文帝〕二年。
擬唐以韓休同平章事誥〔開元二十一年〕。
擬宋崇政殿說書趙師民獻勸講箴表〔慶〕曆四年。
判語〔五條〕
translation_en:
Book of Rites

“The essential feelings expressed in ritual and music are the same; hence enlightened kings have continued them from one reign to the next. Thus undertakings accord with their times, and names correspond to achievements.”

“They are vividly present, never forgotten in the heart. How, then, could one fail to be reverent?”

“What is valued is its ceaselessness, like the sun and moon following one another from east to west without end: this is the Way of Heaven. To endure without cessation is the Way of Heaven. For things to reach completion without deliberate action is the Way of Heaven. To become manifest once completed is the Way of Heaven.”

“Thus, when the gentleman presides over the common people with trustworthiness and deference, the people respond with profound propriety.”

Second Session

Discourse

“Emptying one’s mind to govern all under Heaven.”

Imperial Edicts, Proclamations, and Memorials [One topic from among these categories [?].]

Compose, in imitation of the Han, an imperial edict calling for the recommendation of worthy, good, upright, and principled men capable of speaking frankly and remonstrating with utmost directness. [Emperor Wen,] second year.

Compose, in imitation of the Tang, a proclamation appointing Han Xiu as Joint Manager of Affairs with the Secretariat-Chancellery. [Twenty-first year of Kaiyuan.]

Compose, in imitation of the Song, a memorial in which Zhao Shimin, Expositor in Chongzheng Hall, presents an admonition encouraging imperial lectures. [Fourth year of Qingli.]

Legal Judgments [Five items.]

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
官員赴任過限
錢糧互相覺察
禁止師巫邪術
縱放軍人歇役
失時不脩隄防
第叄場
策五道
問箕子陳洪範五行休咎各以類應至漢
儒始為之傳而歷代史氏所述災異因
===
之然必曰某事召某災合某應者是果
有所驗而言歟夫孔子脩春秋紀變異
而不著其事應漢儒皆治春秋者又何
所稽而著其事應歟以為有應也或者
謂天災不可以象類求以為無應也或
者謂陰陽之理各應其感是必有定說
矣誕惟
太祖高皇帝因講洪範至休咎之應語講臣曰
上下交脩斯格天之本又嘗命儒臣纂
punctuated:
官員赴任過限。
錢糧互相覺察。
禁止師巫邪術。
縱放軍人歇役。
失時不脩隄防。

第叄場
策五道

問：箕子陳《洪範》，五行休咎各以類應，至漢儒始為之傳，而歷代史氏所述災異因之。然必曰某事召某災、合某應者，是果有所驗而言歟？夫孔子脩《春秋》，紀變異而不著其事應，漢儒皆治《春秋》者，又何所稽而著其事應歟？以為有應也，或者謂天災不可以象類求；以為無應也，或者謂陰陽之理各應其感。是必有定說矣。誕惟太祖高皇帝因講《洪範》，至休咎之應，語講臣曰：「上下交脩，斯格天之本。」又嘗命儒臣纂
translation_en:
Officials exceeding the time limit for taking up their appointments.
Mutual scrutiny of matters concerning money and grain.
Prohibiting the heterodox arts of ritual masters and spirit mediums.
Allowing soldiers to absent themselves from duty.
Failing to repair dikes and embankments at the proper season.

Third Session
Five Policy Questions

Question: When Jizi expounded the Great Plan (Hongfan), the auspicious and inauspicious signs associated with the Five Phases each corresponded according to their kind. Only with the Han Confucian scholars were commentaries on this produced, and the accounts of disasters and anomalies by historians of successive dynasties followed them. Yet when they invariably state that a particular affair brought on a particular disaster and matched a particular correspondence, were these assertions truly based on verified evidence? Confucius, in editing the Spring and Autumn Annals, recorded unusual phenomena but did not specify the human affairs to which they corresponded. The Han Confucian scholars all studied the Spring and Autumn Annals; on what evidence, then, did they record such correspondences? If one holds that there are correspondences, some say that heavenly disasters cannot be explained by seeking similarities of form and category. If one holds that there are none, others say that, according to the principles of yin and yang, each responds to what stimulates it. Surely there must be a settled explanation of this.

We solemnly recall that Emperor Taizu Gao, during a lecture on the Great Plan, upon reaching the correspondences of auspicious and inauspicious signs, told the lecturing officials: “Those above and below must cultivate themselves together: this is the foundation for moving Heaven.” He also once ordered his Confucian officials to compile…

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
集存心省躬二錄凡歷代帝王祭祀而
有感于災祥及漢唐宋以來災祥之應
于臣下者皆載焉無非欲上下同其警
畏以致力于身心之間也
列聖相承同一警畏今我
皇上嗣守丕基克篤前烈中外臣工咸有中興
之望焉固宜天協應而休祥滋至也比
年以來災變頻仍近復有
仁壽宮災厥咎何由豈昔人所謂天心仁愛
===
欲有以警動之歟抑或有所感而然歟
不知何脩何為而可以荅天變也試敬
陳之以為
當宁格天之謨
問賞罰者礪世之具也賞當功則人莫不
勸罰當罪則人莫不懲故天命天討陳
于虞書不僭不濫播于商頌八則八柄
著于周禮自古帝王未有不率此以治
天下者後之令主何莫不然若漢宣帝
punctuated:
集《存心》《省躬》二錄，凡歷代帝王祭祀而有感于災祥，及漢唐宋以來災祥之應于臣下者，皆載焉。無非欲上下同其警畏，以致力于身心之間也。列聖相承，同一警畏。今我皇上嗣守丕基，克篤前烈，中外臣工咸有中興之望焉。固宜天協應而休祥滋至也。比年以來，災變頻仍，近復有仁壽宮災，厥咎何由？豈昔人所謂天心仁愛，欲有以警動之歟？抑或有所感而然歟？不知何脩何為而可以荅天變也？試敬陳之，以為當宁格天之謨。

問：賞罰者，礪世之具也。賞當功，則人莫不勸；罰當罪，則人莫不懲。故天命天討陳于《虞書》，不僭不濫播于《商頌》，八則八柄著于《周禮》。自古帝王未有不率此以治天下者，後之令主何莫不然？若漢宣帝
translation_en:
…to compile the two records, Preserving the Mind and Examining Oneself. These recorded all instances in which emperors and kings of successive ages performed sacrifices in response to disasters or auspicious signs, as well as instances from the Han, Tang, and Song onward in which disasters and auspicious signs manifested their correspondences in the lives of officials. The purpose was invariably to have ruler and ministers share the same vigilance and reverence, applying themselves to the cultivation of body and mind. The successive sage emperors inherited this same vigilance and reverence. Now Our Emperor has inherited and safeguards the great imperial foundation and earnestly carries forward his predecessors’ achievements. Officials at court and throughout the realm all look forward to a resurgence. Surely Heaven should respond harmoniously and auspicious signs arrive in abundance. Yet in recent years disasters and anomalies have occurred repeatedly, and lately there has also been a fire at Renshou Palace. What fault brought this about? Is it, as men of former times said, that Heaven’s heart is benevolent and loving, and seeks thereby to warn and stir the ruler? Or has something elicited this response? What should be cultivated, and what action taken, to respond to Heaven’s portents? Set forth your views respectfully, to provide the reigning sovereign with a plan for moving Heaven.

Question: Rewards and punishments are instruments for encouraging and admonishing the world. When rewards match achievements, everyone is encouraged; when punishments match offenses, everyone is deterred. Thus Heaven’s appointments and Heaven’s chastisements are set forth in the Documents of Yu; rewards without error and punishments without excess are celebrated in the Hymns of Shang; and the eight regulations and eight instruments of authority are recorded in the Rites of Zhou. From antiquity, no emperor or king has failed to follow these principles in governing the realm. What worthy ruler of later times did otherwise? Take Emperor Xuan of the Han…

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
之詔王成唐文皇之諭房玄齡宋太宗
之諭宋琪皆以賞罰為言夷攷其時所
賞所罰果盡當乎抑徒言之而弗允蹈
之也仰惟
聖天子嗣服之初誕布
明詔忠諫則旌之節義則表之倖位則黜之
奸黨則誅之雖大舜之四罪武王之大
賚何以加焉不知
今日之賞罰果盡如歟初乎諸生服官有日將
===
何言以為
丹扆規執事者願有聞也
問儒道與天地參也故夫子以儒行告哀
公以儒學教子夏士之所以立身國之
所以為治皆是賴矣但世之業儒者與
夫用儒者有可疑焉是故或以豎儒見
譏或以宿儒為貴何美惡之相絕也或
以俗儒為鄙或以大儒見稱何高下之
頓異也稱儒之名亦難矣何乃或為儒
punctuated:
之詔王成、唐文皇之諭房玄齡、宋太宗之諭宋琪，皆以賞罰為言。夷攷其時所賞所罰，果盡當乎？抑徒言之而弗允蹈之也？仰惟聖天子嗣服之初，誕布明詔：忠諫則旌之，節義則表之，倖位則黜之，奸黨則誅之。雖大舜之四罪、武王之大賚，何以加焉？不知今日之賞罰，果盡如歟初乎？諸生服官有日，將何言以為丹扆規？執事者願有聞也。

問：儒道與天地參也。故夫子以儒行告哀公，以儒學教子夏。士之所以立身，國之所以為治，皆是賴矣。但世之業儒者與夫用儒者，有可疑焉。是故或以豎儒見譏，或以宿儒為貴，何美惡之相絕也？或以俗儒為鄙，或以大儒見稱，何高下之頓異也？稱儒之名亦難矣，何乃或為儒
translation_en:
…the edict addressed to Wang Cheng, Emperor Wen of Tang’s instructions to Fang Xuanling, and Emperor Taizong of Song’s instructions to Song Qi all spoke of rewards and punishments. Examining the rewards and punishments of their times, were they indeed all appropriate? Or did these rulers merely speak of them without faithfully putting their words into practice? We reverently reflect that, at the beginning of his reign, our sagely Son of Heaven promulgated an illustrious edict far and wide: those who remonstrated loyally were to be honored; those of integrity and righteousness publicly commended; those who had gained office through favor dismissed; and members of treacherous factions executed. How could even the Great Shun’s punishment of the four offenders or King Wu’s lavish bestowal of rewards surpass this? We wonder whether today’s rewards and punishments are indeed entirely as they were at the beginning [?]. You students will one day hold office. What words will you offer as admonition to the imperial throne? We who administer this examination wish to hear them.

Question: The Way of the Confucian scholar stands alongside Heaven and Earth. Thus the Master explained the conduct of the Confucian scholar to Duke Ai and instructed Zixia in Confucian learning. Both the means by which scholars establish themselves and the means by which the state achieves good government depend upon it. Yet there are grounds for doubt concerning those in the world who pursue Confucian learning and those who employ Confucian scholars. Thus some are mocked as petty scholars, while others are esteemed as seasoned scholars. Why are these favorable and unfavorable judgments so far apart? Some are despised as vulgar scholars, while others are acclaimed as great scholars. Why is the difference in their standing so stark? It is indeed difficult to merit the name of Confucian scholar. How, then, do some become scholars who…

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
之高蹈或為儒之大醇歟得儒之道亦
罕矣何乃或為群儒之首或為世儒之
宗歟世之待儒者雅尚儒術與褒封儒
先似矣而治效何不加多不好儒者與
不任儒者非矣而治功何不加少三者
五吏既知尊崇何所建亦不古若也六
經四書既為大禁何危亡亦不速至也
夫考儒道醇駁之習究治道興衰之故
諸士子必有所見矣不知於古之用儒
者以何為是以何為非業儒者以何為
法以何為戒耶願卒言之將采而為
===
聖天子崇儒獻
問山東古齊魯之地也昔周公治魯太公
治齊其政宜無不善矣然一則有寖弱
之弊一則有爭奪之弊何歟毋乃各因
所尚而致之歟孔子曰齊一變至於魯
魯一變至於道然則周公之餘化固愈
於太公抑太公之餘化猶愈於他俗歟
punctuated:
之高蹈，或為儒之大醇歟？得儒之道亦罕矣，何乃或為群儒之首，或為世儒之宗歟？世之待儒者，雅尚儒術與褒封儒先似矣，而治效何不加多？不好儒者與不任儒者非矣，而治功何不加少？三者五吏既知尊崇，何所建亦不古若也？六經四書既為大禁，何危亡亦不速至也？夫考儒道醇駁之習，究治道興衰之故，諸士子必有所見矣。不知於古之用儒者，以何為是，以何為非？業儒者，以何為法，以何為戒耶？願卒言之，將采而為聖天子崇儒獻。
問：山東，古齊魯之地也。昔周公治魯，太公治齊，其政宜無不善矣。然一則有寖弱之弊，一則有爭奪之弊，何歟？毋乃各因所尚而致之歟？孔子曰：「齊一變至於魯，魯一變至於道。」然則周公之餘化固愈於太公，抑太公之餘化猶愈於他俗歟？
translation_en:
…one who stands loftily apart among Confucians, or one of great purity among Confucians? Attaining the Way of the Confucians is also rare; how, then, have some become leaders of the assembled Confucians, or exemplary masters for the Confucians of their age? In the world’s treatment of Confucians, esteeming Confucian learning and bestowing honors and titles upon earlier Confucian masters seem proper; why, then, have the results of government not increased? Disliking Confucians and declining to employ them are wrong; why, then, have the achievements of government not diminished? When rulers knew to honor the “three persons and five officials” [?], why did their accomplishments still fall short of antiquity? When the Six Classics and Four Books were strictly prohibited, why did peril and ruin not arrive swiftly? You candidates must surely have views on the practices through which the Confucian Way became pure or mixed, and on the causes of flourishing and decline in government. Among those in antiquity who employed Confucians, what do you consider right, and what wrong? For those who pursue Confucian learning, what should serve as a model, and what as a warning? Please explain fully. Your words will be gathered into an offering to our sagely Son of Heaven in support of his honoring Confucian learning.
Question: Shandong is the ancient territory of Qi and Lu. Formerly, the Duke of Zhou governed Lu, and Taigong governed Qi; their governments ought to have been good in every respect. Yet one suffered from gradual weakening, and the other from rivalry and contention. Why was this? Might these consequences have arisen from what each esteemed? Confucius said: “With one transformation, Qi could attain to Lu; with one transformation, Lu could attain to the Way.” Thus, was the enduring influence of the Duke of Zhou’s civilizing work indeed superior to that of Taigong, while Taigong’s enduring influence was still superior to the customs elsewhere?

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
說者又謂齊之士好經術矜功名其失
夸詐魯之民上禮義重廉耻其俗儉嗇
其然歟抑何以致是歟不知今之士習
民風尚猶昔否也越漢唐宋其牧齊者
或以恩信化盜或以詩書訓士或以賑
濟活民其牧魯者或以清約束下或以
仁信為政或以剛嚴决事其政固不同
也不知其孰優抑不知今之牧斯民者
將安法而可諸生固齊魯之良也必知
之素矣尚明著于篇以為牧民者告
===
問為政莫先於平民平民之大要在賦與
役而已故書貴任土之貢傳稱力役之
征斯民之休戚誠視此二端為輕重也
然而行者有不同之規論者有各殊之
指自夫賦稅言之什一而稅中正之道
也後世輕者或五十而稅一或三十而
稅一重者或收太半之賦或作兩稅之
法盖桀與貉之異也然輕者不見其歟
punctuated:
說者又謂：「齊之士好經術，矜功名，其失夸詐；魯之民上禮義，重廉耻，其俗儉嗇。」其然歟？抑何以致是歟？不知今之士習民風尚猶昔否也？越漢唐宋，其牧齊者，或以恩信化盜，或以詩書訓士，或以賑濟活民；其牧魯者，或以清約束下，或以仁信為政，或以剛嚴决事。其政固不同也，不知其孰優？抑不知今之牧斯民者，將安法而可？諸生固齊魯之良也，必知之素矣。尚明著于篇，以為牧民者告。

問：為政莫先於平民，平民之大要在賦與役而已。故《書》貴任土之貢，《傳》稱力役之征，斯民之休戚誠視此二端為輕重也。然而行者有不同之規，論者有各殊之指。自夫賦稅言之，什一而稅，中正之道也。後世輕者，或五十而稅一，或三十而稅一；重者，或收太半之賦，或作兩稅之法。盖桀與貉之異也。然輕者不見其歟
translation_en:
… Commentators further say: “The scholars of Qi delight in classical learning and pride themselves on achievements and reputation; their failings are boastfulness and deceit. The people of Lu esteem ritual propriety and righteousness and value integrity and a sense of shame; their customs are frugal and parsimonious.” Is this so? And what brought this about? Do the habits of scholars and the customs of the people today still resemble those of former times? Throughout the Han, Tang, and Song dynasties, some who governed Qi reformed bandits through kindness and trustworthiness; some instructed scholars through the Odes and the Documents; and some saved the people through relief. Among those who governed Lu, some restrained their subordinates through personal integrity and frugality; some governed with benevolence and trustworthiness; and some decided affairs with firmness and severity. Their methods of government certainly differed. Which was superior? Moreover, what model should those who govern these people today follow? You candidates are surely the outstanding men of Qi and Lu and must have long been familiar with these matters. Set them forth clearly in your essays to instruct those who govern the people.

Question: In government, nothing takes precedence over bringing peace to the people. The essentials of doing so lie simply in taxation and labor service. Thus the Book of Documents values tribute assessed according to the land’s productive capacity, and the Commentary speaks of levies of labor service. The well-being or suffering of these people truly depends upon the weight of these two burdens. Yet those who implement them follow different rules, and those who discuss them advance differing interpretations. As for taxation, to levy one part in ten is the balanced and proper way. In later ages, lighter rates sometimes took one part in fifty or one part in thirty; heavier exactions sometimes collected two-thirds, or instituted the Twice-a-Year Tax system. This is indeed the difference between Jie and the Mo people. Yet where taxation was light, one does not see their [?] …

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
重者不見其羸何歟自夫力役言之歲
役三日亦經久之規也後世簡者至有
一歲二旬之役孝弟力田免役之條繁
者至有七科之謫與夫三更之役蓋仁
與苛之分也然簡者未見甚樂繁者未
見甚苦何歟論賦民者有謂古者非特
什一之稅彼豈無所見又有謂誦聲作
於什一者厥指則有異矣論役民者有
謂百姓亡事則驕逸勞役則易使是豈
===
無所試又有謂愛日由於省役者其說
復可疑矣夫賦既可輕重矣而什一之
制卒不復役既易增損矣而三日之規
卒不踵豈時勢有不相宜歟將識見之
有所異歟我
朝稽古定制其賦與役皆成周之法也夫何
比歲以來蠲租之
詔屢下而吾民之財愈削輕徭之政甚詳而吾
民之力轉困揆之於人事既無由歸之
punctuated: 重者不見其羸，何歟？自夫力役言之，歲役三日，亦經久之規也。後世簡者，至有一歲二旬之役、孝弟力田免役之條；繁者，至有七科之謫與夫三更之役，蓋仁與苛之分也。然簡者未見甚樂，繁者未見甚苦，何歟？論賦民者，有謂古者非特什一之稅，彼豈無所見？又有謂誦聲作於什一者，厥指則有異矣。論役民者，有謂百姓亡事則驕逸，勞役則易使，是豈無所試？又有謂愛日由於省役者，其說復可疑矣。夫賦既可輕重矣，而什一之制卒不復；役既易增損矣，而三日之規卒不踵。豈時勢有不相宜歟？將識見之有所異歟？我朝稽古定制，其賦與役皆成周之法也。夫何比歲以來，蠲租之詔屢下，而吾民之財愈削；輕徭之政甚詳，而吾民之力轉困？揆之於人事，既無由，歸之
translation_en:
…yet those subjected to heavier taxation do not appear impoverished. Why is this? As for labor service, requiring three days of service each year was likewise a rule intended to endure. In later ages, lighter arrangements included twenty days of service a year and provisions exempting those distinguished for filial piety, fraternal respect, or diligence in farming; heavier arrangements included penal conscription under seven categories and service in three rotations. These presumably mark the distinction between benevolence and harshness. Yet under the lighter arrangements the people do not appear particularly happy, nor under the heavier ones particularly distressed. Why is this?

Among those discussing taxation of the people, some maintain that taxation in antiquity was not limited to a tithe. Surely they had some grounds for this view? Others maintain that songs of praise arose because of the tithe: their meaning is different. Among those discussing the people's labor service, some maintain that when the common people have nothing to do, they become arrogant and idle, whereas labor service makes them easy to command. Surely this view had some basis in experience? Others maintain that cherishing the people's time requires reducing labor service. Their account, too, invites doubt.

Now, although taxation can be made lighter or heavier, the system of the tithe has never been restored; although labor service can readily be increased or reduced, the rule of three days has never again been followed. Is this because circumstances have made these arrangements unsuitable, or because people's judgments differ? Our dynasty examined antiquity in establishing its institutions: its taxation and labor service alike follow the laws of the Zhou at its height. Why, then, in recent years, despite repeated edicts remitting taxes, has our people's wealth dwindled ever further? And why, despite detailed measures to lighten labor service, has our people's strength become increasingly exhausted? Examining human affairs affords no basis for explaining this; to attribute it to…

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
於歲凶又不可不知何如處而後濟也
諸生行將有爲民之責願言所以平民
之政
punctuated: 於歲凶，又不可。不知何如處而後濟也？諸生行將有爲民之責，願言所以平民之政。
translation_en: …to years of poor harvest is also untenable. How, then, should this situation be handled so that relief may be achieved? You candidates will soon bear responsibility for the people; please set forth the measures of government by which the people may be brought peace and security.

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
君子務本本立而道生孝弟也者其為仁
之本與
曹卿
同考試官教諭秦　批〔體貼有子立言之意親切有味似得其謦欬者〕
考試官教諭安　批　精醇典雅可嘉
考試官教諭白　批〔詞以理發可謂知本之學〕
===
賢者言君子事當圖其本必指行仁之本以見
之也夫本立而道自生本固所當務也然則為
仁之本其在於孝弟乎昔有子因論孝弟而其
意若謂君子之學以道充為貴以務本為先知
事在天下莫不有本也專心致志而加敦篤之
功不泛用其力焉知事必有本在所當務也身
體力行以為持循之地不徒事于末焉由是所
務者專而其本以立道之散于事者自爾生不
punctuated:
第壹場
四書
「君子務本，本立而道生。孝弟也者，其為仁之本與！」
曹卿
同考試官教諭秦批〔體貼有子立言之意，親切有味，似得其謦欬者。〕
考試官教諭安批：精醇典雅，可嘉。
考試官教諭白批〔詞以理發，可謂知本之學。〕
賢者言君子事當圖其本，必指行仁之本以見之也。夫本立而道自生，本固所當務也。然則為仁之本，其在於孝弟乎？昔有子因論孝弟，而其意若謂君子之學，以道充為貴，以務本為先。知事在天下莫不有本也，專心致志而加敦篤之功，不泛用其力焉；知事必有本在所當務也，身體力行以為持循之地，不徒事于末焉。由是所務者專，而其本以立，道之散于事者自爾生不
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books
“The gentleman attends to the root. Once the root is established, the Way grows forth. Surely filial devotion and respect for elder brothers are the root of practicing humaneness!”
Cao Qing
Associate Examiner Qin, Instructor, comments: “He sensitively grasps Youzi’s intent in making this statement. Intimate and full of savor, it seems to capture Youzi’s very voice.”
Examiner An, Instructor, comments: “Refined and pure, classically elegant: worthy of praise.”
Examiner Bai, Instructor, comments: “His phrasing proceeds from principle. This may be called learning that understands the root.”
The worthy said that, in his undertakings, the gentleman should attend to their root; he necessarily pointed to the root of practicing humaneness to make this clear. Once the root is established, the Way naturally grows forth: the root is indeed what one ought to attend to. Then does not the root of practicing humaneness lie in filial devotion and respect for elder brothers? When Youzi discussed filial devotion and brotherly respect, his meaning seemed to be that the gentleman’s learning prizes the fullness of the Way and gives priority to attending to the root. Knowing that every undertaking in the world has a root, he concentrates his mind and directs his purpose, applying himself with earnest devotion rather than expending his strength indiscriminately. Knowing that undertakings necessarily have a root to which he ought to attend, he personally puts this into practice as a basis for steadfast adherence, rather than merely concerning himself with peripheral matters. Thus, his efforts are concentrated and the root is established; the Way, as it extends throughout affairs, naturally grows forth, unable to…

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
可已而有觸處貫通之機所培者厚而其本益
固事之原于道者自爾發不可遏而有曲暢旁
通之妙本立而道自生如此若吾所謂孝弟者
善事其親而不至于悖德善事其長而不至于
悖禮雖曰庸行之常也然和順充積之天皆惻
怛慈愛之周流推而行之仁將不可勝用矣雖
曰庸德之行也然良心真切之地皆易直子諒
之發見擴而充之愛將無所不盡矣謂之為仁
之本或者其在玆乎是則道不易充也本立而
後可充仁不易為也孝弟而後可為然則人可
不躬行孝弟以為為仁之本耶抑論仁道至大
有子以孝弟言之何耶蓋仁者體而孝弟其用
也一言之間而仁之體用備矣自是而後周子
謂德愛曰仁張子謂仁統天下之善程子謂盡
性至命必本於孝弟其皆有得於有子之意而
發與若龜山以萬物一體為仁則遺體上蔡以
知覺為仁則遂用要之皆不足以名仁志於仁
者當知所從事矣
punctuated: 可已，而有觸處貫通之機；所培者厚，而其本益固，事之原于道者自爾發不可遏，而有曲暢旁通之妙。本立而道自生如此。若吾所謂孝弟者，善事其親而不至于悖德，善事其長而不至于悖禮，雖曰庸行之常也，然和順充積之天，皆惻怛慈愛之周流，推而行之，仁將不可勝用矣。雖曰庸德之行也，然良心真切之地，皆易直子諒之發見，擴而充之，愛將無所不盡矣。謂之為仁之本，或者其在玆乎？是則道不易充也，本立而後可充；仁不易為也，孝弟而後可為。然則人可不躬行孝弟，以為為仁之本耶？抑論仁道至大，有子以孝弟言之，何耶？蓋仁者體，而孝弟其用也，一言之間而仁之體用備矣。自是而後，周子謂德愛曰仁，張子謂仁統天下之善，程子謂盡性至命必本於孝弟，其皆有得於有子之意而發與？若龜山以萬物一體為仁，則遺體；上蔡以知覺為仁，則遂用。要之，皆不足以名仁。志於仁者，當知所從事矣。
translation_en:
…cannot cease, and there is the potential for comprehensive understanding wherever one turns. When what is nurtured grows substantial, its root becomes still firmer; affairs that have their source in the Way then emerge spontaneously and irresistibly, with the marvelous capacity to unfold fully in every particular and extend in every direction. Such is how, once the root is established, the Way naturally grows.

As for what I call filial piety and fraternal deference: serving one’s parents well without violating virtue, and serving one’s elders well without violating ritual propriety, may be called ordinary, everyday conduct. Yet the Heaven-endowed nature in which harmony and compliance accumulate is entirely the circulation of compassion and loving concern. Extend these into action, and humaneness will be inexhaustible in its applications. Though these may be called the practice of everyday virtues, the genuine workings of the good heart are entirely manifestations of gentleness, uprightness, affection, and trustworthiness. Expand and fulfill them, and love will leave nothing unfulfilled. Might this be why they are called the root of practicing humaneness?

Thus the Way is not easily brought to fullness: only after the root is established can it be fulfilled. Humaneness is not easily practiced: only through filial piety and fraternal deference can it be practiced. Can people, then, fail personally to practice filial piety and fraternal deference as the root of practicing humaneness? Yet the Way of humaneness is supremely great. Why did Master You speak of it in terms of filial piety and fraternal deference? It is because humaneness is the substance, while filial piety and fraternal deference are its functioning. Within a single statement, both the substance and functioning of humaneness are fully present.

Thereafter, Master Zhou said that virtue expressed in love is called humaneness; Master Zhang said that humaneness encompasses all the goodness under Heaven; and Master Cheng said that fully realizing one’s nature and arriving at an understanding of Heaven’s mandate must be rooted in filial piety and fraternal deference. Were these pronouncements not all made through some grasp of Master You’s meaning? As for Guishan, who took forming one body with the myriad things as humaneness, he thereby leaves out its substance [?]; Shangcai, who took awareness as humaneness, thereby pursues its functioning [?]. In any event, neither is sufficient to define humaneness. Those who aspire to humaneness should know where to direct their efforts.

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
莫見乎隱莫顯乎微故君子慎其獨也
楊縉
同考試官訓導劉　批〔慎獨是省察工夫作者類以不敢忽為言似與存養無別是篇認理真〕
〔而措詞當故特録之以示學者〕
同考試官訓導黄　批〔體認親切而詞足以達之必嘗用功于獨者〕
考試官教諭安　批〔說理文字簡潔似此亦難〕
考試官教諭白　批〔講慎獨工夫語意精到可觀〕
===
中庸論君子體道必指其幾而示其功焉盖幾
之動至難掩也君子於此而致謹焉體道之功
切矣中庸論道不可離及此謂夫體道之功固
莫切於存養尤莫切於省察是故目所共睹者
人皆以為見也然見莫見於隱焉盖幽暗之中
迹雖未形而念慮之始幾則已動人固不知我
自知之甚於目之所共睹矣天下之事孰有著
punctuated:
「莫見乎隱，莫顯乎微，故君子慎其獨也。」
楊縉
同考試官訓導劉批〔慎獨是省察工夫，作者類以不敢忽為言，似與存養無別。是篇認理真〕〔而措詞當，故特録之以示學者。〕
同考試官訓導黄批〔體認親切，而詞足以達之，必嘗用功于獨者。〕
考試官教諭安批〔說理文字，簡潔似此亦難。〕
考試官教諭白批〔講慎獨工夫，語意精到可觀。〕
中庸論君子體道，必指其幾而示其功焉。盖幾之動至難掩也，君子於此而致謹焉，體道之功切矣。中庸論道不可離，及此謂夫體道之功，固莫切於存養，尤莫切於省察。是故目所共睹者，人皆以為見也；然見莫見於隱焉。盖幽暗之中，迹雖未形，而念慮之始，幾則已動。人固不知，我自知之，甚於目之所共睹矣。天下之事，孰有著
translation_en:
“Nothing is more visible than what is hidden; nothing is more manifest than what is minute. Therefore the gentleman is watchful over himself when alone.”

Yang Jin

Associate Examiner Liu, an Assistant Instructor, comments: “Watchfulness when alone is a practice of self-examination. Writers generally speak of it as not daring to be negligent, making it seem indistinguishable from preserving and nurturing the mind. This essay understands the principle truly and expresses it appropriately; hence it has been specially selected to show students.”

Associate Examiner Huang, an Assistant Instructor, comments: “The understanding is intimate and immediate, and the wording adequately conveys it. The author must have devoted effort to watchfulness when alone.”

Examiner An, an Instructor, comments: “In writing that expounds principles, such simplicity and concision are difficult to achieve.”

Examiner Bai, an Instructor, comments: “In discussing the practice of watchfulness when alone, the language and meaning are precise and penetrating, and worthy of attention.”

When the Doctrine of the Mean discusses how the gentleman embodies the Way, it necessarily points to the incipient stirrings of his thoughts and shows the effort required. For these stirrings, once set in motion, are exceedingly difficult to conceal. If the gentleman exercises care at this point, his efforts to embody the Way strike close to the essentials. The Doctrine of the Mean discusses how the Way cannot be departed from, and, on reaching this passage, says that in the effort to embody the Way, nothing is more essential than preserving and nurturing the mind, and still more essential is self-examination. Thus, what all eyes can see, everyone considers visible; yet nothing is more visible than what is hidden. For amid darkness and obscurity, although no outward trace has yet taken shape, at the very beginning of thought the incipient stirrings are already in motion. Others indeed do not know them, but I myself know them more clearly than what all eyes can see. Among the affairs of the world, what is manifest …

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
見而過于隱者邪耳所共聞者人皆以為顯也
然顯莫顯於微焉盖細微之事迹雖未露而思
慮之初幾則已萌人固不覺我自覺之甚於耳
之所共聞矣天下之事孰有明顯而過於微者
邪夫幾之不可掩如此是以君子不但戒慎于
所不睹而已於此獨睹之時尤必審之覯省益
力勿使人欲或滋而為天理之妨也敢曰人尚
未睹而苟焉以自欺乎不但恐懼于所不聞而
已於此獨聞之地尤必察之防檢益周勿使人
===
心或危而致道心之微也敢曰人尚未聞而怠
焉以自肆乎夫然則隱微之幾謹而省察之功
盡矣尚何離道之有哉抑體道之功非存養則
無以全本然之體非省察則無以謹善惡之幾
二者相須而後盡也故堯之命舜曰惟精惟一
一則存養之屬精則省察之屬也至後程子亦
曰涵養須用敬進學則在致知亦有合於二者
之旨焉然則子思之傳得非本之堯舜程子之
傳寧非得之子思哉觀中庸者宜於所授受者
punctuated:
見而過于隱者邪？耳所共聞者，人皆以為顯也，然顯莫顯於微焉。盖細微之事，迹雖未露，而思慮之初，幾則已萌。人固不覺，我自覺之，甚於耳之所共聞矣。天下之事，孰有明顯而過於微者邪？夫幾之不可掩如此，是以君子不但戒慎于所不睹而已，於此獨睹之時，尤必審之，覯省益力，勿使人欲或滋而為天理之妨也。敢曰人尚未睹，而苟焉以自欺乎？不但恐懼于所不聞而已，於此獨聞之地，尤必察之，防檢益周，勿使人心或危而致道心之微也。敢曰人尚未聞，而怠焉以自肆乎？夫然則隱微之幾謹，而省察之功盡矣，尚何離道之有哉？

抑體道之功，非存養則無以全本然之體，非省察則無以謹善惡之幾，二者相須而後盡也。故堯之命舜曰：「惟精惟一。」一則存養之屬，精則省察之屬也。至後程子亦曰：「涵養須用敬，進學則在致知。」亦有合於二者之旨焉。然則子思之傳，得非本之堯舜？程子之傳，寧非得之子思哉？觀中庸者，宜於所授受者
translation_en:
…more manifest than what is hidden? What all ears hear, people consider evident; yet nothing is more evident than what is minute. For in minute matters, although no outward trace has yet appeared, the incipient impulse has already sprouted at the very beginning of thought. Others indeed do not perceive it, but I perceive it myself more clearly than what all ears hear. What in the world is more evident than what is minute? Since incipient impulses are thus impossible to conceal, the gentleman does more than exercise caution over what is unseen. At the moment when he alone sees, he must examine it especially closely, redoubling his scrutiny and self-examination [?], lest human desires grow and obstruct heavenly principle. Would he dare say that others have not yet seen, and carelessly deceive himself? Nor does he merely feel apprehension over what is unheard. Where he alone hears, he must investigate especially closely, making his safeguards and restraints ever more thorough, lest the human mind become precarious and cause the mind of the Way to grow faint. Would he dare say that others have not yet heard, and slacken into self-indulgence? Thus he exercises care over hidden and minute impulses and fully accomplishes the work of scrutiny and self-examination. How could there then be any departure from the Way?

Moreover, in the work of embodying the Way, without preservation and nourishment one cannot maintain the wholeness of one’s original nature; without scrutiny and self-examination one cannot exercise care over the incipient impulses of good and evil. These two depend upon one another, and only together can they be fully accomplished. Thus Yao’s charge to Shun says: “Be discerning; be single-minded.” Single-mindedness belongs to preservation and nourishment; discernment belongs to scrutiny and self-examination. Later, Master Cheng also said: “Nourishing one’s nature requires reverent attentiveness; advancing in learning lies in extending knowledge.” This too accords with the purport of these two practices. Could the teaching transmitted by Zisi, then, fail to have its foundation in Yao and Shun? Could the teaching transmitted by Master Cheng fail to derive from Zisi? Those who read the Doctrine of the Mean should, with regard to what was handed down and received…

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
併考也
諫行言聽膏澤下於民
毛渠
同考試官訓導陳　批　〔諫言字分析明白而詞氣蔚然必善於諫言者〕
同考試官教諭鄧　批　〔膏澤本諫言中來意相承而詞不泛若此篇者不多見也〕
考試官教諭安　批　〔辭氣春容宛若孟子告宣王氣象〕
考試官教諭白　批　〔說出君臣一體之意可錄〕
===
道用于上而惠及于下君待臣然也甚矣君臣
一體也用其道而及之民焉其相待之隆何如
哉昔孟子曉齊王之意若曰國君之於臣下不
徒責其所報而貴審其所施是故止君之欲謂
之諫諫不同而皆可見之行也于焉以身而體
其心嚞犯顏之無欺而即措於施為感納約之
為忠而悉達諸事業直諫不以為忤諷諫不以
punctuated:
併考也。

諫行言聽，膏澤下於民。
毛渠
同考試官訓導陳批〔諫言字分析明白，而詞氣蔚然，必善於諫言者。〕
同考試官教諭鄧批〔膏澤本諫言中來，意相承而詞不泛，若此篇者不多見也。〕
考試官教諭安批〔辭氣春容，宛若孟子告宣王氣象。〕
考試官教諭白批〔說出君臣一體之意，可錄。〕

道用于上，而惠及于下，君待臣然也。甚矣，君臣一體也！用其道而及之民焉，其相待之隆何如哉！昔孟子曉齊王之意，若曰：國君之於臣下，不徒責其所報，而貴審其所施。是故止君之欲謂之諫，諫不同，而皆可見之行也。于焉以身而體其心，嚞犯顏之無欺而即措於施為，感納約之為忠而悉達諸事業。直諫不以為忤，諷諫不以
translation_en:
…should be examined together.

“When remonstrances are acted upon and counsel is heeded, beneficence reaches the people.”
By Mao Qu.

Associate Examiner Chen, Assistant Instructor, comments: “The terms ‘remonstrance’ and ‘counsel’ are clearly distinguished and explained, and the language has abundant vigor. The writer must be skilled in remonstrance and counsel.”

Associate Examiner Deng, Instructor, comments: “Beneficence derives from remonstrance and counsel. The ideas follow one another coherently, and the language avoids generalities. Essays like this are seldom seen.”

Examiner An, Instructor, comments: “The language is expansive and unhurried, just like the manner in which Mencius addressed King Xuan.”

Examiner Bai, Instructor, comments: “It brings out the idea that ruler and minister form one body. It merits inclusion.”

The Way is put into practice above, and its benefits reach those below: such is the ruler’s treatment of his ministers. How profoundly ruler and minister form one body! When the ruler puts his minister’s Way into practice and extends it to the people, how exalted is their regard for one another!

The purport of Mencius’s instruction to the King of Qi was as though he said: A ruler, in dealing with his ministers, should not merely demand what they give in return; he should above all examine carefully what he himself bestows upon them. Thus, restraining the ruler’s desires is called remonstrance. Remonstrances differ, but all can be put into action. The ruler then personally enters into his minister’s heart, recognizes [?] the absence of deceit in his daring to affront the royal countenance, and immediately puts his advice into practice. Moved by the loyalty of counsel that gains entry through an opening in his understanding, he gives it full expression in his undertakings. He does not regard direct remonstrance as defiance, nor does he regard indirect remonstrance as…

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
爲疑也諫豈有不行者哉引君之善謂之言言
不同而皆可施之用也于焉以意而逆其志入
告于內者有嘉納而無難色日陳于前者有翕
受而無拒意法言之所必從巽言之所必說也
言豈有不聽者哉夫諫不行固有也其膏而不
能下及者今諫則行矣由是稱民之政自息於
箴規之餘德澤流行沛然霖雨之及時也言不
聽固有壅其澤而莫之下究者今言則聽矣由
是利民之政自舉於啓沃之後恩惠廣大油然
===
膏雨之潤物也夫道用於上而志始同惠及於
下而道斯顯則臣之望君者畢而君之體臣者
至矣抑論君臣之間禮雖嚴於勢分之尊而道
必通於天地之泰故堯舜之賡歌每得於交儆
而周人之燕樂實通乎上下伊尹陳戒一德而
天下有雲霓之望周公進戒無逸而罔不配天
其澤此古之君臣所以都俞吁咈於一堂之上
而共成正大光明之業也後世君恃其勢臣病
其難道始扞格於上而斯民不被其澤矣可勝
punctuated:
爲疑也，諫豈有不行者哉？引君之善謂之言，言不同而皆可施之用也。于焉以意而逆其志，入告于內者有嘉納而無難色，日陳于前者有翕受而無拒意，法言之所必從，巽言之所必說也。言豈有不聽者哉？夫諫不行，固有也其膏而不能下及者；今諫則行矣，由是稱民之政自息於箴規之餘，德澤流行，沛然霖雨之及時也。言不聽，固有壅其澤而莫之下究者；今言則聽矣，由是利民之政自舉於啓沃之後，恩惠廣大，油然膏雨之潤物也。夫道用於上而志始同，惠及於下而道斯顯，則臣之望君者畢，而君之體臣者至矣。
抑論君臣之間，禮雖嚴於勢分之尊，而道必通於天地之泰。故堯舜之賡歌每得於交儆，而周人之燕樂實通乎上下。伊尹陳戒一德，而天下有雲霓之望；周公進戒無逸，而罔不配天其澤。此古之君臣所以都俞吁咈於一堂之上，而共成正大光明之業也。後世君恃其勢，臣病其難，道始扞格於上，而斯民不被其澤矣。可勝
translation_en:
…regarded with suspicion. How could any remonstrance fail to be acted upon? Drawing forth the ruler’s goodness is called offering counsel. Counsel takes different forms, but all may be put into practice. The ruler therefore uses his own understanding to discern his ministers’ intentions. Those who enter to advise him in private find gracious acceptance, with no sign of displeasure; those who present their views before him daily find ready reception, with no intention of rejection. Upright words he invariably follows; gently accommodating words he invariably welcomes. How could any counsel go unheard? When remonstrance is not acted upon, there are indeed cases in which its nourishing benefits cannot reach those below [?]. Now, however, remonstrance is acted upon. Thus policies suited to the people develop naturally [?] in the wake of admonition and correction. The blessings of virtue spread abroad, abundant as timely rain. When counsel goes unheard, there are indeed cases in which its benefits are obstructed and cannot reach those below. Now, however, counsel is heard. Thus policies benefiting the people are naturally undertaken after ministers have enlightened and nourished the ruler’s understanding. His kindness and beneficence spread far and wide, like nourishing rain moistening all things. When the Way is put into practice above, ruler and ministers begin to share a common purpose; when benefits reach those below, the Way becomes manifest. Then all that ministers hope for from their ruler is fulfilled, and the ruler’s sympathetic understanding of his ministers reaches its utmost extent.
Now, in considering the relationship between ruler and ministers, although ritual strictly maintains the dignity of their respective ranks and positions, the Way must circulate between them, as in the harmonious intercourse of Heaven and Earth represented by the hexagram Tai. Thus the responsive singing of Yao and Shun arose from mutual admonition, while the banquet music of the Zhou people truly joined those above with those below. Yi Yin presented his admonitions on unified virtue, and all under Heaven looked forward to relief as to clouds and a rainbow in time of drought. The Duke of Zhou offered his admonitions against ease, and the resulting beneficence everywhere matched that of Heaven. This is how the rulers and ministers of antiquity could voice assent and dissent together in a single hall and jointly accomplish undertakings that were upright, great, radiant, and clear. In later ages, rulers relied on their power, while ministers suffered from the difficulty of their position. The Way then became obstructed above, and the people ceased to receive its blessings. Could one ever fully…

text:
歎哉噫孟子以是為齊王告其亦有所警也夫
易
大有元亨
曹卿

保有言之尤見忠愛之意
考試官教諭安　批　〔詞理豐潔大有之意當〕
如此作
===
考試官教諭白　批　〔講世道治道之隆精采〕
雅重予殆能鳴
國家之盛者歟宜冠本房以為得人慶也
前聖以世道之盛名夫卦後聖以治道之盛善
其占盖世道與治道而相因也前聖以世道名
卦後聖以治道繫辭而各言其盛厥旨淵哉昔
伏羲交離於乾名卦大有誠以此卦乾為天也
離為火也離上乾下則是輝光煥於九重而海

punctuated:
歎哉！噫！孟子以是為齊王告，其亦有所警也夫！

易
大有，元亨。
曹卿

translation_en:
…How lamentable! Ah! When Mengzi addressed these words to the King of Qi, surely he also intended a warning!

Book of Changes
“Great Possession: supreme success.”
Cao Qing

Comment by Associate Examiner Qin, Instructor: 〔When the sages named hexagrams and appended statements, their words always drew upon what the hexagrams contained. This essay grasps the meaning clearly and precisely and develops it with refinement and vigor. At the end, it returns to〕 the preservation of possession, especially revealing a spirit of loyalty and devotion.

Comment by Examiner An, Instructor: 〔The language and reasoning are rich and clear. The meaning of Great Possession ought to〕 be treated in this way.

Comment by Examiner Bai, Instructor: 〔In discussing the flourishing of the world’s condition and the way of governance, its brilliance〕 is elegant and dignified. Am I perhaps one who can give voice to the state’s flourishing [?]? This essay should rank first in this examining section, as a cause for celebrating the discovery of talent.

The earlier sage named the hexagram for the flourishing condition of the world; the later sage pronounced its divination auspicious for the flourishing of the way of governance. For the condition of the world and the way of governance depend upon one another. The earlier sage named the hexagram according to the world’s condition; the later sage appended its statement according to the way of governance. Each spoke of its flourishing: how profound their meaning!

Long ago, Fuxi combined Li with Qian and named the hexagram Great Possession. Indeed, in this hexagram Qian represents heaven, and Li represents fire. With Li above and Qian below, radiance shines forth from the ninefold heights of the imperial court, illuminating all within the seas, reaching even the most distant places. Civilizing brilliance shines in mid-heaven, and the earth…

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
圓爲之覆冐無地不有也是固有大有之義矣
又以卦體六五居尊得中而五陽應之則是惟
皇作極而承德祗若者合臣庶而皆同大觀在
上而用賓利見者隨遠近而無閒亦有大有之
義焉伏羲之所以名卦者以此文王繫其辭以
爲乾健離明居尊應天有亨道也占者有是德
焉吾知剛明果斷而所以治有者有其本承天
時行而所以治有者有其道紀綱立而法度舉
凡所以左右斯民者周旋而無虧禮樂興而政
===
教明凡所以經綸天下者咸正而罔缺神化之
機馨所有而推行之无外不疾而速沛然何天
之衢矣亨何大邪利用之妙盡所有而旁達之
无疆不行而至豁然良馬之逐矣何元亨邪吁
當大有之世盡治有之善如此則人謀以臧天
命攸歸矣尚何有之不可保哉大抵造化有循
環之機人事有盛衰之理古之人君所以能久
安長治者亦惟安不忘危治不忘亂耳使當盛
滿之時不知所以儆畏則驕逸怠荒之心生而
punctuated: 圓爲之覆冐，無地不有也，是固有大有之義矣。又以卦體六五居尊得中，而五陽應之，則是惟皇作極，而承德祗若者合臣庶而皆同；大觀在上，而用賓利見者隨遠近而無閒，亦有大有之義焉。伏羲之所以名卦者以此。文王繫其辭，以爲乾健離明，居尊應天，有亨道也。占者有是德焉，吾知剛明果斷，而所以治有者有其本；承天時行，而所以治有者有其道。紀綱立而法度舉，凡所以左右斯民者周旋而無虧；禮樂興而政教明，凡所以經綸天下者咸正而罔缺。神化之機，馨所有而推行之无外，不疾而速，沛然何天之衢矣，亨何大邪！利用之妙，盡所有而旁達之无疆，不行而至，豁然良馬之逐矣，何元亨邪！吁！當大有之世，盡治有之善如此，則人謀以臧，天命攸歸矣，尚何有之不可保哉？大抵造化有循環之機，人事有盛衰之理。古之人君所以能久安長治者，亦惟安不忘危、治不忘亂耳。使當盛滿之時，不知所以儆畏，則驕逸怠荒之心生而
translation_en: …the round earth is covered by it, with no place beyond its possession. This certainly embodies the meaning of Great Possession (Dayou). Moreover, in the hexagram’s structure, the six in the fifth place occupies the honored position and attains centrality, while the five yang lines respond to it. Thus, the sovereign establishes the supreme standard, and officials and commoners alike receive his virtue and reverently follow him. A grand example is displayed above, and those who come as guests and benefit from seeing the ruler do so without distinction between far and near. This, too, embodies the meaning of Great Possession. It was for these reasons that Fuxi named the hexagram. King Wen appended its statement, considering that Qian’s strength and Li’s brightness, occupying the honored position and responding to Heaven, provided a way to success. If the person consulting the oracle possesses these virtues, I know that his firmness, discernment, and decisiveness will provide the foundation for governing what he possesses; his compliance with Heaven and timely action will provide the proper way to govern it. Guiding principles are established and laws and standards implemented: all means of assisting the people operate comprehensively, without deficiency. Rites and music flourish, and governance and moral instruction become clear: all means of ordering the realm are correct and complete. The workings of numinous transformation encompass all that exists [?] and extend their operation everywhere, moving swiftly without haste—flowing freely along Heaven’s highway [?]. How great the success! The subtle efficacy of making things useful exhausts all available resources and reaches everywhere without limit, arriving without traveling—as freely as fine horses in pursuit. What supreme success! Ah! In an age of Great Possession, if one thus fulfills every excellence in governing what one possesses, human counsels will be good, and Heaven’s mandate will come to rest upon one. What possession could then fail to be preserved? Generally speaking, creation operates in cycles, and human affairs follow a pattern of flourishing and decline. The rulers of antiquity could maintain lasting peace and enduring order simply because, in security, they did not forget danger and, amid order, they did not forget disorder. If, at a time of prosperity and abundance, one does not understand the need for vigilance and reverence, then arrogance, indulgence, indolence, and neglect arise in the heart, and…

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
不能保其有也故周公於泰則曰城復于隍孔
子於既濟亦以思患豫防言之其垂戒之意至
矣噫當大有之任者尚鑒于斯
以言乎遠則不禦以言乎邇則靜而正
范瑟
同考試官教諭秦　批〔此節遠近字橫說天地間直說正是易理廣大處作者類多體貼不明冗〕
〔雜可厭惟此認理真而措詞整蓋邃於易者〕
考試官教諭安　批〔不禦靜正處明暢醇粹自異衆作録之〕
===
考試官教諭白　批〔說理文字最難此言廣大處有思致有發明有斟酌超群軼駕于固東省之英儁乎〕
語遠而理無盡語近而理自存此易之廣大也
盖易者理之會也遠者无盡而近者自存其廣
大也何如哉宜大傳指言以示人也且陰陽無
處而不有故易理無往而不在是以自其遠者
言之法象隱於幽玄邃邈而難知氣類散於□
punctuated:
不能保其有也。故周公於泰則曰：「城復于隍。」孔子於既濟亦以思患豫防言之，其垂戒之意至矣。噫！當大有之任者，尚鑒于斯！

「以言乎遠則不禦，以言乎邇則靜而正。」
范瑟

同考試官教諭秦　批〔此節遠近字，橫說天地間，直說正是易理廣大處。作者類多體貼不明，冗〕〔雜可厭。惟此認理真而措詞整，蓋邃於易者。〕
考試官教諭安　批〔不禦、靜正處，明暢醇粹，自異衆作，録之。〕
考試官教諭白　批〔說理文字最難。此言廣大處，有思致，有發明，有斟酌，超群軼駕，于固東省之英儁乎！〕

語遠而理無盡，語近而理自存，此易之廣大也。盖易者，理之會也。遠者无盡，而近者自存，其廣大也何如哉！宜大傳指言以示人也。且陰陽無處而不有，故易理無往而不在。是以自其遠者言之，法象隱於幽玄，邃邈而難知；氣類散於□
translation_en:
…and cannot preserve what he possesses. Thus, concerning the hexagram Peace (Tai), the Duke of Zhou said, “The city wall falls back into the moat.” Concerning Already Across (Jiji), Confucius likewise spoke of anticipating calamities and taking precautions beforehand. The admonition they bequeathed was most earnest. Ah! May those charged with the responsibilities of Great Possession (Dayou) take warning from this!

“If speaking of what is distant, it admits no bounds; if speaking of what is near, it is still and correct.”
Fan Se

Associate Examiner Qin, Instructor, comments: 〔In this passage, the words “distant” and “near,” treated horizontally, refer to the space between Heaven and Earth; treated directly, they refer precisely to the vastness of the principles of the Changes. Most writers fail to apprehend this clearly, producing tedious〕〔and tiresome miscellanies. This author alone grasps the principles truly and expresses them in orderly language. He is evidently deeply versed in the Changes.〕
Examiner An, Instructor, comments: 〔The treatment of “admits no bounds” and “still and correct” is clear, fluent, and pure. It stands apart from the other compositions. Include it in the record.〕
Examiner Bai, Instructor, comments: 〔Writing that expounds principles is the most difficult. In discussing vastness, this composition displays thoughtful insight, elucidation, and careful judgment. It surpasses the multitude and outstrips its rivals. Surely you are an outstanding talent of the eastern province [?]!〕

Speak of what is distant, and principle is inexhaustible; speak of what is near, and principle is present of itself. Such is the vastness of the Changes. For the Changes is the convergence of principles. In what is distant they are inexhaustible; in what is near they are present of themselves. How vast it is! It is fitting that the Great Commentary points this out to instruct people. Moreover, there is nowhere that yin and yang do not exist; thus there is nowhere that the principles of the Changes are absent. Hence, speaking of what is distant, patterns and images lie concealed in profound obscurity, remote and difficult to comprehend; categories of vital energy are dispersed in □ [illegible]…

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
位懸絶而莫測是遠者宜若可盡也然陰陽妙
闔闢之機混淪磅礴極所有而无外剛柔神變
化之用布濩流行隨所到而有餘絶域窮荒地
雖異矣而成象成形莫非此理之根柢孰得而
究其極耶遐陬僻壤方雖殊矣而為陰為陽一
皆此理之綱維孰得而窮其際耶是蓋無有而
無乎不有矣曾以遠而有盡乎自其近者言之
物類雜陳昭然于指顧之下事情隱伏居然于
步履之間是近者宜若可遺也然太極本然之
===
妙即物默寓索之而愈精天命自然之理隨事
潛融驗之而益至不出戶庭有是物則有是則
成性攸存无少偏倚也近取諸身有是器則寓
是道實理具備不相假借也是蓋無為而無所
不為矣曾以近而有窮乎是則遠易盡也而無
所盡近易遺也而不能遺非易之廣大其孰能
與於此抑論易之廣大信乎不可加矣而其所
以廣大則本於乾坤動靜以生焉皆實理也故
可推之實用不然遠必流於荒而近必淪於卑
punctuated: 位懸絶而莫測，是遠者宜若可盡也。然陰陽妙闔闢之機，混淪磅礴，極所有而无外；剛柔神變化之用，布濩流行，隨所到而有餘。絶域窮荒，地雖異矣，而成象成形，莫非此理之根柢，孰得而究其極耶？遐陬僻壤，方雖殊矣，而為陰為陽，一皆此理之綱維，孰得而窮其際耶？是蓋無有而無乎不有矣，曾以遠而有盡乎？自其近者言之，物類雜陳，昭然于指顧之下；事情隱伏，居然于步履之間。是近者宜若可遺也。然太極本然之妙，即物默寓，索之而愈精；天命自然之理，隨事潛融，驗之而益至。不出戶庭，有是物則有是則，成性攸存，无少偏倚也；近取諸身，有是器則寓是道，實理具備，不相假借也。是蓋無為而無所不為矣，曾以近而有窮乎？是則遠易盡也而無所盡，近易遺也而不能遺，非易之廣大，其孰能與於此？抑論易之廣大，信乎不可加矣，而其所以廣大，則本於乾坤動靜以生焉，皆實理也，故可推之實用。不然，遠必流於荒，而近必淪於卑
translation_en:
…positions, so far removed as to be unfathomable. Thus, what is distant might seem capable of being exhausted. Yet yin and yang work wondrously through the mechanism of closing and opening: undivided and all-pervading, they encompass everything that exists and leave nothing outside. The firm and the yielding work numinously through transformation: spreading and flowing, their efficacy remains inexhaustible wherever they reach. In remote regions and the farthest wilderness, the lands may differ, yet all that takes on an image or a form has this principle as its foundation. Who could fathom its ultimate extent? In distant corners and secluded places, the regions may differ, yet all that constitutes yin or yang is governed by this principle. Who could exhaust its bounds? Thus, it has no determinate existence, yet there is nowhere it does not exist. Could distance ever bring it to an end?

Speaking of what is near, the various kinds of things are arrayed together, clearly visible wherever one points or looks; the circumstances of affairs lie concealed within the very space of one's footsteps. Thus, what is near might seem possible to leave out. Yet the inherent subtlety of the Supreme Ultimate silently resides in things themselves: the more one seeks it, the more refined it becomes. The spontaneous principle of Heaven's mandate is latently infused into every affair: the more one examines it, the more fully it is realized. Without going beyond one's gate and courtyard, wherever there is a thing, there is its norm. Here the fully constituted nature abides, without the slightest deviation or imbalance. Taking what is near at hand in one's own person, wherever there is a concrete vessel, the Way resides within it. Substantial principle is fully present, with no need to borrow from elsewhere. Thus, it acts without contrivance, yet there is nothing it does not accomplish. Could proximity ever impose a limit upon it?

Thus, what is distant is easily exhausted, yet here there is nothing that can be exhausted; what is near is easily overlooked, yet here it cannot be left out. What but the vastness of the Changes could attain this? Indeed, in discussing the vastness of the Changes, truly nothing could be added to it. Yet that whereby it is vast arises fundamentally from the movement and stillness of Qian and Kun. All of this is substantial principle, and therefore it can be extended to practical application. Otherwise, what is distant must stray into the outlandish, and what is near must sink into the lowly…

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
矣何以神道化為萬世斯民利邪噫聖人以此
為訓後之人至以太玄準易卜筮小易者亦獨
何哉
書
予欲左右有民汝翼予欲宣力四方汝為
楊縉
同考試官訓導劉　批〔左右宣力處此作體認真切且模寫股肱之意殆盡君臣一體氣象讀之可以想見子其有志作股肱者乎取冠本房〕
===
同考試官訓導黃　批〔此題以政教股肱立說非但以其文也場中士子類能言之求其措詞老健簡明者無踰此篇允宜錄之〕
考試官教諭安　批〔說翼為處得旨〕
考試官教諭白　批〔詞理通暢作典謨義正如此〕
聖君資大臣有欲施教於天下有欲施政於天
下甚矣君之有賴於臣也聖君欲施政教於天
punctuated:
矣，何以神道化為萬世斯民利邪？噫！聖人以此為訓，後之人至以《太玄》準《易》，卜筮小《易》者，亦獨何哉？

書

予欲左右有民，汝翼；予欲宣力四方，汝為。

楊縉

同考試官訓導劉　批〔左右宣力處，此作體認真切，且模寫股肱之意殆盡。君臣一體氣象，讀之可以想見。子其有志作股肱者乎？取冠本房。〕

同考試官訓導黃　批〔此題以政教股肱立說，非但以其文也。場中士子類能言之，求其措詞老健簡明者，無踰此篇，允宜錄之。〕

考試官教諭安　批〔說翼為處得旨。〕

考試官教諭白　批〔詞理通暢，作典謨義正如此。〕

聖君資大臣，有欲施教於天下，有欲施政於天下。甚矣，君之有賴於臣也！聖君欲施政教於天
translation_en:
…how, then, could transformation through the numinous Way benefit these people for ten thousand generations? Alas! The sage left this as his teaching; why, then, have later people gone so far as to set the Supreme Mystery (Taixuan) alongside the Book of Changes and belittle the Changes as mere divination?

Book of Documents

“I wish to assist the people: you shall aid me. I wish to extend my efforts throughout the four quarters: you shall carry this out.”

Yang Jin

Associate Examiner Liu, Assistant Instructor, comments: “In its treatment of ‘assist’ and ‘extend my efforts,’ this essay shows a penetrating and accurate understanding. It also conveys almost fully the meaning of ministers serving as the ruler’s limbs. Reading it, one can envision ruler and ministers forming a single body. Do you perhaps aspire to serve as such a minister? Selected as the best in this examining room.”

Associate Examiner Huang, Assistant Instructor, comments: “This essay develops its argument through government, moral instruction, and ministers serving as the ruler’s limbs; its merit is not merely literary. Most candidates in the examination hall can discuss these matters, but for mature, vigorous, concise, and clear expression, none surpasses this essay. It certainly deserves inclusion.”

Examiner An, Instructor, comments: “The explanation of ‘aid’ and ‘carry this out’ captures the essential meaning.”

Examiner Bai, Instructor, comments: “The language and reasoning flow clearly. This is precisely how an exposition on the Canons and Counsels should be written.”

The sage ruler relies on his great ministers, wishing both to extend moral instruction throughout the realm and to administer government throughout the realm. How greatly the ruler depends on his ministers! When the sage ruler wishes to extend government and moral instruction throughout the realm…

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
下能不資大臣以盡其職哉帝舜告禹以臣隣
之義及此謂夫君能以一人而總萬機之柄不
能以一身而理天下之事所謂臣作股肱者豈
無謂邪誠以五教未敷予之憂也茲欲輔以立
之翼以行之使百姓之不親者咸囿之於民彝
物則之中五品之不遜者舉範之於綱常倫理
之內民生雖衆而教無不行焉是豈予之所自
能哉惟汝禹也居百揆之官總教化之任其必
敬以敷其訓寬以俟其化作新斯民勞來匡直
===
之有法也化導有衆振舉軌範之有方也俛布
四體而爲予之翼可焉汝能翼之則予左右之
心遂矣庶績未凝治之累也茲欲綱以立之紀
以陳之使政足以道其行黎民免阻饑之患刑
足以防其奸蠻夷無猾夏之虞四方雖遠而政
無不行焉是豈予之所自致哉惟汝禹也當百
揆之位董治理之責其必致勉以脩其職克勤
以施於邦撫安斯世導之而生養遂也均平天
下治之而爭奪息也竭乃心力而爲予之助可
punctuated: 下，能不資大臣以盡其職哉？帝舜告禹以臣隣之義，及此謂：「夫君能以一人而總萬機之柄，不能以一身而理天下之事。所謂臣作股肱者，豈無謂邪？誠以五教未敷，予之憂也。茲欲輔以立之，翼以行之，使百姓之不親者咸囿之於民彝物則之中，五品之不遜者舉範之於綱常倫理之內。民生雖衆，而教無不行焉，是豈予之所自能哉？惟汝禹也，居百揆之官，總教化之任，其必敬以敷其訓，寬以俟其化。作新斯民，勞來匡直之有法也；化導有衆，振舉軌範之有方也。俛布四體而爲予之翼，可焉。汝能翼之，則予左右之心遂矣。庶績未凝，治之累也。茲欲綱以立之，紀以陳之，使政足以道其行，黎民免阻饑之患；刑足以防其奸，蠻夷無猾夏之虞。四方雖遠，而政無不行焉，是豈予之所自致哉？惟汝禹也，當百揆之位，董治理之責，其必致勉以脩其職，克勤以施於邦。撫安斯世，導之而生養遂也；均平天下，治之而爭奪息也。竭乃心力而爲予之助，可
translation_en: …under Heaven, could he fail to rely on his great ministers to discharge their duties fully? Emperor Shun instructed Yu in the meaning of a minister’s close relationship to his ruler, and at this point said: “A ruler can, as a single person, hold overall authority over the myriad affairs of government, but cannot personally administer everything under Heaven. Surely the saying that ministers serve as his arms and legs is not without meaning! Indeed, that the five teachings have not yet spread is my concern. I now wish to support their establishment and assist their implementation, so that all among the people who lack affection for one another may be brought within the enduring norms of human relationships and the principles governing things, and all who fail to observe the five relationships may be brought into conformity with the cardinal bonds and constant virtues of moral life. Though the people are numerous, these teachings would reach them all. Could I possibly accomplish this by myself? You, Yu, occupy the office of Chief Minister and bear overall responsibility for moral instruction. You must reverently disseminate its lessons and patiently await their transforming effect. In renewing this people, have methods for encouraging, attracting, correcting, and rectifying them; in transforming and guiding the multitude, have means of reviving and upholding proper standards. You may exert your four limbs in humble service and act as my support. If you can give this support, my wish to guide and assist the people will be fulfilled. That the many undertakings of government have not yet been firmly accomplished is an impediment to good order. I now wish to establish their main framework and set out their organizing details, so that governance may adequately guide people’s conduct and the common people escape the affliction of hardship and hunger; so that punishments may adequately prevent wrongdoing and there be no fear of the Man and Yi peoples disturbing the Xia realm. Though the four quarters are distant, governance would reach them all. Could I possibly bring this about by myself? You, Yu, hold the position of Chief Minister and bear responsibility for overseeing orderly government. You must exert yourself to discharge your duties and work diligently in administering the realm. In bringing peace and security to this age, guide the people so that their livelihood and sustenance are assured; in bringing equity and peace to all under Heaven, govern them so that contention and strife cease. Exert your utmost mental and physical strength to assist me; you may …

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
爲汝能爲之則予宣力之心遂矣是則政教之
立在君而政教之施在臣君臣之相資一體之
相須也臣非君之股肱而何哉抑論有虞之世
四方風動萬國咸寧民已化治已成矣帝舜猶
以是資之禹者何哉蓋古之君臣不以世治民
安爲自足故當泰之時猶審復隍之戒居豐之
世尚懷日昃之憂此治之所以不可及也後世
治僅小康者遂驕盈以自足爲之臣者又每爲
豐亨豫大之說以諂之意其亦不思之甚矣
===
自古商人亦越我周文王立政立事牧夫
準人則克宅之克由繹之茲乃俾乂
趙文燿
同考試官訓導劉　批　立政一題傳註甚明作
者多不體貼俾乂處乃以治效爲言大戾經旨
此作本傳註以成文禹湯文王任賢之道宛然
在目非經明者不能也吾得于可以薦矣
同考試官訓導黃　批　此題士子多掇拾舊語
敷演成篇至於克宅由繹俾乂正意鮮有能說
punctuated:
爲。汝能爲之，則予宣力之心遂矣。是則政教之立在君，而政教之施在臣，君臣之相資，一體之相須也。臣非君之股肱而何哉？抑論有虞之世，四方風動，萬國咸寧，民已化，治已成矣。帝舜猶以是資之禹者，何哉？蓋古之君臣不以世治民安爲自足，故當泰之時，猶審復隍之戒；居豐之世，尚懷日昃之憂。此治之所以不可及也。後世治僅小康者，遂驕盈以自足；爲之臣者，又每爲豐亨豫大之說以諂之，意其亦不思之甚矣。

自古商人，亦越我周文王，立政、立事、牧夫、準人，則克宅之，克由繹之，茲乃俾乂。
趙文燿

同考試官訓導劉批：立政一題，傳註甚明，作者多不體貼俾乂處，乃以治效爲言，大戾經旨。此作本傳註以成文，禹、湯、文王任賢之道，宛然在目，非經明者不能也。吾得于，可以薦矣。

同考試官訓導黃批：此題士子多掇拾舊語，敷演成篇。至於克宅、由繹、俾乂正意，鮮有能說
translation_en:
…act. If you can accomplish this, my wish that you exert yourself on my behalf will be fulfilled. Thus, establishing government and instruction rests with the ruler, while putting them into effect rests with his ministers. Ruler and ministers support one another as mutually dependent parts of a single body. What, then, are ministers if not the ruler’s arms and legs?
Yet consider the age of Youyu: all quarters responded as grass bends before the wind, and the myriad states were at peace. The people had already been transformed, and good government had already been achieved. Why, then, did Emperor Shun still rely upon Yu in these matters? The rulers and ministers of antiquity did not regard an orderly realm and a peaceful populace as grounds for complacency. Thus, in times of peace, they still weighed the warning that the city wall might collapse back into the moat; amid abundance, they still harbored anxiety that the sun would pass its zenith. This is why their government remains unsurpassed. In later ages, rulers whose government achieved only modest peace became arrogant, complacent, and satisfied with themselves. Their ministers, moreover, repeatedly flattered them with talk of abundance, prosperity, ease, and greatness. Surely this shows an utter failure to reflect!

“From the Shang rulers of antiquity down to King Wen of our Zhou, in establishing government and appointing officials, regional governors, and judicial officers, they were able to place these men in office and employ and continually examine them; only then did they entrust them with governing.”
Zhao Wenyao

Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Assistant Instructor:
The commentaries explain this topic from ‘Establishing Government’ very clearly. Most writers fail to attend closely to the words ‘entrust them with governing,’ instead discussing the results of government, in serious contradiction to the classic’s meaning. This essay is composed on the basis of the commentaries. The ways in which Yu, Tang, and King Wen employed worthy men appear vividly before our eyes. Only someone who understands the classic clearly could accomplish this. I have found him [?] and can recommend him.

Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, Assistant Instructor:
On this topic, most candidates collect familiar phrases and expand them into an essay. As for the true meaning of ‘were able to place them in office,’ ‘employ and continually examine them,’ and ‘entrust them with governing,’ few can articulate…

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
出者此篇獨能脫去陳腐發輝詳盡真程式之
文也錄之
考試官教諭安　批〔能說出三王任賢爲治之意〕
考試官教諭白　批〔旨明詞暢佳士也〕
大臣申言三王於三宅能盡任用之道而使之
以爲治焉蓋賢才爲治之本也非三王任用之
能盡其道焉何以能使之爲治哉周公戒成王
以任用賢才之道及此謂夫立政莫急於用賢
===
用賢莫先於三宅自古知恤之君有曰夏后氏
之禹殷先哲王之湯及我周文王者焉其於立
政之官有曰立事之常任牧民之常伯及守法
之準人者焉是三王也用是三宅也豈無其道
哉方其始用也克知之真灼見之切度德定位
所任者皆三德六德之賢量才授職所立者皆
克宅克俊之彥名與實相須也德與位相稱也
能宅才以安其職如此及其既用也詳其所行
考其所就推心以委任之使得以勉脩其職業
punctuated:
出者。此篇獨能脫去陳腐，發輝詳盡，真程式之文也，錄之。
考試官教諭安，批〔能說出三王任賢爲治之意〕。
考試官教諭白，批〔旨明詞暢佳士也〕。
大臣申言三王於三宅能盡任用之道，而使之以爲治焉。蓋賢才爲治之本也，非三王任用之能盡其道焉，何以能使之爲治哉？周公戒成王以任用賢才之道，及此謂夫立政莫急於用賢，用賢莫先於三宅。自古知恤之君，有曰夏后氏之禹、殷先哲王之湯及我周文王者焉。其於立政之官，有曰立事之常任、牧民之常伯及守法之準人者焉。是三王也，用是三宅也，豈無其道哉？方其始用也，克知之真，灼見之切，度德定位，所任者皆三德六德之賢；量才授職，所立者皆克宅克俊之彥。名與實相須也，德與位相稱也，能宅才以安其職如此。及其既用也，詳其所行，考其所就，推心以委任之，使得以勉脩其職業，
translation_en:
…express it. This essay alone succeeds in casting off stale formulations and expounding the meaning fully and thoroughly. It is truly an exemplary composition. Let it be recorded.
Examiner An, Instructor, comments: 〔It succeeds in explaining how the Three Kings employed worthy men to achieve good government.〕
Examiner Bai, Instructor, comments: 〔The meaning is clear and the language fluent. A fine scholar indeed.〕
The great minister further explains that, with respect to the three principal offices, the Three Kings fully realized the proper way of employing men and thereby enabled them to govern. Worthy and talented men are the foundation of government. Had the Three Kings not fully realized the proper way of employing them, how could they have enabled them to govern? In admonishing King Cheng about the proper way to employ worthy and talented men, the Duke of Zhou reaches this point: in establishing government, nothing is more urgent than employing the worthy; in employing the worthy, nothing takes precedence over the three principal offices. Among rulers of antiquity who understood the need for solicitude were Yu of the Xia ruling house, Tang, the former sage king of Yin, and King Wen of our Zhou. Among the officers responsible for establishing government were the regular administrators who managed affairs, the regular chiefs who shepherded the people, and the officers of standards who upheld the laws. Could these Three Kings have employed men in these three principal offices without a proper method?
When first employing them, they knew them truly and perceived their qualities clearly. They assessed virtue and assigned rank: those they appointed were all worthy men possessing the three virtues or the six virtues. They measured ability and conferred office: those they installed were all outstanding men capable of holding office and distinguished in talent. Name and substance supported one another; virtue and position corresponded. Such was their ability to place talented men so that they were secure in their offices. Once they had employed them, they examined their conduct closely and assessed their accomplishments. They entrusted them with responsibilities in wholehearted confidence, enabling them diligently to cultivate the work of their offices…

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
嚴思而丕法之使得以大展其才猷不閒之以
人也不誤之以己也能繹才以盡其用如此夫
知之既明足以遂三宅欲為之心待之既誠足
以堅三宅樂為之志以之理天事而牧天民也
事無不治而民無不安矣寧不精白一心以敬
應其上乎以之和庶獄而明庶慎也法無不立
而政無不舉矣能不各率其屬以興起治功乎
謂之曰俾乂信乎能使之以為治也是則用賢
得其道而得賢以為用三王之成法可鑒也嗣
===
王可不知所法哉大抵論治以唐虞為至取法
以堯舜為上周公告戒成王用賢為治歷舉禹
湯文武而未及堯舜者何哉蓋遠宗之雖不如
近述之易而況文王又耳目之所及成憲之所
在乎能法三王以用賢堯舜之道亦不外此唐
虞之治可馴致矣此又周公言外之意也後之
有志唐虞三代之治者必知用賢之道而後可
詩
我有嘉賓德音孔昭視民不恌君子是則
punctuated:
嚴思而丕法之，使得以大展其才猷，不閒之以人也，不誤之以己也。能繹才以盡其用如此。夫知之既明，足以遂三宅欲為之心；待之既誠，足以堅三宅樂為之志。以之理天事而牧天民也，事無不治，而民無不安矣，寧不精白一心以敬應其上乎？以之和庶獄而明庶慎也，法無不立，而政無不舉矣，能不各率其屬以興起治功乎？謂之曰「俾乂」，信乎能使之以為治也。是則用賢得其道，而得賢以為用，三王之成法可鑒也。嗣王可不知所法哉？大抵論治以唐虞為至，取法以堯舜為上。周公告戒成王，用賢為治，歷舉禹、湯、文、武而未及堯舜者，何哉？蓋遠宗之雖不如近述之易，而況文王又耳目之所及、成憲之所在乎？能法三王以用賢，堯舜之道亦不外此，唐虞之治可馴致矣。此又周公言外之意也。後之有志唐虞三代之治者，必知用賢之道而後可。

詩

我有嘉賓，德音孔昭。視民不恌，君子是則
translation_en:
…regard them with grave consideration and greatly emulate them [?], enabling them to give full scope to their talents and plans. He neither lets others come between them and himself nor lets his own errors lead them astray. Such is his ability to develop talent and put it fully to use. His understanding of them is clear enough to fulfill the desire to serve of those occupying the three offices; his treatment of them is sincere enough to strengthen their resolve to serve gladly. When he employs them to administer Heaven’s affairs and shepherd Heaven’s people, no affair goes unregulated and no person lacks peace. How could they fail to purify their hearts and respond reverently to their sovereign with undivided purpose? When he employs them to bring fairness to all judicial cases and clarity to all matters requiring care, no law goes unestablished and no measure of government goes unimplemented. How could they fail, each leading his subordinates, to advance the work of good government? The phrase “enable them to govern” indeed means that he can employ them to achieve good government. Thus, by following the proper way of employing worthy men, he obtains worthy men to serve him. The established methods of the Three Kings offer a clear example. Can a succeeding king fail to know what he should emulate?

Generally, discussions of government regard the ages of Tang and Yu as the highest achievement, and the choice of models places Yao and Shun foremost. Why, then, when the Duke of Zhou admonished King Cheng to employ worthy men in governing, did he enumerate Yu, Tang, King Wen, and King Wu without mentioning Yao and Shun? Taking distant precedents as one’s guide is less easy than following recent ones. Moreover, King Wen was still within the reach of living memory, and his established institutions remained available. If one can emulate the Three Kings in employing worthy men, the Way of Yao and Shun lies within this very practice, and the good government of Tang and Yu can gradually be attained. This, too, is an implication beyond the Duke of Zhou’s explicit words. Those in later ages who aspire to the good government of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties must first understand the way to employ worthy men.

Book of Odes

I have excellent guests, whose virtuous renown shines brightly. They show the people how to shun frivolity; gentlemen take them as their pattern…

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
是傚
同考試官訓導陳　批　〔篇中求教之意首尾圓洽可謂善說詩者取之〕
毛渠
同考試官教諭鄧　批　〔王者求教凡以為民爾嘉賓之德足以視民而為治民君子所當法教在其中矣此作得之〕
考試官教諭安　批　〔文字轉合處深得傳意當是作手〕
考試官教諭白　批　〔講則𣉻處得旨〕
===
詩人美嘉賓之德足以化民而君子所當法也
夫有天下者以德化為先也嘉賓之德旣足以
化民非君子所當取法者哉此燕饗賓客之詩
也意以我所望於嘉賓者欲示之以有言而乃
得之於無言維我嘉賓大道藴諸心遠近皆稱
其令德赫赫乎仁有聲義有問也實德備於己
