上下皆稱其令名昭昭乎彼無惡此無斁也譽
望所加而導民之路在其中足以示之而使大
punctuated:
是傚。
同考試官訓導陳　批　〔篇中求教之意，首尾圓洽，可謂善說詩者，取之。〕
毛渠
同考試官教諭鄧　批　〔王者求教，凡以為民爾。嘉賓之德足以視民，而為治民君子所當法，教在其中矣。此作得之。〕
考試官教諭安　批　〔文字轉合處，深得傳意，當是作手。〕
考試官教諭白　批　〔講則𣉻處得旨。〕
詩人美嘉賓之德足以化民，而君子所當法也。夫有天下者，以德化為先也。嘉賓之德旣足以化民，非君子所當取法者哉？此燕饗賓客之詩也。意以我所望於嘉賓者，欲示之以有言，而乃得之於無言。維我嘉賓，大道藴諸心，遠近皆稱其令德，赫赫乎仁有聲、義有問也；實德備於己，上下皆稱其令名，昭昭乎彼無惡、此無斁也。譽望所加，而導民之路在其中，足以示之而使大
translation_en:
…and emulate them.
Associate Examiner Chen, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔The theme of seeking instruction is developed smoothly and coherently from beginning to end. The author may be called skilled at explaining the Odes. Accept this essay.〕
Mao Qu
Associate Examiner Deng, Instructor, comments: 〔A king seeks instruction entirely for the people's sake. The virtue of the excellent guests is sufficient to serve as an example to the people and ought to be emulated by the gentlemen who govern them. Instruction is contained within it. This composition grasps that point.〕
Examiner An, Instructor, comments: 〔The transitions and concluding passages capture the commentary's meaning profoundly. This must be an accomplished writer.〕
Examiner Bai, Instructor, comments: 〔The discussion of taking as a model and emulating [?] captures the essential meaning.〕
The poet praises the virtue of the excellent guests as sufficient to transform the people and as something gentlemen ought to emulate. For one who possesses all under Heaven, transformation through virtue takes precedence. Since the virtue of the excellent guests is sufficient to transform the people, should gentlemen not take it as their model? This is an ode about feasting guests. Its meaning is: what I hoped for from my excellent guests was instruction through words, yet I obtained it without words. These excellent guests of mine harbor the great Way in their hearts. Those far and near alike praise their fine virtue: resplendent indeed is their reputation for benevolence and righteousness. Genuine virtue is fully embodied in them. Those above and below alike acclaim their good name: manifestly, there is no hatred of them there, nor any weariness with them here. Wherever their reputation and prestige extend, the means of guiding the people are contained therein. They suffice to instruct the people and cause the great…

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
樸之風不散而為偷薄焉弊光所被而錫民之
極在於是足以喻之而使可封之俗不降而為
澆漓焉夫嘉賓之德足以化民如此凡我君子
正唯此為急則而象之以為治道計豈可以他
求哉凡欲化民當以此為法儀而刑之以為斯
民計豈可以或後哉庶乎蘊大道而為德亦將
以其所以示民者而示吾民期底於治可也庶
乎畜令德而建極亦將以其所以善俗者而善
吾俗用弘其化可也夫嘉賓之所以為法於君
===
子者如此則其所以教我者亦不外乎此何待
於言語間哉噫周王可謂善於師臣者矣抑君
莫難於求言臣不難於進言進言而拒之者有
矣未有求言而忍負之者也夫求言固難求無
言之教尤難在臣必正己之大人而後能在君
必篤恭之至聖而後能是豈可以易言哉雖然
君臣之間有相成之道焉若周家可謂盛矣説
者乃歸之氣化然與
古訓是式威儀是力
punctuated:
樸之風不散而為偷薄焉。弊光所被，而錫民之極在於是，足以喻之而使可封之俗不降而為澆漓焉。夫嘉賓之德足以化民如此，凡我君子，正唯此為急，則而象之，以為治道計，豈可以他求哉？凡欲化民，當以此為法，儀而刑之，以為斯民計，豈可以或後哉？庶乎蘊大道而為德，亦將以其所以示民者而示吾民，期底於治可也；庶乎畜令德而建極，亦將以其所以善俗者而善吾俗，用弘其化可也。夫嘉賓之所以為法於君子者如此，則其所以教我者亦不外乎此，何待於言語間哉？噫！周王可謂善於師臣者矣。抑君莫難於求言，臣不難於進言。進言而拒之者有矣，未有求言而忍負之者也。夫求言固難，求無言之教尤難。在臣，必正己之大人而後能；在君，必篤恭之至聖而後能。是豈可以易言哉？雖然，君臣之間有相成之道焉，若周家可謂盛矣。説者乃歸之氣化，然與？

古訓是式，威儀是力。
translation_en:
…so that the spirit of unspoiled simplicity does not dissipate into meanness and dishonesty. Wherever his radiance reaches [?], therein lies the standard bestowed upon the people: it suffices to instruct them, so that customs worthy of households fit to receive enfeoffment do not decline into moral shallowness. Since the honored guest’s virtue can thus transform the people, all our noble men must make this their urgent concern. Taking it as their rule and model in planning the way of government, how could they seek elsewhere? All who wish to transform the people should take this as their standard. Emulating it in their plans for these people, how could they allow it to come later? If they would embody the Great Way and make it their virtue, they should instruct our people by the very means through which he instructs his, aiming thereby to attain good government. If they would nurture excellent virtue and establish the supreme standard, they should improve our customs by the very means through which he improves his, thereby extending their transforming influence. Since this is how the honored guest serves as a model for the noble man, his teaching of me likewise goes no further than this. Why should it depend upon spoken words?

Ah! The king of Zhou may indeed be called adept at taking his ministers as teachers. Yet for a ruler, nothing is harder than seeking counsel; for a minister, offering counsel is not hard. There have been rulers who rejected counsel when it was offered, but never a minister who could bear to disappoint a ruler who sought it. Seeking counsel is certainly difficult; seeking wordless instruction is harder still. A minister can accomplish this only if he is a great man who rectifies himself; a ruler can accomplish it only if he is a consummate sage of profound reverence. How could this be spoken of lightly? Nevertheless, ruler and minister have a way of bringing one another to fulfillment. In the house of Zhou, this may be said to have flourished. Yet commentators attribute it to the transforming action of qi. Is that so?

“He takes the ancient teachings as his model and devotes himself to dignified deportment.”

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
揚應儒
同考試官訓導陳　批　烝民首章乃三百篇中
性理文字此第二章承秉彞則即前物則此二
句言學問進修本前維則說來源委明白作者
率昧本旨獨此篇純正有理致可以式矣
同考試官教諭鄧　批　此章備舉仲山甫之德
此二句言學問進修不過大段着力處作者率
講始學工夫非也體認明白僅見此篇
考試官教諭安　批　文義從物則中說來良
是
===
考試官教諭白　批　文字簡古冲澹自是大
雅
稽諸古而脩諸身賢俟全美德然也甚矣美德
難乎其全也賢俟學問進脩而交致其力焉此
美德所以全而異於凡民也哉宣王命樊俟仲
山甫築城于齊尹吉甫作詩送之意謂山甫之
德天固啓之而學問進脩之力焉可誣也今夫
民莫不有是物則也而鮮能學焉山甫之德有
punctuated:
揚應儒

同考試官訓導陳批：烝民首章，乃三百篇中性理文字。此第二章承秉彞，則即前物則。此二句言學問進修，本前維則說來，源委明白。作者率昧本旨，獨此篇純正有理致，可以式矣。

同考試官教諭鄧批：此章備舉仲山甫之德，此二句言學問進修，不過大段着力處。作者率講始學工夫，非也。體認明白，僅見此篇。

考試官教諭安批：文義從物則中說來，良是。

考試官教諭白批：文字簡古冲澹，自是大雅。

稽諸古而脩諸身，賢俟全美德然也。甚矣，美德難乎其全也！賢俟學問進脩而交致其力焉，此美德所以全而異於凡民也哉！宣王命樊俟仲山甫築城于齊，尹吉甫作詩送之，意謂山甫之德，天固啓之，而學問進脩之力焉可誣也？今夫民莫不有是物則也，而鮮能學焉。山甫之德有
translation_en:
Yang Yingru

Associate Examiner Chen, Assistant Instructor, comments: The opening stanza of “The Multitudes” (Zheng min) is a passage concerning human nature and principle within the Three Hundred Odes. This second stanza continues the theme of holding fast to constant human norms; these norms are precisely the standards inherent in things mentioned earlier. These two lines discuss learning and progressive cultivation, developing their meaning from the preceding phrase “there are standards.” The connection is clear. Most writers fail to grasp the original purport. This essay alone is sound and correct, with coherent reasoning, and may serve as a model.

Associate Examiner Deng, Instructor, comments: This stanza comprehensively sets forth Zhong Shanfu’s virtues. These two lines speak of learning and progressive cultivation, simply identifying the principal area in which he applied his efforts. Most writers discuss the work of beginning to learn, which is mistaken. Only this essay displays a clear understanding.

Examiner An, Instructor, comments: The essay develops its meaning from the standards inherent in things. This is indeed correct.

Examiner Bai, Instructor, comments: The writing is concise, antique, tranquil, and restrained. It is truly of great elegance.

To consult antiquity and cultivate oneself: this is how a worthy lord [?] perfects his fine virtue. How exceedingly difficult it is to bring fine virtue to perfection! The worthy lord [?] applies his efforts jointly to learning and progressive cultivation. Is this not how his fine virtue becomes complete and distinguishes him from ordinary people? King Xuan ordered Zhong Shanfu, Lord of Fan [?], to build walls at Qi, and Yin Jifu composed a poem to see him off. Its meaning is that Heaven certainly awakened Shanfu’s virtue, but how could the contribution of learning and progressive cultivation be denied? Now, all people possess these standards inherent in things, yet few are able to learn. Shanfu’s virtue has …

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
獨得於學問者吾見其學于古訓以為畜德之
資前言往行莫非模範之所在尚友古人以為
進善之助成法遺矩一皆精神之所通盖儀式
刑五事之訓而能自得師也清緝熙五品之典
而主善為師也肯自是其學而過此民彝之則
乎亦莫不有是懿德也而鮮能脩焉山甫之德
有自得於進脩者吾見其中情好脩而動容周
旋不忘矜持之力慎厥身脩而動作威儀恒加
撿飭之功如耳目視聽之際必欲其惟聰惟明
===
也君臣父子之間必欲其有節有文也肯自惰
其力而違此帝降之衷乎夫如是則有以全美
德而異凡民措諸事業有餘裕矣於城齊何有
哉抑是德也易所謂極書所謂性所謂中皆一
物也山甫能舉之而其為功曰稽古脩身而已
稽古亦所以脩身也先民有言民受天地之中
以生所謂命也是以有動作禮義威儀之則以
定命也又曰能者養之以福若山甫者可謂能
定命矣而事業之大非養之以福者乎
punctuated: 獨得於學問者。吾見其學于古訓，以為畜德之資，前言往行莫非模範之所在；尚友古人，以為進善之助，成法遺矩一皆精神之所通。盖儀式刑五事之訓，而能自得師也；清緝熙五品之典，而主善為師也。肯自是其學，而過此民彝之則乎？亦莫不有是懿德也，而鮮能脩焉。山甫之德有自得於進脩者，吾見其中情好脩，而動容周旋不忘矜持之力；慎厥身脩，而動作威儀恒加撿飭之功。如耳目視聽之際，必欲其惟聰惟明也；君臣父子之間，必欲其有節有文也。肯自惰其力，而違此帝降之衷乎？夫如是，則有以全美德而異凡民，措諸事業有餘裕矣。於城齊何有哉？抑是德也，《易》所謂極，《書》所謂性、所謂中，皆一物也。山甫能舉之，而其為功曰稽古脩身而已。稽古亦所以脩身也。先民有言：「民受天地之中以生，所謂命也。是以有動作禮義威儀之則，以定命也。」又曰：「能者養之以福。」若山甫者，可謂能定命矣，而事業之大非養之以福者乎？
translation_en:
…something uniquely attained through learning and inquiry. I see that he studies ancient teachings to provide resources for accumulating virtue: the words and deeds of the ancients all furnish models. He befriends the ancients in spirit to assist his advancement in goodness: his spirit communes with all their established methods and inherited standards. He takes as his models the teachings concerning the Five Activities and thus finds teachers for himself; he clarifies and illuminates [?] the canonical norms of the five human relationships, taking goodness as his teacher. Would he presume that his own learning was sufficient and transgress these constant norms of human conduct?

All people likewise possess this admirable virtue, yet few cultivate it. There is something in Shanfu’s virtue that he has personally attained through advancement in self-cultivation. I see that in his innermost feelings he delights in cultivation, never forgetting the effort of self-restraint in his bearing and movements. He attends carefully to cultivating himself, constantly applying the work of discipline to his actions and demeanor. Whenever his ears and eyes hear and see, he insists upon acuity of hearing and clarity of sight; in the relationships between ruler and minister and father and son, he insists upon due measure and proper form. Would he slacken his efforts and violate this balanced nature bestowed by the Lord on High? In this way he can perfect his virtue and distinguish himself from ordinary people, with more than enough capacity to apply it to practical undertakings. What difficulty, then, could there be in building the walls of Qi?

Moreover, this virtue, what the Book of Changes calls the Ultimate, and what the Book of Documents calls nature and calls the Mean, are all one thing. Shanfu could fully realize it, and his efforts amounted simply to examining antiquity and cultivating himself. Examining antiquity is itself a means of self-cultivation. An ancient worthy said: “People receive the balanced principle of Heaven and Earth at birth; this is what is called their allotted mandate. Thus there are standards for conduct, ritual propriety, righteousness, and dignified bearing, by which to secure that mandate.” He also said: “Those who are capable nurture it through blessings.” Someone like Shanfu may indeed be said to have secured his mandate. And was not the greatness of his achievements a matter of nurturing it through blessings?

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
春秋
冬齊人來歸衛俘〔莊公六年〕六月齊侯來
獻戎捷〔莊公三十有一年〕
王儒
同考試官訓導吳　批〔此題兩傳明甚盖不以〕
〔隱僻困士子但作者率多浮冗可厭豈以其易〕
〔而忽之歟是篇措詞精當且以輕功利重道義〕
〔立說必邃於經學者〕
考試官教諭安　批〔簡而明華而不肆可為〕
〔學經者式〕
===
考試官教諭白　批〔體貼經傳而悉去浮詞〕
〔無踰此篇〕
大國分利于內春秋正義以貶之伯主矜功于
內春秋明道以抑之盖利不可徇功不可伐也
考經所書意自見矣且寶玉之俘成湯所以伐
三朡也齊襄之歸衛俘春秋何貶乎爾盖為國
者非無賄之患而無義問之難彼衛朔逆亂天
常王法所不赦者齊襄盍亦率義師以討之焉
punctuated:
春秋

冬，齊人來歸衛俘〔莊公六年〕。六月，齊侯來獻戎捷〔莊公三十有一年〕。

王儒

同考試官訓導吳批〔此題兩傳明甚，盖不以〕〔隱僻困士子。但作者率多浮冗可厭，豈以其易〕〔而忽之歟？是篇措詞精當，且以輕功利、重道義〕〔立說，必邃於經學者。〕

考試官教諭安批〔簡而明，華而不肆，可為〕〔學經者式。〕

考試官教諭白批〔體貼經傳而悉去浮詞，〕〔無踰此篇。〕

大國分利于內，春秋正義以貶之；伯主矜功于內，春秋明道以抑之。盖利不可徇，功不可伐也。考經所書，意自見矣。且寶玉之俘，成湯所以伐三朡也，齊襄之歸衛俘，春秋何貶乎爾？盖為國者，非無賄之患，而無義問之難。彼衛朔逆亂天常，王法所不赦者，齊襄盍亦率義師以討之焉？
translation_en:
Spring and Autumn Annals

“In winter, men of Qi came to deliver spoils taken from Wei.” 〔Sixth year of Duke Zhuang.〕 “In the sixth month, the Marquis of Qi came to present spoils from his victory over the Rong.” 〔Thirty-first year of Duke Zhuang.〕

Wang Ru

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Assistant Instructor: 〔The two commentaries explain this topic very clearly; the intention was evidently not to burden the candidates with obscure or abstruse material. Yet most responses were tiresomely superficial and prolix. Did the writers slight the topic because it was easy? This essay is precise and apt in its wording, and bases its argument on valuing moral principle above achievement and profit. Its author must be deeply versed in classical learning.〕

Comment by Examiner An, Instructor: 〔Concise yet clear, elegant yet restrained: it can serve as a model for students of the Classics.〕

Comment by Examiner Bai, Instructor: 〔For closely following the Classic and its commentaries while entirely eliminating empty verbiage, nothing surpasses this essay.〕

When a great state shared its gains with our state, the Spring and Autumn Annals upheld righteousness to condemn it; when a hegemon vaunted his achievements in our state, the Spring and Autumn Annals clarified the Way to restrain him. For profit must not be pursued, nor achievements boasted of. Examine what the Classic records, and its meaning becomes apparent. Now, taking precious jade as spoils was something Cheng Tang did in his attack on Sanzong. Why, then, does the Spring and Autumn Annals condemn Duke Xiang of Qi for delivering the spoils taken from Wei? For those who govern states, the concern is not a lack of wealth; the difficulty lies in lacking a reputation for righteousness. Shuo of Wei had defied and disrupted Heaven’s constant order, an offense that royal law could not pardon. Why did Duke Xiang of Qi not lead a righteous army to punish him?

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
用賄顧借四國撓王官以往納焉遂以所獲之
俘來歸于魯毋乃各利其惡而助之與然古之
諸侯率由典常以蕃王室未聞私相遺賂者何
其喪心若是邪吾於伊訓見殉貨之儆焉於盤
庚見總貨之戒焉況援惡乎是故特書歸俘以
結正諸侯有規利之心而後動於惡爾若僖公
之奏吉甫所以伐玁狁也齊桓之獻戎捷春秋
何抑乎爾蓋為伯者非無功之患而無文德之
難彼山戎僻在荒服王法所不治者齊桓盍姑
===
內樹德以綏之焉用威顧勤三軍越千里以往
伐焉遂以所獲之捷躬獻于魯毋乃自以為功
而誇之與然古之諸侯有四夷之功則獻于王
未聞自相遺俘者何其屈體若是邪吾於禹謨
見不伐之辭焉於說命見矜能之訓焉矧略遠
乎是故特書獻捷以深抑桓公有急功之心而
動兵於遠爾吁徇於利必至於奪攘急於功必
至於生事春秋垂戒之意其在玆乎夫義所以
建利也道所以懋功也是以先王之訓動則思
punctuated:
用賄？顧借四國，撓王官以往納焉，遂以所獲之俘來歸于魯，毋乃各利其惡而助之與？然古之諸侯率由典常，以蕃王室，未聞私相遺賂者，何其喪心若是邪？吾於《伊訓》見殉貨之儆焉，於《盤庚》見總貨之戒焉，況援惡乎？是故特書歸俘，以結正諸侯有規利之心而後動於惡爾。
若僖公之奏，吉甫所以伐玁狁也，齊桓之獻戎捷，《春秋》何抑乎爾？蓋為伯者，非無功之患，而無文德之難。彼山戎僻在荒服，王法所不治者，齊桓盍姑內樹德以綏之，焉用威？顧勤三軍，越千里以往伐焉，遂以所獲之捷躬獻于魯，毋乃自以為功而誇之與？然古之諸侯有四夷之功，則獻于王，未聞自相遺俘者，何其屈體若是邪？吾於《禹謨》見不伐之辭焉，於《說命》見矜能之訓焉，矧略遠乎？是故特書獻捷，以深抑桓公有急功之心而動兵於遠爾。
吁！徇於利，必至於奪攘；急於功，必至於生事。《春秋》垂戒之意，其在玆乎？夫義所以建利也，道所以懋功也。是以先王之訓，動則思
translation_en:
…use bribes? Instead, he enlisted the four states to obstruct the king’s officers and went to restore him to his position. He then sent the spoils he had obtained to Lu. Was this not a case of each seeking profit from the other’s wrongdoing and assisting it? Yet the ancient regional lords followed established norms in order to defend the royal house; one never heard of their privately giving one another gifts of wealth. How could they lose their moral judgment so completely? In the Instructions of Yi, I find a warning against pursuing wealth; in Pan Geng, I find an admonition against hoarding wealth. How much more objectionable, then, is abetting wrongdoing! Thus the Spring and Autumn Annals specifically records the delivery of spoils, conclusively condemning the regional lords for first harboring thoughts of profit and then being moved to wrongdoing.
As for the achievement of Duke Xi [?], it was through Jifu’s campaign against the Xianyun that it was accomplished. Why, then, does the Spring and Autumn Annals disparage Duke Huan of Qi’s presentation of spoils from his victory over the Rong? For a hegemon, the concern is not a lack of military achievement; the difficulty lies in possessing civil virtue. The Mountain Rong lived far away in the remote outer domain, beyond the reach of royal law. Why did Duke Huan of Qi not first cultivate virtue at home in order to bring them peace? What need was there to use force? Instead, he wearied the three armies, traveling a thousand li to attack them. He then personally presented the spoils of his victory to Lu. Was this not treating the deed as his own accomplishment and boasting of it? Yet when the ancient regional lords achieved victories over the peoples of the four quarters, they presented their spoils to the king; one never heard of their giving captives to one another. Why did he abase himself in this way? In the Counsels of Yu, I find words against boasting of one’s achievements; in the Charge to Yue, I find an admonition against pride in one’s abilities. How much more does this apply to attacking distant peoples! Thus the Spring and Autumn Annals specifically records the presentation of spoils, sharply censuring Duke Huan for his eagerness for achievement, which led him to wage war far away.
Alas! Pursuing profit inevitably leads to plunder; eagerness for achievement inevitably leads to stirring up trouble. Is this not the warning that the Spring and Autumn Annals intended to leave to posterity? Righteousness is the means of establishing benefit, and the Way is the means of advancing achievement. Thus the teaching of the former kings was that, whenever one acts, one should consider…

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
義行則思道故國無不卑遠無不懷春秋之時
嚋克知之討齊之師竟沮于慶封滅狄之俘載
獻于士會大抵然也嗚呼以此爲防後世猶有
貪得重賂僥倖邉功者
秋晉荀吳帥師伐鮮虞〔昭公十有五年八〕
月晉荀吳帥師滅陸渾之戎〔昭公十有七年〕
毛熙
同考試官訓導吳　批〔善敘荀吳當時用兵之事不泛不畧且歸重於君臣夷夏之分可謂得〕
===
春秋之大旨故録之
考試官教諭安　批〔融會二傳成文而序事〕
嚴整異乎諸子之撰
考試官教諭白　批〔昔人論左氏之文詞氣〕
不迫此作近之
春秋於伯臣之用兵有明其近於正者有明其
近於義者夫用兵之道惟正與義爾荀吳其庶
乎春秋所以皆免於貶也昔鮮虞密邇于晉荀
punctuated:
義，行則思道，故國無不卑，遠無不懷。春秋之時，嚋克知之？討齊之師竟沮于慶封，滅狄之俘載獻于士會，大抵然也。嗚呼！以此爲防，後世猶有貪得重賂、僥倖邉功者。
秋，晉荀吳帥師伐鮮虞。〔昭公十有五年八〕月，晉荀吳帥師滅陸渾之戎。〔昭公十有七年〕
毛熙。
同考試官訓導吳批：〔善敘荀吳當時用兵之事，不泛不畧，且歸重於君臣夷夏之分，可謂得〕春秋之大旨，故録之。
考試官教諭安批：〔融會二傳成文，而序事〕嚴整，異乎諸子之撰。
考試官教諭白批：〔昔人論左氏之文，詞氣〕不迫，此作近之。
春秋於伯臣之用兵，有明其近於正者，有明其近於義者。夫用兵之道，惟正與義爾。荀吳其庶乎！春秋所以皆免於貶也。昔鮮虞密邇于晉，荀
translation_en:
…righteousness; in acting, consider the Way. Thus no state failed to submit, and no distant people failed to be drawn into allegiance. In the Spring and Autumn period, who could understand this? [?] The army sent to punish Qi was ultimately thwarted by Qing Feng, and captives taken in destroying the Di were presented to Shi Hui: affairs generally followed this pattern. Alas! Even with this warning, later generations still included men who coveted substantial bribes and sought the chance of military distinction on the frontier.
“In autumn, Xun Wu of Jin led an army to attack Xianyu.” 〔Fifteenth year of Duke Zhao; ‘eight’〕 “In the [eighth?] month, Xun Wu of Jin led an army to destroy the Rong of Luhun.” 〔Seventeenth year of Duke Zhao〕 [The placement of ‘eight’ in the transcription is doubtful.]
Mao Xi.
Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Assistant Instructor: 〔“He skillfully recounts Xun Wu’s military operations at the time, without being vague or cursory, and places the emphasis on the distinctions between ruler and minister, and between the Yi and the Xia. He may be said to have grasped〕 the central purport of the Spring and Autumn Annals; hence its inclusion.”
Comment by Examiner An, Instructor: 〔“He integrates the two commentaries into his composition, and his narration〕 is rigorous and orderly, unlike the compositions of the other candidates.”
Comment by Examiner Bai, Instructor: 〔“Earlier writers, discussing the prose of Master Zuo, said that its diction and manner〕 were unhurried. This composition approaches that quality.”
In its treatment of military operations undertaken by ministers of the hegemons, the Spring and Autumn Annals sometimes makes clear their approximation to rectitude, and sometimes their approximation to righteousness. The way of employing armies consists solely in rectitude and righteousness. Did not Xun Wu come close to these? This is why the Spring and Autumn Annals spared him censure in both instances. Formerly, Xianyu lay very close to Jin, and Xun…

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
吳將兵以伐之且圍鼓焉吾聞周官有八成之
法以臣悖君罪也彼鼓方被圍而其臣請降罪
莫大焉若受而弗拒非所以懲姦慝公好惡也
荀吳則曰吾寧無城不可欲城而邇姦吾寧無
邑不可獲邑而賈怠乃俾爾繕守俾爾脩城及
食竭力盡而後鼓子就俘焉君子謂荀吳於是
乎知正正以加敵視昔見利忘義以行欺詐不
猶愈乎故昔陽之入稱國而此書其名氏非褒
之也纔免於貶爾則用兵非正者可知矣若陸
===
渾啓貳于晉荀吳將兵以滅之遂至雒焉吾聞
禹貢有五服之制以夷居華變也彼雒在王畿
而陸渾雜處變莫邇焉若縱而弗治非所以明族
類別內外也荀吳則以屠蒯將命事已請于王
庭祭史用牲師遂陳于甸服乃問爾南向驅爾
南奔及衆潰俘獲而後王畿始靖焉君子謂荀
吳於是乎知義義以膺戎視彼闢土服遠以圖
強霸不有間乎故潞甲之滅稱師與人而此書
其名氏非褒詞也纔得無貶爾則窮兵非義者
punctuated:
吳將兵以伐之，且圍鼓焉。吾聞《周官》有八成之法，以臣悖君，罪也。彼鼓方被圍，而其臣請降，罪莫大焉。若受而弗拒，非所以懲姦慝、公好惡也。荀吳則曰：「吾寧無城，不可欲城而邇姦；吾寧無邑，不可獲邑而賈怠。」乃俾爾繕守，俾爾脩城，及食竭力盡，而後鼓子就俘焉。君子謂荀吳於是乎知正。正以加敵，視昔見利忘義以行欺詐，不猶愈乎？故昔陽之入稱國，而此書其名氏，非褒之也，纔免於貶爾。則用兵非正者可知矣。
若陸渾啓貳于晉，荀吳將兵以滅之，遂至雒焉。吾聞《禹貢》有五服之制，以夷居華，變也。彼雒在王畿，而陸渾雜處，變莫邇焉。若縱而弗治，非所以明族類、別內外也。荀吳則以屠蒯將命，事已請于王庭；祭史用牲，師遂陳于甸服。乃問爾南向，驅爾南奔，及衆潰俘獲，而後王畿始靖焉。君子謂荀吳於是乎知義。義以膺戎，視彼闢土服遠以圖強霸，不有間乎？故潞甲之滅稱師與人，而此書其名氏，非褒詞也，纔得無貶爾。則窮兵非義者
translation_en:
…Wu led troops to attack them and also besieged Gu. I have heard that the Offices of Zhou sets out eight established rules of adjudication: for a minister to rebel against his lord is a crime. While Gu was under siege, its ministers offered to surrender; no crime could be greater. To accept rather than reject their offer would be no way to punish wickedness and make approval and disapproval impartial. Xun Wu therefore said: “I would rather go without a city than desire one and draw wicked men close; I would rather go without a town than acquire one and invite negligence.” He then allowed them to put their defenses in order and repair their walls. Only when their provisions and strength were exhausted was the ruler of Gu taken captive. The gentleman says that in this Xun Wu understood rectitude. To confront an enemy with rectitude—was this not better than those earlier cases of forgetting righteousness at the sight of profit and practicing deceit? Thus, the entry for the incursion into Xiyang names the state, whereas here the Spring and Autumn Annals records his personal and clan names. This does not praise him; he merely escapes censure. We may therefore understand the judgment upon those who wage war without rectitude.
When Luhun began to waver in its allegiance to Jin, Xun Wu led troops to destroy it and proceeded to Luo. I have heard that the Tribute of Yu establishes the system of five zones of service: for the Yi peoples to dwell among the Hua is a disruption of order. Luo lay within the royal domain, yet the people of Luhun lived intermingled there; no disruption could be closer at hand. To indulge them without taking corrective action would be no way to clarify distinctions between peoples or distinguish the inner realm from the outer. Xun Wu therefore sent Tu Kuai to convey his message, and the matter was duly put before the royal court. The sacrificial scribe used the sacrificial animals, and the army then deployed in the royal agricultural domain. He then advanced southward to call them to account [?] and drove them fleeing south. Only after their forces had scattered and captives had been taken was the royal domain pacified. The gentleman says that in this Xun Wu understood righteousness. To assail the Rong in righteousness—was this not different from expanding territory and subduing distant peoples in pursuit of power and hegemony? Thus, the entries for the destruction of Lu and Jia refer to an “army” and to “men,” whereas here the Annals records his personal and clan names. These are not words of praise; he merely avoids censure. Thus, as for those who exhaust their forces in warfare without righteousness…

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
可知矣夫悖君者拒之則君臣之義明亂華者
治之則華夷之防立荀吳其晉之良乎抑又有
議焉先王耀德不觀兵維時晉伯方衰荀吳不
能翼其君以脩厥德以復文襄悼公之業顧紛
紛于干戈則亦何益春秋所以無貶焉者蓋欲
杜悖君之萌遏亂華之禍爾嗚呼悉怛請降唐
臣以為不可受羌胡徙内晉臣以為不宜居其
知此義乎
禮記
禮樂之情同故明王以相沿也故事與時
===
並名與功偕
袁繼
同考試官教諭徐 批 題本平易類能言之而
於不易禮樂之體始終說得痛快僅見此篇是
用錄出
考試官教諭安 批 聖王禮樂制作不同體
未嘗易子能說得明快殆深於經學者
考試官教諭白 批 發揮體用制作瑩潤可
punctuated:
可知矣。夫悖君者拒之，則君臣之義明；亂華者治之，則華夷之防立。荀吳其晉之良乎！抑又有議焉：先王耀德不觀兵。維時晉伯方衰，荀吳不能翼其君以脩厥德，以復文襄悼公之業，顧紛紛于干戈，則亦何益？春秋所以無貶焉者，蓋欲杜悖君之萌，遏亂華之禍爾。嗚呼！悉怛請降，唐臣以為不可受；羌胡徙内，晉臣以為不宜居。其知此義乎？
禮記
禮樂之情同，故明王以相沿也。故事與時並，名與功偕。
袁繼
同考試官教諭徐批：題本平易，類能言之，而於不易禮樂之體，始終說得痛快，僅見此篇，是用錄出。
考試官教諭安批：聖王禮樂制作不同，體未嘗易。子能說得明快，殆深於經學者。
考試官教諭白批：發揮體用制作，瑩潤可
translation_en:
…can thus be understood. If those who defy their ruler are resisted, the rightful relationship between ruler and subject is made clear; if those who disrupt the Chinese realm are punished, the boundary between Chinese and non-Chinese is established. Was Xun Wu not a worthy servant of Jin! Yet there is also a criticism to make. The former kings displayed their virtue rather than parading their troops. At that time Jin’s hegemony was declining. Xun Wu could not assist his ruler in cultivating his virtue and restoring the achievements of Dukes Wen, Xiang, and Dao, but instead busied himself with warfare. What benefit was there in this? The Spring and Autumn Annals refrains from censuring him because it seeks to forestall incipient defiance of rulers and avert the calamity of disruption to the Chinese realm. Alas! When Xida [?] requested permission to surrender, a Tang minister held that the surrender should not be accepted; when the Qiang and Hu moved into the interior, a Jin minister held that they should not be allowed to settle there. Did they understand this principle?
Record of Rites
“The essential feelings underlying ritual and music are the same; therefore enlightened kings carry them forward from one reign to the next. Thus undertakings accord with their times, and names match achievements.”
Yuan Ji
Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor: The topic is straightforward, and most candidates can say something about it. But this essay alone explains, forcefully and satisfyingly from beginning to end, the unchanging substance of ritual and music. For this reason it has been selected for inclusion.
Comment by Examiner An, Instructor: The sage kings differed in their institutions of ritual and music, but the underlying substance never changed. You explain this clearly and incisively; you must be deeply versed in classical learning.
Comment by Examiner Bai, Instructor: The exposition of substance, function, and the establishment of institutions is lucid and polished, fit to be…

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
誦
惟制作之本聖人所不易故制作之末聖人所
不同葢本同而末異正所以見其為同也然則
聖人之制禮作樂夫豈苟哉樂記君子謂夫有
一代之興王必有一代之禮樂然禮樂也者所
以緣人情而制作者也故以禮之情言之敬其
是已敬也者禮由斯制歷萬世而同歸有不可
得而強變焉以樂之情言之愛其是已愛也者
樂緣斯作曠千古而一致有不可得而或易焉
===
惟其不可變故聖帝之興不能不制禮以飾治
而敬者禮制之本也則相沿而無異惟其不可
易故明王之起不能不作樂以象功而愛者樂
生之本也則相因而不殊夫聖人所因如此是
故秉時設施者事也事則與時而並如揖讓施
於唐虞而人不以為非放伐施於夏商而人不
以為異事之變者時之變也相並而為用耳若
夫合敬之情何嘗與時而並變哉因功而起立
者名也名則與功而偕如韶武名於虞廷而紹
punctuated:
誦。

惟制作之本，聖人所不易，故制作之末，聖人所不同。葢本同而末異，正所以見其為同也。然則聖人之制禮作樂，夫豈苟哉？《樂記》君子謂，夫有一代之興王，必有一代之禮樂。然禮樂也者，所以緣人情而制作者也。故以禮之情言之，敬其是已。敬也者，禮由斯制，歷萬世而同歸，有不可得而強變焉。以樂之情言之，愛其是已。愛也者，樂緣斯作，曠千古而一致，有不可得而或易焉。惟其不可變，故聖帝之興，不能不制禮以飾治，而敬者，禮制之本也，則相沿而無異。惟其不可易，故明王之起，不能不作樂以象功，而愛者，樂生之本也，則相因而不殊。夫聖人所因如此，是故秉時設施者，事也；事則與時而並。如揖讓施於唐虞，而人不以為非；放伐施於夏商，而人不以為異。事之變者，時之變也，相並而為用耳。若夫合敬之情，何嘗與時而並變哉？因功而起立者，名也；名則與功而偕。如韶武名於虞廷，而紹
translation_en:
…fit to be recited.

It is the foundations of ritual and musical institutions that sages do not alter; hence, in their outward particulars, sages establish different forms. That their foundations are the same while their particulars differ is precisely what reveals their underlying unity. How, then, could the sages have instituted rites and composed music arbitrarily? The gentleman in the Record of Music says that whenever a dynasty has a founding king, it must have rites and music proper to that dynasty. Yet rites and music are institutions fashioned in accordance with human feelings. Thus, if we speak of the feeling underlying rites, it is reverence. Reverence is the source from which rites are instituted: through ten thousand generations they converge upon it, and it cannot be forcibly changed. If we speak of the feeling underlying music, it is love. Love is the source from which music is composed: across the ages it remains consistent, and it cannot be altered.

Precisely because this cannot change, when a sage emperor arises, he must institute rites to adorn his governance; yet reverence, the foundation of ritual institutions, is transmitted without alteration. Precisely because this cannot be altered, when an enlightened king arises, he must compose music to represent his achievements; yet love, the foundation from which music arises, is inherited without difference. Such is what the sages follow. Accordingly, what they put into practice in keeping with the times consists of actions; actions move with the times. Thus, deferential yielding was practiced under Tang and Yu, and people did not consider it wrong; banishment and punitive conquest were practiced under Xia and Shang, and people did not consider them anomalous. Changes in actions are changes in the times: they simply move together to serve practical purposes. But when have the shared feelings of reverence ever changed along with the times? What is established in response to achievements consists of names; names accompany achievements. Thus, Shaowu [?] was named at the court of Yu, and carried forward …

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
讓之成功以象大武名於周室而征伐之大烈
以章名之異者功之異也相借而為華耳若夫
同愛之情何嘗與功而借異哉吁因其同而變
其異于以辯其異而歸諸同也聖人會通以興
禮樂有如是夫大抵情之不可變雖聖人無所
用其聰用之不可同在聖人無所執其智無非
一自然而然也以是制禮作樂大之則與天地
同其和節達之則使四海合其敬愛盖有不期
然而然者任制作之柄者既知禮樂之所以為
異又知禮樂之所以為同則庶乎達禮樂之體
用矣
===
故君子信讓以涖百姓則民之報禮重
王儀鳳
同考試官教諭徐　批　〔君子涖百姓不出政教〕
子能發揮明盡而筆勢沛然可以式矣
考試官教諭安　批　〔融會傳註而文不凡佳〕
士也
考試官教諭白　批　〔君民感應之機宛然在目〕
punctuated:
讓之成功以象；大武名於周室，而征伐之大烈以章。名之異者，功之異也，相借而為華耳。若夫同愛之情，何嘗與功而借異哉？吁！因其同而變其異，于以辯其異而歸諸同也。聖人會通以興禮樂，有如是夫！大抵情之不可變，雖聖人無所用其聰；用之不可同，在聖人無所執其智。無非一自然而然也。以是制禮作樂，大之則與天地同其和節，達之則使四海合其敬愛，盖有不期然而然者。任制作之柄者，既知禮樂之所以為異，又知禮樂之所以為同，則庶乎達禮樂之體用矣。
故君子信讓以涖百姓，則民之報禮重。
王儀鳳
同考試官教諭徐　批：〔君子涖百姓，不出政教。〕子能發揮明盡，而筆勢沛然，可以式矣。
考試官教諭安　批：〔融會傳註，而文不凡，佳〕士也。
考試官教諭白　批：〔君民感應之機，宛然在目。〕
translation_en:
…the achievement of yielding the throne was thereby represented; the Great Wu was named at the Zhou court, thereby displaying the great deeds of conquest. Differences in names arise from differences in achievements; each borrows from the other to lend it splendor. But when has the shared feeling of love ever borrowed differences from achievements? Ah! By following what they share while changing what differs, one distinguishes their differences and brings them back to their common ground. Such is the way the sages comprehensively grasped their interconnections to establish ritual and music! In general, where feelings cannot change, even the sages have no occasion to employ their discernment; where applications cannot be identical, the sages cannot cling to their own wisdom. All simply follows its natural course. Establishing ritual and creating music on this basis, on the grandest scale they share the harmony and measured order of Heaven and Earth; extended everywhere, they unite all within the Four Seas in reverence and love. These results indeed come about without being deliberately sought. If those who wield the authority to establish institutions understand both what makes ritual and music different and what makes them alike, they will come close to comprehending their substance and function.
“Thus, when the gentleman presides over the common people with trustworthiness and deference, the people respond with profound propriety.”
Wang Yifeng 王儀鳳
Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor: 〔“The gentleman’s presiding over the common people goes no further than government and moral instruction.”〕 You have expounded this clearly and exhaustively, and your writing flows with vigor. It may serve as a model.
Comment by Examiner An, Instructor: 〔“He integrates the commentaries and annotations, and his writing is exceptional: an excellent〕 scholar.”
Comment by Examiner Bai, Instructor: 〔“The workings of stimulus and response between ruler and people appear vividly before our eyes.”〕

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
上能不忽於所施下必不輕於所報夫下之報
禮顧上施之道何如耳然則君之施於民者而
豈可忽乎坊記謂夫君民之分雖殊而施報之
機不爽是故以術馭民其弊易至於自欺君子
則知民愚而神也凡所以施之者平易真實略
無逆詐猜忌之私以位臨民其勢易至於自恃
君子則知民賤而貴也凡所以治之者謙卑遜
順絕無矜己陵人之態如行其政焉必參揆乎
輿論之公然後遜以出之信以成之也如施其
===
教與必允協乎群情之當然後謙以居之忠以
行之也夫不忽於所施如此由是觀感於謙光
之下者咸起其恭順之貞翕受於敷施之餘者
均竭其報效之念養君以自安也事君以自顯
也誠款畢露凡分之所當盡者無不盡之矣報
禮何其厚邪趨事忘其勞也犯難忘其身也忠
義激發凡力之所能為者無弗為之矣報禮不
亦重邪是則一施一報各有其道如此而其機
則在乎上之人也為君者而可不慎其所以施
punctuated: 上能不忽於所施，下必不輕於所報。夫下之報禮，顧上施之道何如耳。然則君之施於民者，而豈可忽乎？《坊記》謂夫君民之分雖殊，而施報之機不爽。是故以術馭民，其弊易至於自欺；君子則知民愚而神也，凡所以施之者，平易真實，略無逆詐猜忌之私。以位臨民，其勢易至於自恃；君子則知民賤而貴也，凡所以治之者，謙卑遜順，絕無矜己陵人之態。如行其政焉，必參揆乎輿論之公，然後遜以出之，信以成之也。如施其教與，必允協乎群情之當，然後謙以居之，忠以行之也。夫不忽於所施如此，由是觀感於謙光之下者，咸起其恭順之貞；翕受於敷施之餘者，均竭其報效之念。養君以自安也，事君以自顯也，誠款畢露，凡分之所當盡者，無不盡之矣。報禮何其厚邪！趨事忘其勞也，犯難忘其身也，忠義激發，凡力之所能為者，無弗為之矣。報禮不亦重邪？是則一施一報，各有其道如此，而其機則在乎上之人也。為君者而可不慎其所以施
translation_en:
If those above do not neglect what they bestow, those below will certainly not treat lightly what they return. The people’s propriety in reciprocating depends simply on how those above bestow their benefits. How, then, could a ruler be careless about what he bestows upon the people? The Record of Restraints (Fang ji) explains that although ruler and people differ in their stations, the workings of giving and reciprocation do not fail. Thus, when one controls the people through stratagems, the resulting abuses readily lead to self-deception. The gentleman, however, knows that the people, though ignorant, possess uncanny discernment. In all that he bestows upon them, he is straightforward and sincere, without the slightest selfish inclination to anticipate deceit or harbor suspicion. When one rules the people by virtue of rank, that position readily leads to self-conceit. The gentleman, however, knows that the people, though lowly, are precious. In all his dealings with them, he is humble and deferential, wholly free of any manner of exalting himself and overbearing others. When implementing his government, he must consult and weigh impartial public opinion; only then does he introduce his measures with deference and carry them through with trustworthiness. When imparting his instruction, he must truly accord with what is fitting in the sentiments of the people; only then does he occupy his position with humility and carry out his instruction with wholehearted sincerity.
When he takes such care over what he bestows, all who witness and are moved by the radiance of his humility awaken to steadfast reverence and obedience; all who together receive his widely bestowed benefits devote themselves fully to repaying him through service. They support their ruler and thereby secure their own peace; they serve their ruler and thereby distinguish themselves. Their sincerity is fully revealed, and they leave unfulfilled none of the duties their station requires. How generous is their propriety in reciprocating! They hasten to their tasks, forgetting their toil; they confront danger, forgetting their own persons. Stirred by loyalty and righteousness, they leave undone nothing within their power. Is their propriety in reciprocating not weighty indeed? Thus, giving and reciprocation each have their proper way, yet the impulse that sets them in motion lies with those above. Can one who is a ruler fail to take care over how he bestows…

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
之也邪嗟夫信所以結民大詐若信而后信之
道失讓所以示民大偽若讓而后讓之道乖自
夫忘言不讓之化遠而后盟誓相要之會作禮
讓為國之論興斯可以觀世變矣誠以飾貌之
召徠不若實德之感孚也故上信讓而民之報
禮重有由然矣報禮重而忘言不讓之化可馴
至矣茲固君子之為政而亦聖人立言之意也
噫以是垂訓而后世猶有徙木以立信謙恭以
下士者亦獨何哉
===
第貳場
論
虛心以為天下
毛渠
同考試官訓導陳　批　題本正大而作者多失
之浮泛過於纖巧此篇莊重典雅無一字冗弱
且帝王虛心為治氣象委曲詳盡宛然在目誠
可於是而亮子之心矣
同考試官教諭鄧　批　文法典則義理精當不
punctuated:
之也邪？嗟夫！信所以結民，大詐若信，而后信之道失；讓所以示民，大偽若讓，而后讓之道乖。自夫忘言不讓之化遠，而后盟誓相要之會作，禮讓為國之論興，斯可以觀世變矣。誠以飾貌之召徠，不若實德之感孚也。故上信讓，而民之報禮重，有由然矣。報禮重，而忘言不讓之化可馴至矣。茲固君子之為政，而亦聖人立言之意也。噫！以是垂訓，而后世猶有徙木以立信、謙恭以下士者，亦獨何哉？

第貳場
論
虛心以為天下
毛渠

同考試官訓導陳　批：題本正大，而作者多失之浮泛，過於纖巧。此篇莊重典雅，無一字冗弱，且帝王虛心為治氣象，委曲詳盡，宛然在目。誠可於是而亮子之心矣。

同考試官教諭鄧　批：文法典則，義理精當，不
translation_en:
…in bestowing it? Alas! Trustworthiness binds the people together; when great deceit resembles trustworthiness, the way of trustworthiness is lost. Deference sets an example for the people; when great hypocrisy resembles deference, the way of deference goes astray. Once the transforming influence that transcended words and outward acts of deference had receded, gatherings at which people bound one another by covenants and oaths arose, and discussions of governing a state through ritual and deference flourished. Here one can observe how the world has changed. Truly, attracting people through an embellished appearance cannot compare with moving them to trust through genuine virtue. Thus there is good reason why, when those above are trustworthy and deferential, the people respond generously with propriety. When their response is generous, the transforming influence that transcends words and outward acts of deference can gradually be attained. This is indeed how the gentleman governs, and it is also what the sage intended in setting forth his teaching. Ah! Although this instruction was handed down, later generations still had men who moved a timber to establish trust, or adopted a humble and respectful manner to show deference to scholars. Why should this have been so?

Second Session
Discourse
Governing All under Heaven with an Open Mind
By Mao Qu

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Assistant Instructor: The topic itself is upright and grand, but writers mostly fall into superficial generalities or excessive ingenuity in fine details. This essay is dignified, classically refined, and elegant, without a single redundant or feeble word. Moreover, its depiction of emperors and kings governing with open minds is nuanced and exhaustive, appearing vividly before our eyes. Truly, through this one can discern your own heart.

Comment by Associate Examiner Deng, Instructor: The composition follows classical models, and its reasoning is precise and sound. It is not…

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
特場屋之文而已宜為士式
考試官教諭安　批　理明詞雅應是大家氣
象
考試官教諭白　批　寓張子意出
聖人取善而大無我之心所以求天下之治切
矣聖人身任天下非不欲其皆自我而治之也
然力有所窮勢有所阻欲盡如吾意也亦難故
以天下之治而望於天下之善收天下之善而
承以無我之心由是以其善致其治舉皆如吾
===
之所欲而治天下之功盡嗚呼心之虛而事以
實矣張子歷敘堯舜禹湯文王取善之事而以
虛心為天下言之可謂知聖人治天下之道者
與今夫聖人以一身而處天下民物之上其所
以仰視而責望於我者至重且繁也吾茍不為
之所則有以孤彼之望而負吾之責聖人固不
若是恝然也故夫天下之治非天下之善無以
為而天下之善非吾心之虛無以受是以操無
我之心以為取善之地則衆人之善皆於我乎
punctuated:
特場屋之文而已，宜為士式。
考試官教諭安批：理明詞雅，應是大家氣象。
考試官教諭白批：寓張子意出。
聖人取善而大無我之心，所以求天下之治切矣。聖人身任天下，非不欲其皆自我而治之也。然力有所窮，勢有所阻，欲盡如吾意也亦難。故以天下之治而望於天下之善，收天下之善而承以無我之心。由是以其善致其治，舉皆如吾之所欲，而治天下之功盡。嗚呼！心之虛而事以實矣。張子歷敘堯舜禹湯文王取善之事，而以虛心為天下言之，可謂知聖人治天下之道者與！今夫聖人以一身而處天下民物之上，其所以仰視而責望於我者至重且繁也。吾茍不為之所，則有以孤彼之望而負吾之責。聖人固不若是恝然也。故夫天下之治，非天下之善無以為；而天下之善，非吾心之虛無以受。是以操無我之心以為取善之地，則衆人之善皆於我乎
translation_en:
…merely a composition for the examination hall; it deserves to serve as a model for scholars.
Examiner An, Instructor, comments: “The principles are clear and the language elegant: this surely has the bearing of a great master.”
Examiner Bai, Instructor, comments: “It brings out Master Zhang’s meaning [?].”
The sage adopts what is good in others and enlarges his selfless mind: earnest indeed is his pursuit of good government throughout the realm. Taking responsibility for the realm upon himself, the sage certainly wishes to bring order to it entirely through his own efforts. Yet his strength has limits, and circumstances present obstacles; it is difficult to have everything accord with his intentions. Thus, for the governance of the realm, he looks to the goodness found throughout it, gathering that goodness and receiving it with a selfless mind. Through that goodness he achieves good government, so that everything accords with his wishes and the work of governing the realm is fully accomplished. Ah! Through the mind’s emptiness, affairs attain substance. Master Zhang recounts in turn how Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, and King Wen adopted what was good in others, and speaks of this as emptying the mind for the sake of the realm. May he not be called one who understood the sages’ way of governing the realm?
Now the sage, a single person, occupies a position above all the people and things of the realm. The expectations and demands of those who look up to him are exceedingly weighty and numerous. If I fail to make proper provision for them, I will disappoint their hopes and fail in my responsibilities. The sage certainly is not so indifferent. Thus the realm cannot be governed without the goodness found throughout it, and that goodness cannot be received unless my mind is empty. Therefore, by maintaining a selfless mind as the ground for adopting what is good in others, all the goodness of the multitude will, in me…

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
集舉而求之治綽綽乎有餘用矣何政之不立
而何治之不成不然訑訑氣象者且將拒人于千
里而善不得聞矣如天下何故易之咸曰君子
以虛受人夫咸山澤之卦也山澤以氣相通而
不以形相礙故取受人之義而得感物之理焉
然則聖人所以感天下之善而成之治顧有外
於心之虛哉噫虛心未易言也湛而無所有謂
之虛靜而無所擾謂之虛廣而無所不受畢而
無所不承謂之虛一有所係吝焉則隘而非虛
===
矣一有所牽制焉則偏而非虛矣一有所猶豫
而未定矯飾而未誠則蔽而非虛矣聖人之心
何心哉有受益之謙而無招損之滿有用人之
入而無自用之小有下人之慮而無上人之思
其澄於中者無所不容而納於外者無所不受
是故稽衆舍己堯之心虛於稽之舍之之時而
欽明文思不自恃也與人為善舜之心虛於與
之為之之際而濬哲文明不自足也以至聞善
則拜禹之改過不聞不諫而亦式亦入又禹湯
punctuated: 集，舉而求之治，綽綽乎有餘用矣。何政之不立，而何治之不成？不然，訑訑氣象者，且將拒人于千里，而善不得聞矣，如天下何？故《易》之《咸》曰：「君子以虛受人。」夫咸，山澤之卦也。山澤以氣相通，而不以形相礙，故取受人之義，而得感物之理焉。然則聖人所以感天下之善而成之治，顧有外於心之虛哉？噫！虛心未易言也。湛而無所有謂之虛，靜而無所擾謂之虛，廣而無所不受，畢而無所不承謂之虛。一有所係吝焉，則隘而非虛矣；一有所牽制焉，則偏而非虛矣；一有所猶豫而未定，矯飾而未誠，則蔽而非虛矣。聖人之心何心哉？有受益之謙，而無招損之滿；有用人之入，而無自用之小；有下人之慮，而無上人之思。其澄於中者，無所不容，而納於外者，無所不受。是故稽衆舍己，堯之心虛於稽之舍之之時，而欽明文思不自恃也；與人為善，舜之心虛於與之為之之際，而濬哲文明不自足也。以至聞善則拜，禹之改過，不聞不諫，而亦式亦入，又禹湯
translation_en:
…gather together. Bringing all this goodness to bear in seeking good government, one has more than enough for the task. What policy could fail to be established, and what good order could fail to be achieved? Otherwise, an air of smug self-satisfaction will keep others a thousand li away, and good counsel will go unheard. What then can be done for the world? Thus the Xian hexagram of the Book of Changes says: “The noble man receives others with an open mind.” Xian is the hexagram of mountain and lake. Mountain and lake communicate through their vital energies, without their physical forms obstructing one another. Hence it conveys the meaning of receiving others and embodies the principle of responding to things. Can the means by which the sage draws forth the goodness of the world and brings it to fruition in government lie anywhere beyond openness of mind?

Ah! Openness of mind is not easily spoken of. To be clear and hold nothing within is called openness; to be still and undisturbed is called openness; to be broad enough to receive everything, and comprehensive enough to embrace everything [?], is called openness. Once there is any attachment or reluctance to let go, the mind is confined rather than open. Once anything constrains it, it is partial rather than open. Once there is hesitation without resolution, or affectation without sincerity, it is obscured rather than open. What sort of mind does the sage possess? He has the humility that brings benefit, without the fullness of pride that invites loss; he has the receptiveness that comes from employing others [?], without the narrowness of relying solely on himself. He thinks of placing himself below others, without thinking of placing himself above them. In his inward clarity, there is nothing he cannot accommodate; in admitting what comes from outside, there is nothing he cannot receive.

Thus, in consulting the many and setting aside his own views, Yao’s mind was open at the very moment of consulting and relinquishing; he did not rely complacently on his reverence, intelligence, refinement, and thoughtfulness. In joining others in doing good, Shun’s mind was open at the very moment of joining and acting; he did not rest content with his profound wisdom and luminous cultivation. Further, there was bowing upon hearing good counsel, Yu’s correcting his faults [?], and leaving nothing unheard and no remonstrance unoffered, both following counsel and accepting it [?]; and further, Yu and Tang…

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
文王之心之虛不以勤儉既克聖武既昭徽柔
既成而無復望於人也然取善雖在於吾心而
其所以取之之意實為夫天下故堯以所稽之
善而治夫唐則所以同事登庸者不獨岳牧之
屬矣舜以所與之善而治夫虞則所以同熙帝
載者不獨元凱之輩矣禹湯文王以所拜所用
與夫所聞入之善而治夫夏商周則所以同亮
天工者又不專咸事之九德戮力之元聖巳知
巳見之宅俊而巳自九族之睦以至庶績之熙
===
堯皆以取諸人者而為之也自璿衡之齊以至
山川之定舜皆以取諸人者而治之也自九功
以至六府自修紀以至殖民自修和以至篤祜
禹湯文王又皆以取諸人者而經理之也天下
之事皆衆人聰明之所運天下之治皆衆善積
累之所成是故有萬邦協和黎民於變之治焉
是故有四方風動黎民敏德之治焉是故有文
命四敷邦家輯寧西土怙冐之治焉天下之所
當為者無不成而吾心之所欲為者無不遂至
punctuated: 文王之心之虛，不以勤儉既克、聖武既昭、徽柔既成，而無復望於人也。然取善雖在於吾心，而其所以取之之意，實為夫天下。故堯以所稽之善而治夫唐，則所以同事登庸者，不獨岳牧之屬矣；舜以所與之善而治夫虞，則所以同熙帝載者，不獨元凱之輩矣；禹、湯、文王以所拜、所用與夫所聞入之善而治夫夏、商、周，則所以同亮天工者，又不專咸事之九德、戮力之元聖、巳知巳見之宅俊而巳。自九族之睦以至庶績之熙，堯皆以取諸人者而為之也；自璿衡之齊以至山川之定，舜皆以取諸人者而治之也；自九功以至六府，自修紀以至殖民，自修和以至篤祜，禹、湯、文王又皆以取諸人者而經理之也。天下之事，皆衆人聰明之所運；天下之治，皆衆善積累之所成。是故有萬邦協和、黎民於變之治焉；是故有四方風動、黎民敏德之治焉；是故有文命四敷、邦家輯寧、西土怙冐之治焉。天下之所當為者無不成，而吾心之所欲為者無不遂。至
translation_en:
…and King Wen’s openness of mind: they did not cease to look to others merely because diligence and frugality had already been achieved, sagely martial prowess had already been displayed, and gracious gentleness had already been perfected. Although adopting what is good depends upon one’s own mind, the purpose of adopting it is truly to benefit all under Heaven. Thus, when Yao governed Tang through the good he had sought out, those raised to office to work alongside him were not confined to the chiefs of the sacred peaks and regional governors. When Shun governed Yu through the good he shared with others, those who joined him in bringing the sovereign’s undertakings to fruition were not confined to the Eight Worthies and Eight Talents. When Yu, Tang, and King Wen governed Xia, Shang, and Zhou through the good before which they bowed, which they employed, and which they heard and accepted, those who joined them in assisting Heaven’s work were likewise not confined to men possessing the nine virtues who served together, the great sage who exerted himself to the utmost, or the eminent men established in office whom the ruler already knew and had observed [?].

From bringing harmony to the nine degrees of kinship to making every undertaking flourish, Yao accomplished everything through what he drew from others. From making observations with the jade celestial instrument and sighting tube to determining the mountains and rivers, Shun ordered everything through what he drew from others. From the nine achievements to the six resources, from setting the guiding principles in order to fostering the people’s growth, and from cultivating harmony to securing abundant blessings, Yu, Tang, and King Wen likewise managed everything through what they drew from others. The affairs of all under Heaven are carried forward by the intelligence of many; good government throughout the world is achieved by the accumulation of many kinds of goodness. Thus there was government under which the myriad states were brought into concord and the common people were transformed. Thus there was government whose influence moved the four quarters like the wind and under which the common people strove earnestly toward virtue. Thus there was government under which civil instruction spread to the four quarters, states and households enjoyed concord and peace, and the western lands found protection and shelter. Nothing that ought to be done in the world remained unaccomplished, and nothing that one’s own mind wished to do remained unfulfilled. Upon reaching…

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
是則堯可以不憂舜可以無為而禹也湯也文
王也可以告成可以垂裕可以觀成矣治天下
之實何莫不本於虛心致哉後之人主寛仁大
度如漢高似矣而溺冠嫚罵之心則不肯虛止
輦受言如文帝似矣而禮樂謙讓之心則不能
虛以人為鑑如太宗亦幾矣而漸不克終之心
則不久虛三君且然他尚何望焉宜乎治之不
古若也張子叙聖人取善而賛之為為天下之
虛心可謂能知聖人而善言治道者矣雖然取
===
善在於虛心而心之虛否則又係德之純疵也
德或不純則有勉強而不能從背馳而不肯從
者矣此虛心所以獨歸群聖而其他不與也故
曰純心要矣是取善以虛心為先虛心又以純
心為本
表
擬宋崇政殿說書趙師民獻勸講箴表慶
曆四年
劉東
punctuated:
是則堯可以不憂，舜可以無為，而禹也、湯也、文王也，可以告成，可以垂裕，可以觀成矣。治天下之實，何莫不本於虛心致哉？後之人主，寛仁大度如漢高似矣，而溺冠嫚罵之心則不肯虛；止輦受言如文帝似矣，而禮樂謙讓之心則不能虛；以人為鑑如太宗亦幾矣，而漸不克終之心則不久虛。三君且然，他尚何望焉？宜乎治之不古若也。張子叙聖人取善，而賛之為「為天下之虛心」，可謂能知聖人而善言治道者矣。雖然，取善在於虛心，而心之虛否，則又係德之純疵也。德或不純，則有勉強而不能從、背馳而不肯從者矣。此虛心所以獨歸群聖，而其他不與也。故曰：「純心要矣。」是取善以虛心為先，虛心又以純心為本。

表

擬宋崇政殿說書趙師民獻勸講箴表，慶曆四年。

劉東
translation_en:
…at this point, Yao could be free of care, Shun could govern without action, and Yu, Tang, and King Wen could announce their accomplishments, leave a rich legacy to posterity, and behold the fruition of their work. How could the actual achievements of governing the realm fail to be rooted in an open mind [?]?

Among later rulers, Gaozu of Han, with his generosity and magnanimity, seemed to approach this ideal; yet the disposition that led him to urinate in a scholar’s cap and hurl insults would not open itself to others. Emperor Wen, who stopped his carriage to receive advice, seemed to approach it; yet in matters of ritual, music, and deferential yielding, his mind could not remain open. Taizong, who took other people as his mirror, also came close; yet as he gradually failed to carry through to the end, his mind did not remain open for long. If even these three rulers were like this, what could one hope for from the others? It is no wonder that their government fell short of antiquity’s.

Master Zhang described how the sages adopted what was good in others and praised this as “keeping an open mind for the sake of all under Heaven.” He may indeed be said to have understood the sages and spoken well about the Way of government. Nevertheless, adopting what is good depends on an open mind, while whether the mind is open depends in turn on the purity or imperfection of one’s virtue. If virtue is not pure, some will strive but prove unable to follow what is good, while others will turn away and refuse to follow it. This is why openness of mind belongs exclusively to the sages, and others have no share in it. Thus it is said: “Purity of mind is essential.” Adopting what is good therefore requires openness of mind first; openness of mind, in turn, is founded upon purity of mind.

Memorial

A memorial composed in the voice of Zhao Shimin, Expositor in Chongzheng Hall under the Song, presenting an Admonition Encouraging Lectures, in the fourth year of Qingli [1044].

By Liu Dong.

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
同考試官訓導陳　批〔備述當時上箴之意而〕
〔忠愛宛然非但長於四六而已〕
同考試官教諭鄧　批〔特雖用武不可輟講此〕
〔師氏意也子能道之可為〕
今日緝熙之一助
考試官教諭安　批〔詞婉意詳非專事駢麗〕
〔者〕
考試官教諭白　批〔典麗中寓剴切得古君〕
〔體〕
===
慶曆四年某月日崇政殿說書臣趙師民
謹以所撰勸講箴上
獻者伏以
瑞應奎纏
昭代闡賁文之化道崇
宸極聖王敏乾健之功政貴不迷學乃有獲敢
效盤銘之警用陳
黼扆之規臣師民誠惶誠恐稽首頓首上言
竊惟帝王之學與韋布不同文武之猷惟
punctuated:
同考試官訓導陳，批〔備述當時上箴之意，而〕〔忠愛宛然，非但長於四六而已。〕
同考試官教諭鄧，批〔特雖用武，不可輟講，此〕〔師氏意也。子能道之，可為〕今日緝熙之一助。
考試官教諭安，批〔詞婉意詳，非專事駢麗〕〔者。〕
考試官教諭白，批〔典麗中寓剴切，得古君〕〔體。〕
慶曆四年某月日，崇政殿說書臣趙師民，謹以所撰《勸講箴》上獻者。伏以瑞應奎纏，昭代闡賁文之化；道崇宸極，聖王敏乾健之功。政貴不迷，學乃有獲。敢效盤銘之警，用陳黼扆之規。臣師民誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首上言：竊惟帝王之學，與韋布不同；文武之猷，惟
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Chen, Assistant Instructor, comments: “This fully recounts the intent behind submitting the admonition at that time, vividly conveying loyalty and devotion. Its merit is not merely skill in four-and-six-character parallel prose.”
Associate Examiner Deng, Instructor, comments: “In particular [?], even when employing military force, lectures must not cease: this was Master Zhao’s intention. Your ability to express it can contribute to the continued cultivation of luminous virtue today.”
Examiner An, Instructor, comments: “The phrasing is graceful and the meaning fully developed; this does not merely pursue ornate parallelism.”
Examiner Bai, Instructor, comments: “Within its classical elegance lies pointed admonition; it captures the manner of ancient rulers [?].”
On a certain day of a certain month in the fourth year of Qingli [1044], your servant Zhao Shimin, Expositor in Chongzheng Hall, respectfully submits the Admonition to Encourage Lectures that he has composed.
I humbly consider that auspicious signs answer in the celestial domain of Kui, the constellation of literary culture, and this illustrious age spreads the transforming influence of refined learning. The Way is exalted at the imperial pole, and the sage king diligently pursues the vigorous activity of Heaven. In government, what matters is not to go astray; through learning, one gains understanding. I venture to emulate the warning inscribed upon the basin and thus present an admonition before the imperial throne. Your servant Shimin, in utmost fear and trembling, bows his head to the ground and prostrates himself, submitting these words:
I humbly reflect that the learning of emperors and kings differs from that of common scholars clad in plain cloth. The plans of Kings Wen and Wu are only …

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
典章攸載盖将求夫實用匪直玩乎空文
雖事戒不虞允協師貞之吉而志存無逸
寧忘畜德之新粤考前聞率由古訓苗夷
七旬之格寔本數文荆旅三載之征不違
典學減開豐水用昭不顯之純馬散華山
肇訪惟皇之極自時厥後亦有可稱藝講
石渠竟起北夷之慕經横虎觀何妨西域
之勲或搆藻思于轅門或覽瑶編于帷幄
威加遼海館中之緗帙頻開兵入蔡城屏
===
上之皇墳未撤惟學可以懋敬厥德非書
無以維持此心式典之勤屢聞自昔
講筵之創僅見于今於皇
太祖之肇基有赫
二宗之繼統
神功掀揭載揚蜀漢之師
聖翰昭回爰製孔顏之賛
殿臨講武俊乂盈庭館啓崇文圖書充棟開
卷樂三編之益揮戈成四克之功
punctuated:
典章攸載，盖将求夫實用，匪直玩乎空文。雖事戒不虞，允協師貞之吉，而志存無逸，寧忘畜德之新？粤考前聞，率由古訓。苗夷七旬之格，寔本數文；荆旅三載之征，不違典學。減開豐水，用昭不顯之純；馬散華山，肇訪惟皇之極。自時厥後，亦有可稱。藝講石渠，竟起北夷之慕；經横虎觀，何妨西域之勲？或搆藻思于轅門，或覽瑶編于帷幄。威加遼海，館中之緗帙頻開；兵入蔡城，屏上之皇墳未撤。惟學可以懋敬厥德，非書無以維持此心。式典之勤，屢聞自昔；講筵之創，僅見于今。
於皇太祖之肇基，有赫二宗之繼統！神功掀揭，載揚蜀漢之師；聖翰昭回，爰製孔顏之賛。殿臨講武，俊乂盈庭；館啓崇文，圖書充棟。開卷樂三編之益，揮戈成四克之功。
translation_en:
…recorded in the statutes and institutions. The purpose is to seek their practical application, not merely to delight in empty words. Though precautions against unforeseen dangers accord fully with the auspiciousness of an army steadfast in rectitude, when one’s resolve is set upon avoiding ease, how could one forget to renew one’s accumulated virtue? Examining what has been handed down from earlier times, we find adherence throughout to ancient teachings. The submission of the Miao after seventy days was truly rooted in “enumerating civil accomplishments” [?]; the three-year campaign against Jing did not depart from the learning of the classics. The opening at the Feng River [?] manifested the purity of hidden virtue; the horses were released on Mount Hua, and inquiry began into the sovereign’s supreme norm.
Thereafter, too, there were achievements worthy of praise. Discussion of the classical arts in the Shiqu Pavilion ultimately stirred the admiration of the northern peoples; how did the exposition of the classics at the Tiger Observatory impede achievements in the Western Regions? Some composed elegant writings at the gates of military camps; others read precious books within the command tent. While imperial might extended to the Liaohai region, the pale-yellow book wrappers in the hall were frequently opened; when troops entered the city of Cai, the writings of the ancient sovereigns displayed on the screen had not been removed. Only learning can strengthen reverent attention to one’s virtue; without books, there is no means of sustaining this mind. Diligent adherence to the classics has often been reported since antiquity; the establishment of court lectures is seen only in the present age.
How august was Taizu’s founding of the dynasty, and how illustrious the succession of the two ancestral emperors! Their divine achievements shook the world, gloriously advancing armies into Shu and Han; their sagely writings shone forth, producing eulogies of Confucius and Yan Hui. They presided in the palace over instruction in martial affairs, with outstanding men filling the court; halls were opened to honor civil learning, with books filling the buildings. Opening their books, they delighted in the benefits of the three compilations [?]; wielding their weapons, they accomplished four victories.

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
法駕御北城氣褫驕虜直廬設
秘閣論集醇儒
燕翼有貽
鴻謨具在恭惟
○○○○
鳳姿純懿
龍德正中
聖養蒙泉
命凝鼎位辟雍首
===
幸時甫及乎冲年崇政
躬臨學無間于隻日設諸科以取士吉協泰
征建二閣以親賢禮隆晉接顧咸寧之世
乃遺宗膾之憂而明德之君未免混夷之
慍蠢茲元昊犯我環州肆蠆毒于邉陲馳
羽書于
魏闕雖仁人無敵尚軫
當宁之憂而
王師有征暫輟
punctuated: 法駕御北城，氣褫驕虜；直廬設秘閣，論集醇儒。燕翼有貽，鴻謨具在。恭惟○○○○，鳳姿純懿，龍德正中。聖養蒙泉，命凝鼎位。辟雍首幸，時甫及乎冲年；崇政躬臨，學無間于隻日。設諸科以取士，吉協泰征；建二閣以親賢，禮隆晉接。顧咸寧之世，乃遺宗膾之憂；而明德之君，未免混夷之慍。蠢茲元昊，犯我環州，肆蠆毒于邉陲，馳羽書于魏闕。雖仁人無敵，尚軫當宁之憂；而王師有征，暫輟
translation_en: …The imperial carriage proceeded to the northern city, its imposing presence robbing the arrogant enemy of courage; duty quarters were established in the Palace Library, and learned discussions brought together scholars of pure Confucian learning. Provision was bequeathed for future generations, and the grand designs remain fully intact. Reverently we consider ○○○○: your phoenix-like bearing is pure and admirable; your dragon-like virtue is upright and centered. Your sagely character was nurtured like a spring emerging at the foot of a mountain; Heaven’s mandate settled firmly upon your imperial throne. When you first visited the Biyong, the imperial academy, you had only just reached tender youth; you attended Chongzheng Hall in person, never omitting study on the odd-numbered days. You established the various examination categories to recruit scholars, auspiciously according with the favorable portent of advance in the hexagram Tai, “Peace”; you founded the two pavilions to draw worthy men close, honoring them with the generous reception evoked by the hexagram Jin, “Advance.” Yet an age when all enjoyed tranquility still left the anxiety of “zongkuai” [?]; and a ruler of illustrious virtue could not escape vexation at the Hunyi barbarians. This unruly Yuanhao invaded our Huanzhou, unleashing his scorpion’s venom upon the frontier and sending feather-marked urgent dispatches speeding to the palace gates. Although a humane ruler has no enemy who can withstand him, the sovereign was still burdened with concern; and when the royal army went on campaign, you temporarily suspended…

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
臨筵之講先王之典似徒善于守成儒者之
謀亦何功于進取臣師民高陽末學幸覩
上國之光東武下僚濫預西垣之選力未勞
于汗馬心有愧于濡鵜數事之敷已塵
睿覽一得之獻少罄愚衷慚非周士之嘉謀竊
擬唐人之大寶彰禮施樂聿弘經世之圖
明舊知新庸作脩身之矩伏願
比弦韋於座右殷鑒常懸
采葑菲於屏間周書並列
===
嚴惟丕式重光景祐之遺規
學有緝熙復覩崇文之曠典勿以
清朝小警遂忘稽古之功無謂
紫禁深居可忽右文之志
明良協一德之休
政教成九功之叙
紬繙晝啓瀲芳潤於群經博帶雲從析精微
於衆論功恒繼於
乙夜志匪懈於十寒
punctuated:
臨筵之講。先王之典，似徒善于守成；儒者之謀，亦何功于進取？臣師民，高陽末學，幸覩上國之光；東武下僚，濫預西垣之選。力未勞于汗馬，心有愧于濡鵜。數事之敷，已塵睿覽；一得之獻，少罄愚衷。慚非周士之嘉謀，竊擬唐人之大寶。彰禮施樂，聿弘經世之圖；明舊知新，庸作脩身之矩。伏願比弦韋於座右，殷鑒常懸；采葑菲於屏間，周書並列。
嚴惟丕式，重光景祐之遺規；學有緝熙，復覩崇文之曠典。勿以清朝小警，遂忘稽古之功；無謂紫禁深居，可忽右文之志。明良協一德之休，政教成九功之叙。紬繙晝啓，瀲芳潤於群經；博帶雲從，析精微於衆論。功恒繼於乙夜，志匪懈於十寒。
translation_en:
…the lectures delivered in the imperial presence. The institutions of the former kings seem useful only for preserving established rule; what contribution, then, can scholars’ counsels make toward advancing its achievements?
Your servant Shimin, an unworthy student from Gaoyang, has been fortunate to behold the splendor of the imperial capital. A lowly official from Dongwu, I have undeservedly been selected for service in the Western Secretariat. I have performed no arduous service amid the sweat of warhorses, and feel the shame of the pelican that wets its wings without catching fish—holding office without earning its rewards. My exposition of several matters has already intruded upon Your Majesty’s discerning gaze; in presenting this one modest insight, I give some expression to my humble devotion. Ashamed that mine is no excellent counsel such as that of the men of Zhou, I venture to emulate the Tang writer’s “Great Treasure.” By honoring ritual and putting music into practice, may the design for ordering the world be enlarged; by understanding the old and knowing the new, may a standard for cultivating oneself be established.
I humbly hope that You will keep this beside Your seat, like bowstring and leather serving as admonitions, with the warning afforded by Yin constantly before You; and that You will accept its humble offerings, like turnips and radishes, placing it upon a screen alongside the Documents of Zhou.
Reverently taking the great model as Your rule [?], renew the brilliance of the precedents bequeathed by the Jingyou era. Through learning that advances toward ever greater illumination, let the exceptional institutions for honoring culture be seen again. Do not, because of a minor alarm in this enlightened reign, forget the work of investigating antiquity. Do not suppose that dwelling deep within the Forbidden Palace permits neglect of the resolve to esteem letters. May an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers share the excellence of a single virtue, and may government and instruction bring the nine achievements into due order.
Let the books be opened and examined by day, drawing fragrant nourishment from all the Classics. Let scholars in broad sashes gather like clouds, analyzing the subtle and profound points in their many discussions. May this effort continue into the second watch of the night, and may Your resolve never slacken through prolonged spells of cold.…

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
王猷允塞載歌江漢之章
帝德罔愆永致鳬鷖之頌臣無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉表隨
獻以
聞
第叄場
策
第一問
曹卿
===
同考試官教諭秦　批　天人之際必以類應而
不可以象求也此篇據洪範以斷漢儒互錯且
於我
皇祖交脩之訓及
今日弭災之實敷揚詳盡非特文辭之工而已是用錄之
考試官教諭安　批　此卷五策具見學識首
篇允能揚厲
聖謨且紆徐曲折千餘言悉據故實無一僻語東省之學者固

第叄場
策
第一問
曹卿
同考試官教諭秦批：天人之際，必以類應，而不可以象求也。此篇據《洪範》以斷漢儒互錯，且於我皇祖交脩之訓及今日弭災之實，敷揚詳盡，非特文辭之工而已，是用錄之。

translation_en:
…The royal way is fully realized: again we sing the verses of “The Jiang and Han Rivers.” Imperial virtue is without fault: forever we offer the praise of “Wild Ducks and Gulls.” Your servant, gazing toward Heaven and looking up to Your Sagely Majesty, cannot contain his fervent emotion and reverent trembling. I respectfully submit this memorial with the presentation for Your Majesty’s hearing.
Third Session
Policy Essays
First Question
Cao Qing
Associate Examiner Qin, Instructor, comments: “In the relationship between Heaven and humanity, responses must occur according to kind; they cannot be sought through outward signs. This essay draws on the ‘Great Plan’ to adjudicate the conflicting errors of Han Confucian scholars. Moreover, it expounds fully and in detail both our imperial ancestor’s injunction that ruler and ministers jointly cultivate themselves and the practical measures taken today to avert calamities.
