title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
有如此也夫
考試官教諭白　批　言天必以理格天必以
實良有見也丑
上下交脩之意條荅詳明未復舉經訓
獻可為
當宁格天之一助
善言天者不惟其數惟其理善格天者不
惟其文惟其實以理言天則天道罔不明
以實應天則天變罔不弭故專泥於數而
===
不究乎理不足以言天徒事其文而不本
乎實不足以格天夫天人相與之際甚可
畏也人事感於下則天變應於上其理固
然而何象類之求然災變雖出於天而所
以消弭之則在於人故為君者必惟實德
是脩以戒其臣為臣者亦惟實德是脩以
警其君則天心克享而天災自弭矣不然
雖日勤于祝幣史詞何益乎禹謨曰惠迪
吉從逆凶惟影響伊訓曰作善降之百祥
punctuated:
有如此也夫！

考試官教諭白，批：言天必以理，格天必以實，良有見也。丑上下交脩之意，條荅詳明，未復舉經訓，獻可為當宁格天之一助。

善言天者，不惟其數，惟其理；善格天者，不惟其文，惟其實。以理言天，則天道罔不明；以實應天，則天變罔不弭。故專泥於數而不究乎理，不足以言天；徒事其文而不本乎實，不足以格天。夫天人相與之際，甚可畏也。人事感於下，則天變應於上，其理固然，而何象類之求？然災變雖出於天，而所以消弭之則在於人。故為君者必惟實德是脩，以戒其臣；為臣者亦惟實德是脩，以警其君，則天心克享，而天災自弭矣。不然，雖日勤于祝幣史詞，何益乎？《禹謨》曰：「惠迪吉，從逆凶，惟影響。」《伊訓》曰：「作善，降之百祥，
translation_en:
…indeed include men such as this!

Comment by Examiner Bai, an Instructor: To speak of Heaven, one must proceed through principle; to move Heaven, one must proceed through substance. This is truly perceptive. The meaning of mutual cultivation by those above and below is addressed point by point, clearly and in detail [?]. Scriptural teachings are further adduced [?], an offering that may help the reigning emperor move Heaven.

Those who speak well of Heaven attend not merely to its numerical patterns but to its principles; those who know how to move Heaven attend not merely to outward forms but to substance. When Heaven is discussed through principle, nothing in the Way of Heaven remains obscure. When Heaven is answered with substance, no anomalous celestial manifestation remains unappeased. Thus, to cling exclusively to numerical patterns without investigating principle is insufficient for speaking of Heaven; merely to pursue outward forms without grounding them in substance is insufficient for moving Heaven. The interaction between Heaven and humanity is indeed deeply awe-inspiring. When human affairs exert an influence below, anomalous celestial manifestations respond above. This is inherently how the principle operates: why seek correspondences of images and categories? Yet although disasters and anomalies originate in Heaven, the means of dispelling them lie with human beings. Thus, the ruler must cultivate substantive virtue alone, thereby admonishing his ministers; ministers likewise must cultivate substantive virtue alone, thereby cautioning their ruler. Then Heaven’s heart can be won over, and Heaven-sent disasters will subside of themselves. Otherwise, even daily diligence in prayers, offerings of silk, and invocations by scribes would be of what benefit? The Counsels of Yu says: “Following the right way brings good fortune; following the contrary brings misfortune—as surely as shadow and echo.” The Instructions of Yi says: “For doing good, a hundred blessings are sent down …

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
作不善降之百殃至論休咎之徵則莫詳
于洪範昔箕子陳洪範皇極于武王先以
五行次以五事而及於庶徵其曰五行則
水火木金土是也其曰五事則貌言視聽
思是也在天為五行在人為五事五事修
有休徵焉曰肅時雨若曰乂時暘若曰哲
時燠若曰謀時寒若曰聖時風若以類而
應矣五事失有咎徵焉曰狂恒雨若曰僭
恒暘若曰豫恒燠若曰急恒寒若曰蒙恒
風若亦以類而應矣是以人而徵諸天推
天而合諸人其理則然不可以象類求也
迨漢伏勝劉向及其子歆乃集上古以來
春秋六國至秦漢符瑞災異之說推迹行
事比類相從名為洪範五行傳有曰田獵
不宿則木不曲直棄法律則火不炎上修
宮室則稼穡不成好戰攻則金不從革簡
宗廟則水不潤下有曰貌之不恭是謂不
肅厥咎狂厥罰恒雨厥極惡言之不從是
punctuated:
作不善，降之百殃。」至論休咎之徵，則莫詳于《洪範》。昔箕子陳《洪範》皇極于武王，先以五行，次以五事，而及於庶徵。其曰五行，則水火木金土是也；其曰五事，則貌言視聽思是也。在天為五行，在人為五事。五事修，有休徵焉，曰「肅，時雨若」，曰「乂，時暘若」，曰「哲，時燠若」，曰「謀，時寒若」，曰「聖，時風若」，以類而應矣。五事失，有咎徵焉，曰「狂，恒雨若」，曰「僭，恒暘若」，曰「豫，恒燠若」，曰「急，恒寒若」，曰「蒙，恒風若」，亦以類而應矣。是以人而徵諸天，推天而合諸人，其理則然，不可以象類求也。
迨漢伏勝、劉向及其子歆，乃集上古以來春秋、六國至秦漢符瑞災異之說，推迹行事，比類相從，名為《洪範五行傳》。有曰：「田獵不宿，則木不曲直；棄法律，則火不炎上；修宮室，則稼穡不成；好戰攻，則金不從革；簡宗廟，則水不潤下。」有曰：「貌之不恭，是謂不肅，厥咎狂，厥罰恒雨，厥極惡。言之不從，是
translation_en:
…when one does evil, a hundred calamities descend upon one.” As for discussing the signs of good and ill fortune, none treats them more fully than the Great Plan (Hongfan). In antiquity, when Jizi expounded the Great Plan’s royal standard to King Wu, he began with the Five Phases, proceeded to the Five Activities, and then reached the Various Signs. What it calls the Five Phases are water, fire, wood, metal, and earth; what it calls the Five Activities are demeanor, speech, sight, hearing, and thought. In Heaven these are the Five Phases; in human beings they are the Five Activities. When the Five Activities are cultivated, there are auspicious signs: “Reverence: timely rain follows”; “Orderliness: timely sunshine follows”; “Discernment: timely warmth follows”; “Deliberation: timely cold follows”; “Sagacity: timely wind follows.” They respond according to their respective kinds. When the Five Activities go astray, there are inauspicious signs: “Wildness: incessant rain follows”; “Overstepping: incessant sunshine follows”; “Indolence: incessant warmth follows”; “Impetuosity: incessant cold follows”; “Benightedness: incessant wind follows.” These too respond according to their respective kinds. Thus one takes human conduct and seeks its verification in Heaven, and reasons from Heaven to find its correspondence in human affairs. Such is the principle, but it cannot be sought through resemblances between phenomena.
By the Han dynasty, Fu Sheng, Liu Xiang, and the latter’s son Xin gathered accounts of auspicious tokens and disastrous anomalies from high antiquity onward, through the Spring and Autumn period and the Six States, down to the Qin and Han. They traced events and actions, grouping together those of similar kinds, and called this the Commentary on the Five Phases of the Great Plan (Hongfan wuxing zhuan). One passage says: “If one hunts without lodging overnight [?], wood will fail to bend and straighten; if one abandons laws and statutes, fire will fail to blaze upward; if one builds palaces and chambers, crops will fail to ripen; if one delights in warfare and attack, metal will fail to yield to reshaping; if one neglects the ancestral temple, water will fail to moisten and descend.” Another says: “When demeanor is not respectful, this is called a lack of reverence. Its fault is wildness; its punishment is incessant rain; its ultimate calamity is ugliness. When speech is not compliant, this…”

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
謂不乂厥咎僭厥罰恒暘厥極憂視之不
明是謂不哲厥咎舒厥罰恒燠厥極疾聽
之不聰是謂不謀厥咎急厥罰恒寒厥極
貧思之不睿是謂不聖厥咎霿厥罰恒風
厥極凶短折又以福極配五行以弱配皇
之不極夫箕子推衍洪範庶徵之疇蓋以
驗之肅乂哲謀聖一出於五事事之貌言
視聽思一出於五行固各有攸當也漢儒
必曰某事得則某事應某五行之旨哉五
===
行含羅九疇者也五事檢御五行者也皇
極裁節五事者也漢儒强以福極配五行
果皇極之旨哉孔子脩春秋紀災異而不
著事應意以天道遠而難知人事近而當
脩若推其事應則有合有不合有同有不
同至於不合不同則使君子怠焉以為偶
然而不懼矣盖慎之也漢儒皆以春秋為
學必著其事應以文之至其不合而自相
背戾又豈聖人脩春秋之意哉旁引曲取
punctuated:
謂不乂，厥咎僭，厥罰恒暘，厥極憂；視之不明，是謂不哲，厥咎舒，厥罰恒燠，厥極疾；聽之不聰，是謂不謀，厥咎急，厥罰恒寒，厥極貧；思之不睿，是謂不聖，厥咎霿，厥罰恒風，厥極凶短折。又以福極配五行，以弱配皇之不極。
夫箕子推衍《洪範》庶徵之疇，蓋以驗之。肅、乂、哲、謀、聖，一出於五事；事之貌、言、視、聽、思，一出於五行，固各有攸當也。漢儒必曰「某事得則某事應」，某五行之旨哉？五行含羅九疇者也，五事檢御五行者也，皇極裁節五事者也。漢儒强以福極配五行，果皇極之旨哉？
孔子脩《春秋》，紀災異而不著事應，意以天道遠而難知，人事近而當脩。若推其事應，則有合有不合，有同有不同。至於不合不同，則使君子怠焉，以為偶然而不懼矣。盖慎之也。漢儒皆以《春秋》為學，必著其事應以文之。至其不合而自相背戾，又豈聖人脩《春秋》之意哉？旁引曲取
translation_en:
…is called a failure of order; its fault is overstepping, its punishment constant sunshine, and its ultimate calamity anxiety. Failure to see clearly is called a failure of discernment; its fault is laxity, its punishment constant heat, and its ultimate calamity illness. Failure to hear acutely is called a failure of deliberation; its fault is haste, its punishment constant cold, and its ultimate calamity poverty. Failure to think perceptively is called a failure of sagacity; its fault is confusion, its punishment constant wind, and its ultimate calamity premature death. They also assigned the blessings and ultimate calamities to the Five Phases, and assigned weakness to the sovereign’s failure to establish the utmost standard.
When Jizi elaborated the category of the various signs in the Great Plan (Hongfan), he presumably intended them as means of verification. Reverence, order, discernment, deliberation, and sagacity all issue from the Five Activities; the activities of demeanor, speech, seeing, hearing, and thinking [?] all issue from the Five Phases. Each certainly has its appropriate correspondence. Yet Han scholars insist that “when a particular activity is properly performed, a particular response follows.” Is this [?] the meaning of the Five Phases? The Five Phases encompass the Nine Categories; the Five Activities regulate the Five Phases; and the Sovereign’s Ultimate Standard regulates the Five Activities. When Han scholars forcibly assign the blessings and ultimate calamities to the Five Phases, is this truly the meaning of the Sovereign’s Ultimate Standard?
When Confucius compiled the Spring and Autumn Annals, he recorded calamities and anomalies without specifying the events to which they responded. His intention was presumably that the Way of Heaven is remote and difficult to know, whereas human affairs are close at hand and ought to be put in order. If one deduces the events to which these signs respond, some correspond and others do not; some are alike and others differ. Where they fail to correspond or differ, this will make the gentleman lax: he will regard them as chance occurrences and feel no fear. Confucius was therefore cautious about this. Han scholars all took the Spring and Autumn Annals as the basis of their learning, yet insisted on specifying the events to which the signs responded, thereby embellishing their accounts. When these fail to correspond and contradict one another, how can this be the sage’s intention in compiling the Spring and Autumn Annals? They draw on extraneous citations and adopt strained interpretations…

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
而遷就其說牽合比類而附會其意驗之
於古則鑿而不經推之將來則膠而不應
甚矣其惑也仰惟
太祖高皇帝御極之時命博士許存仁講洪範
休徵咎徵之應因語之曰天人一理必以
類應又曰豈特為人上者當勉為人臣者
亦當脩省以輔其君上下交脩斯為格天
之本盖有以洞見洪範之理矣既而命儒
臣編葺存心錄一書凡帝王之祭祀而有
感於災祥者咸載焉正欲為人君者以天
===
之心為心必六事自責如成湯遇災而懼
如宣王而所以脩德格天者無不至又命
儒臣編葺省躬錄一書凡漢唐宋以來災
祥之應於臣下者咸載焉正欲為人臣者
以君之心為心必如魏相之災異輒聞李
沆之水旱輒奏而所以輔君格天者無不
至豈徒致謹於祭祀之間而已哉惟我
皇上嗣大歷服惟新厥政天下臣民咸有中興
punctuated:
而遷就其說，牽合比類而附會其意，驗之於古則鑿而不經，推之將來則膠而不應。甚矣，其惑也！

仰惟太祖高皇帝御極之時，命博士許存仁講《洪範》休徵、咎徵之應，因語之曰：「天人一理，必以類應。」又曰：「豈特為人上者當勉？為人臣者亦當脩省，以輔其君。上下交脩，斯為格天之本。」盖有以洞見《洪範》之理矣。既而命儒臣編葺《存心錄》一書，凡帝王之祭祀而有感於災祥者，咸載焉。正欲為人君者以天之心為心，必六事自責如成湯，遇災而懼如宣王，而所以脩德格天者無不至。又命儒臣編葺《省躬錄》一書，凡漢唐宋以來災祥之應於臣下者，咸載焉。正欲為人臣者以君之心為心，必如魏相之災異輒聞，李沆之水旱輒奏，而所以輔君格天者無不至。豈徒致謹於祭祀之間而已哉！

惟我皇上嗣大歷服，惟新厥政，天下臣民咸有中興
translation_en:
…and strain matters to accommodate their explanations, forcing comparisons and analogies to make them fit their interpretations. Tested against antiquity, these are contrived and lack sound foundation; applied to the future, they are rigid and fail to correspond to events. How profound their confusion is!

We reverently recall that when Emperor Taizu Gao occupied the throne, he ordered the Erudite Xu Cunren to expound the correspondences of auspicious and baleful signs in the Great Plan (Hongfan). He then told him: “Heaven and humankind share a single principle and necessarily respond to one another according to kind.” He further said: “Is it only those who rule over others who should exert themselves? Those who serve as ministers must also cultivate and examine themselves to assist their ruler. Mutual cultivation by those above and below is the foundation for moving Heaven.” He thus clearly penetrated the principles of the Great Plan. Subsequently, he ordered his scholarly ministers to compile a book, the Record of Preserving the Mind (Cunxin lu), recording all instances in which emperors and kings, in their sacrificial observances, responded to calamities and auspicious signs. His precise intention was that rulers should take Heaven’s heart as their own: they must reproach themselves on the six matters as Cheng Tang did, and feel apprehension upon encountering calamity as King Xuan did, leaving nothing undone in cultivating virtue and moving Heaven. He also ordered his scholarly ministers to compile a book, the Record of Examining Oneself (Xinggong lu), recording all instances from the Han, Tang, and Song onward in which calamities and auspicious signs corresponded to the conduct of ministers. His precise intention was that ministers should take their ruler’s heart as their own: they must emulate Wei Xiang, who invariably reported calamities and anomalies, and Li Hang, who invariably submitted reports of floods and droughts, leaving nothing undone in assisting their ruler to move Heaven. Could this have meant merely exercising care in sacrificial observances?

Our August Sovereign has succeeded to the great imperial mandate and renewed his governance. The ministers and people throughout the realm all have expectations of a restoration…

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
之望焉固宜天人協應而休徵滋至也比
年以來災變相仍近復有
仁壽宮災不知天意果安咎乎意者嘉言尚
攸伏而俊民或未章與三德或未乂而八
政或未用與百工或未時而庶民或未康
與有一於斯皆足以致災而可不警乎要
之天地一大父母也子之於父盖有視於
無形聽於無聲起敬起孝而已安問其怒
之所由乎君之於天盖有保邦未危致治
未亂之德立政而已安問其變之所來乎
===
宵旰之憂以為弭災之助無他焉亦惟逺宗
茲欲紓
箕子五事之疇近守
皇祖交脩之訓以以其所以存心者存心以其所
以省躬者省躬如是而已盖后克艱厥后
臣克艱厥臣繼自今必安厥止必檢厥身
嚴恭寅畏懼荒寧也愼乃儉德戒侈泰也
監于成憲防過愆也始終典學敏進脩也
punctuated:
之望焉。固宜天人協應，而休徵滋至也。比年以來，災變相仍，近復有仁壽宮災。不知天意果安咎乎？意者嘉言尚攸伏，而俊民或未章與？三德或未乂，而八政或未用與？百工或未時，而庶民或未康與？有一於斯，皆足以致災，而可不警乎？要之，天地一大父母也。子之於父，盖有視於無形、聽於無聲，起敬起孝而已，安問其怒之所由乎？君之於天，盖有保邦未危、致治未亂之德立政而已，安問其變之所來乎？
宵旰之憂，以為弭災之助，無他焉，亦惟逺宗茲欲紓箕子五事之疇，近守皇祖交脩之訓，以以其所以存心者存心，以其所以省躬者省躬，如是而已。盖后克艱厥后，臣克艱厥臣。繼自今，必安厥止，必檢厥身。嚴恭寅畏，懼荒寧也；愼乃儉德，戒侈泰也；監于成憲，防過愆也；始終典學，敏進脩也。
translation_en:
…hopes for a restoration. Surely Heaven and humanity ought to respond harmoniously to one another, with auspicious signs arriving in increasing abundance. Yet in recent years calamities and anomalous events have followed one another, and recently there was also a fire at Renshou Palace. We do not know where Heaven truly intends to lay the blame. Might worthy counsel still lie hidden, and outstanding men remain unrecognized? Might the Three Virtues not yet be properly exercised, and the Eight Affairs of Government not yet be put into practice? Might the various officials not yet attend to their duties at the proper times, and the common people not yet enjoy peace? Any one of these would suffice to bring about calamity. Can we fail to take warning?
In essence, Heaven and Earth are one great father and mother. In serving his father, a son need only perceive what has no visible form, hear what has no sound, and arouse reverence and filial devotion. Why ask the cause of his father's anger? In serving Heaven, a ruler need only establish government through the virtue that safeguards the state before danger arises and secures order before disorder begins. Why ask whence Heaven's anomalies come?
To ease the anxiety that keeps Your Majesty occupied before dawn and late into the day, and to help avert calamity, nothing else is required [?; the transcription is displaced here]: simply follow the ancient precedent of Jizi's category of the Five Personal Conducts, and uphold the more recent instruction of the imperial ancestor concerning mutual cultivation. Preserve your heart as they preserved theirs, and examine yourself as they examined themselves. That is all. For the ruler must recognize the difficulty of being a ruler, and the minister the difficulty of being a minister. Henceforth, each must rest securely in his proper place and exercise restraint over his own conduct. Be solemnly respectful, reverent, and cautious, fearing idle ease; carefully cultivate frugality, guarding against extravagance; look to established statutes, preventing errors and transgressions; and consistently apply yourself to learning, diligently advancing in self-cultivation…

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
從諫弗咈廣言路也不貴異物恐喪志也
利用厚生畏民喦也命德討罪杜僭濫也
如此則
君德罔不脩矣必黜乃心必勵乃節天工未亮
思以亮之百揆未叙思以叙之嘉猷未告
思以告之財賦未慎思以慎之五禮未脩
思以脩之戎兵未詰思以詰之五刑未平
思以平之興作未息思以息之如此則臣
職罔不脩矣
===
一人建極于上百官承式于下將見五紀自兹
而協也百穀自兹而成也庶草自兹而蕃
也五福自兹而歛也尚何災變之不可弭
哉胤征曰先王克謹天戒臣人克有常憲
說命曰惟天聰明惟聖時憲惟臣欽若惟
民從又敢以是為
今日獻
第二問
毛渠
punctuated:
從諫弗咈，廣言路也；不貴異物，恐喪志也；利用厚生，畏民喦也；命德討罪，杜僭濫也。如此，則君德罔不脩矣。必黜乃心，必勵乃節。天工未亮，思以亮之；百揆未叙，思以叙之；嘉猷未告，思以告之；財賦未慎，思以慎之；五禮未脩，思以脩之；戎兵未詰，思以詰之；五刑未平，思以平之；興作未息，思以息之。如此，則臣職罔不脩矣。
一人建極于上，百官承式于下，將見五紀自兹而協也，百穀自兹而成也，庶草自兹而蕃也，五福自兹而歛也。尚何災變之不可弭哉？《胤征》曰：「先王克謹天戒，臣人克有常憲。」《說命》曰：「惟天聰明，惟聖時憲，惟臣欽若，惟民從。」又敢以是為今日獻。
第二問
毛渠
translation_en:
…Accept remonstrance without resisting it, thereby opening channels for counsel; do not prize exotic objects, lest they undermine your resolve; promote useful resources and enrich the people’s livelihood, mindful of the danger posed by the people; appoint the virtuous and punish the guilty, thereby preventing usurpation and indiscriminate grants of favor. In this way, no aspect of the ruler’s virtue will remain uncultivated. You ministers must put aside your selfish inclinations and strengthen your integrity. Where Heaven’s work remains unfulfilled, consider how to fulfill it; where the many affairs of government remain disordered, consider how to order them; where sound counsel has not been presented, consider how to present it; where revenues have not been carefully managed, consider how to manage them carefully; where the five categories of rites have not been duly maintained, consider how to maintain them; where military forces have not been put in order, consider how to put them in order; where the five punishments have not been applied equitably, consider how to apply them equitably; where construction projects have not ceased, consider how to bring them to an end. In this way, no ministerial duty will remain unfulfilled.
When the sovereign establishes the supreme standard above and the hundred officials follow his example below, we shall see the five reckonings of time brought into harmony, the many grains ripening, the various plants flourishing, and the five blessings gathering—all from this moment onward. What calamities or anomalies could then fail to be quelled? The Punitive Expedition of Yin states: “The former kings were scrupulously attentive to Heaven’s warnings, and their ministers maintained constant rules.” The Charge to Yue states: “Heaven is discerning; the sage takes it as his model. Ministers reverently follow, and the people obey.” I venture also to offer these words for the present day.
Second Policy Question
Mao Qu

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
同考試官訓導陳 批 此卷五策皆議論英發
才識過人而賞罰一策尤剴切明當且舉大有
之象以為對非博通經學者曷克爾邪得士如
此可以自慶矣
同考試官教諭鄧 批 此策敷對詳明末復援
引經史以為獻他日立
朝必善于規誨者
考試官教諭安 批 勵天下莫如賞罰司賞
罰莫如剛明此作得之且有斷制有抑揚固可
獻于
===
上矣
考試官教諭白 批 賞罰一策士子類能言
之求其鋪叙有條援據明實如此篇者亦不可
多得故録之
人君之勵天下也取諸大有夫離上乾下
居尊應天而大有之卦名焉彖曰其德剛
健而文明象曰君子以遏惡揚善順天休
命夫揚善者賞之謂也遏惡者罰之謂也
punctuated:
同考試官訓導陳批：此卷五策皆議論英發，才識過人，而賞罰一策尤剴切明當，且舉大有之象以為對，非博通經學者曷克爾邪？得士如此，可以自慶矣。

同考試官教諭鄧批：此策敷對詳明，末復援引經史以為獻，他日立朝，必善于規誨者。

考試官教諭安批：勵天下莫如賞罰，司賞罰莫如剛明。此作得之，且有斷制，有抑揚，固可獻于上矣。

考試官教諭白批：賞罰一策，士子類能言之，求其鋪叙有條、援據明實如此篇者，亦不可多得，故録之。

人君之勵天下也，取諸大有。夫離上乾下，居尊應天，而大有之卦名焉。《彖》曰：「其德剛健而文明。」《象》曰：「君子以遏惡揚善，順天休命。」夫揚善者，賞之謂也；遏惡者，罰之謂也。
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Assistant Instructor: All five policy essays in this script display brilliant argumentation and talent and insight surpassing those of others. The essay on rewards and punishments is especially incisive, clear, and apt. Moreover, it draws on the Image of the hexagram Dayou (Great Possession) in framing its response. How could anyone without a broad command of classical learning accomplish this? Having found a scholar like this, we may congratulate ourselves.

Comment by Associate Examiner Deng, Instructor: This policy essay develops its response fully and clearly, and concludes by drawing further on the classics and histories to offer counsel. When he takes his place at court in the future, he will surely excel in admonition and instruction.

Comment by Examiner An, Instructor: Nothing surpasses rewards and punishments for spurring all under Heaven to exert themselves; nothing surpasses firmness and discernment for administering rewards and punishments. This composition grasps that principle. It also displays decisive judgment and a judicious balance of restraint and encouragement. It is certainly fit to be presented to His Majesty.

Comment by Examiner Bai, Instructor: Most candidates can discuss the subject of rewards and punishments in a policy essay. Yet essays like this one, with an orderly exposition and clear, solid supporting evidence, are not often found. We have therefore included it in the record.

In spurring all under Heaven to exert themselves, the ruler takes his model from Dayou. With Li above and Qian below, occupying the honored position and responding to Heaven, the hexagram is named Great Possession. The Commentary on the Judgments says: “Its virtue is firm and vigorous, and cultured and discerning.” The Commentary on the Images says: “The gentleman thereby curbs evil and promotes good, complying with Heaven’s beneficent mandate.” Promoting good means rewarding it; curbing evil means punishing it.

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
順天休命則反之於身亦如其公而已然
非有文明之德則昜從而知非有剛健之
德則昜從而斷是故人君必取諸大有而
後可以司賞罰之權矣夫立天之道曰陰
與陽陽居春夏以長育爲事陰居秋冬以
肅殺爲事人君代天而爲之子於是乎則
陽以制賞則陰以制罰賞以陽制非私喜
也罰以陰制非私怒也故臯陶之謨曰天
命有德五服五章哉天討有罪五刑五用
===
哉盖言人君之賞罰皆當承天以從事不
得而私之也殷武之頌曰天命降監下民
有嚴不僭不濫不敢怠遑盖言高宗之刑
賞上若天意下順民心不得而私之也周
禮太宰以八則治都鄙七曰刑賞以馭其
威以八柄詔王馭羣臣一曰爵以馭其貴
二曰祿以馭其富三曰予以馭其幸四曰
置以馭其行五曰生以馭其福六曰奪以
馭其貧七曰廢以馭其罪八曰誅以馭其
punctuated: 順天休命，則反之於身，亦如其公而已。然非有文明之德，則昜從而知；非有剛健之德，則昜從而斷。是故人君必取諸大有，而後可以司賞罰之權矣。夫立天之道曰陰與陽，陽居春夏，以長育爲事；陰居秋冬，以肅殺爲事。人君代天而爲之子，於是乎則陽以制賞，則陰以制罰。賞以陽制，非私喜也；罰以陰制，非私怒也。故臯陶之謨曰：「天命有德，五服五章哉！天討有罪，五刑五用哉！」盖言人君之賞罰，皆當承天以從事，不得而私之也。《殷武》之頌曰：「天命降監，下民有嚴，不僭不濫，不敢怠遑。」盖言高宗之刑賞，上若天意，下順民心，不得而私之也。《周禮》太宰以八則治都鄙，七曰：「刑賞，以馭其威。」以八柄詔王馭羣臣，一曰：「爵，以馭其貴。」二曰：「祿，以馭其富。」三曰：「予，以馭其幸。」四曰：「置，以馭其行。」五曰：「生，以馭其福。」六曰：「奪，以馭其貧。」七曰：「廢，以馭其罪。」八曰：「誅，以馭其
translation_en: To follow Heaven’s gracious mandate means turning back to oneself and simply matching Heaven’s impartiality. Yet without the virtue of enlightened refinement, how could one discern matters [?]; without the virtue of firmness and vigor, how could one decide them [?]? Thus a ruler must take his example from the hexagram Great Possession (Dayou) before he can wield authority over rewards and punishments. What establishes the Way of Heaven is called yin and yang. Yang presides over spring and summer, attending to growth and nurture; yin presides over autumn and winter, attending to stern destruction. The ruler acts on Heaven’s behalf as its son. Accordingly, he models his institution of rewards on yang and his institution of punishments on yin. Rewards instituted according to yang do not arise from personal delight; punishments instituted according to yin do not arise from personal anger. Thus the Counsels of Gao Yao says: “Heaven appoints the virtuous: let the five kinds of ceremonial robes distinguish them! Heaven chastises the guilty: let the five punishments be applied to them!” This means that in rewarding and punishing, a ruler must always act in obedience to Heaven and may not make these matters subject to his personal inclinations. The hymn Martial Might of Yin says: “Heaven’s mandate descends to oversee them; the people below stand in awe. Neither erring in rewards nor excessive in punishments, he dares not lapse into idleness or leisure.” This means that Gaozong’s punishments and rewards accorded above with Heaven’s intent and below with the people’s hearts; he could not make them subject to his personal inclinations. In the Rites of Zhou, the Grand Steward governs the domains and their outlying settlements through eight regulations. The seventh is: “Punishments and rewards, by which to regulate their exercise of authority.” Through eight instruments of power, he instructs the king in governing his ministers. The first is: “Rank, by which to control their noble standing.” The second is: “Emoluments, by which to control their wealth.” The third is: “Grants, by which to control the favors they receive.” The fourth is: “Appointments, by which to control their conduct.” The fifth is: “Sparing life, by which to control their good fortune.” The sixth is: “Deprivation, by which to control their poverty.” The seventh is: “Dismissal, by which to control their offenses.” The eighth is: “Punishment, by which to control their …

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
過盖言制爵必以徳制禄必以功所以抑
僥求倖得之心而作進徳興功之志豈人
主所得而私之耶是則賞罰之柄在上而
不在下賞罰之行以公而不以私故有功
者必賞罔及于無功有罪者必刑罔及于
無罪則賞一以勸百罰一以懲衆此帝王
賞罰之公而後世莫之逮也夫勵精為治
宜莫如漢宣帝觀其詔曰有功不賞有罪
不刑雖唐虞不能化天下似矣然王成偽
===
增户口而封盖寛饒數犯上意而到安在
其為公乎功徳兼隆宜莫如唐太宗觀其
謂房玄齡曰有功則賞有罪則刑誰敢不
盡心力以脩職業似矣然長孫無忌以外
戚而封李君羡以讖言而誅安在其為公
乎好文守成宜莫如宋太宗觀其諭宋琪
曰賞當其功罰當其罪即無不治謂為飾
喜怒之具即無不亂似矣然因宣容再誤
之言而相趙普因久得士心之譖而罷曹彬
punctuated:
過。盖言制爵必以徳，制禄必以功，所以抑僥求倖得之心，而作進徳興功之志，豈人主所得而私之耶？是則賞罰之柄在上而不在下，賞罰之行以公而不以私。故有功者必賞，罔及于無功；有罪者必刑，罔及于無罪。則賞一以勸百，罰一以懲衆。此帝王賞罰之公，而後世莫之逮也。
夫勵精為治，宜莫如漢宣帝。觀其詔曰：「有功不賞，有罪不刑，雖唐虞不能化天下。」似矣！然王成偽增户口而封，盖寛饒數犯上意而到，安在其為公乎？功徳兼隆，宜莫如唐太宗。觀其謂房玄齡曰：「有功則賞，有罪則刑，誰敢不盡心力以脩職業？」似矣！然長孫無忌以外戚而封，李君羡以讖言而誅，安在其為公乎？好文守成，宜莫如宋太宗。觀其諭宋琪曰：「賞當其功，罰當其罪，即無不治；謂為飾喜怒之具，即無不亂。」似矣！然因宣容再誤之言而相趙普，因久得士心之譖而罷曹彬
translation_en:
…faults. This means that the conferral of rank must depend upon virtue, and the granting of emoluments upon merit, so as to restrain the desire to seek unearned advantage and obtain favors by chance, and to inspire the resolve to advance in virtue and achieve meritorious deeds. How could the ruler be entitled to dispense these for private ends? Thus the authority to reward and punish rests with those above, not those below, and rewards and punishments are administered impartially, not for private ends. Those with merit must therefore be rewarded, without rewards extending to those without merit; those guilty of offenses must be punished, without punishment extending to the innocent. Rewarding one thereby encourages a hundred; punishing one admonishes the multitude. Such was the impartiality of the ancient emperors and kings in rewarding and punishing, which later ages could not match.
For applying himself diligently to government, surely none could compare with Emperor Xuan of Han. Consider his decree: “If merit goes unrewarded and offenses unpunished, even Tang and Yu could not transform the realm.” This seems right! Yet Wang Cheng was enfeoffed after falsifying an increase in registered households, while Gai Kuanrao repeatedly offended the emperor and met his downfall [?]. Where was the impartiality in this? For eminence in both achievement and virtue, surely none could compare with Emperor Taizong of Tang. Consider his words to Fang Xuanling: “When there is merit, reward it; when there is an offense, punish it. Who would dare not devote all his mind and strength to fulfilling his official duties?” This seems right! Yet Zhangsun Wuji was enfeoffed because he was an imperial relative by marriage, while Li Junxian was executed because of a prophecy. Where was the impartiality in this? For loving literary culture and preserving his inherited achievements, surely none could compare with Emperor Taizong of Song. Consider his instructions to Song Qi: “If rewards match merit and punishments match offenses, good government invariably follows. If they are regarded as instruments for giving expression to pleasure and anger, disorder invariably follows.” This seems right! Yet he appointed Zhao Pu Chief Councilor because of a remark about “twice being misled” [?; 宣容再誤], and dismissed Cao Bin because of the slanderous allegation that he had long won the hearts of the soldiers…

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
安在其爲公乎噫之數君者或溺於好惡
之情而無剛斷以主之或徇於毁譽之偏
而無文明以察之故徒托諸空言耳此其
治所以弗逮於古也與仰惟我
皇上嗣服之初誕布
明詔忠諫則旌酬直言也節義則表顯忠貞也
賞所當賞矣倖位則黜抑貪饕也奸黨則
誅除邪佞也罰所當罰矣雖帝王之賞罰
何以加焉但治道每難於克終人情或懈
===
于持久夫賞所以懋功也或有功而弗賞
或非功而賞加焉於是乎賞不克終矣罰
所以討罪也或有罪而弗罰或非罪而罰
加焉於是乎罰不克終矣賞罰者天下之
公法也而可或違乎方
今大有之時也而凡賞罰之行其惟順天休命
乎其惟剛健文明乎是故賞必當功如書
所謂車服以庸功懋懋賞爵罔及惡德而
後爲賞之公罰必當罪如書所謂怙終賊
punctuated:
安在其爲公乎？噫！之數君者，或溺於好惡之情，而無剛斷以主之；或徇於毁譽之偏，而無文明以察之，故徒托諸空言耳。此其治所以弗逮於古也與？

仰惟我皇上嗣服之初，誕布明詔：忠諫則旌，酬直言也；節義則表，顯忠貞也。賞所當賞矣。倖位則黜，抑貪饕也；奸黨則誅，除邪佞也。罰所當罰矣。雖帝王之賞罰，何以加焉？但治道每難於克終，人情或懈于持久。夫賞所以懋功也，或有功而弗賞，或非功而賞加焉，於是乎賞不克終矣。罰所以討罪也，或有罪而弗罰，或非罪而罰加焉，於是乎罰不克終矣。賞罰者，天下之公法也，而可或違乎？方今大有之時也，而凡賞罰之行，其惟順天休命乎！其惟剛健文明乎！是故賞必當功，如《書》所謂「車服以庸」、「功懋懋賞」、「爵罔及惡德」，而後爲賞之公。罰必當罪，如《書》所謂「怙終賊
translation_en:
…Where was his impartiality? Alas! These several rulers either succumbed to their personal likes and dislikes, lacking firm resolution to govern them, or followed biased praise and blame, lacking enlightened discernment to examine them. Thus they merely entrusted their principles to empty words. Is this not why their government fell short of antiquity?

We reverently consider how, at the beginning of his reign, our Emperor widely promulgated his enlightened decree: loyal remonstrance was to be honored, rewarding forthright speech; integrity and righteousness were to receive public commendation, making loyalty and constancy manifest. Those deserving reward were rewarded. Those who obtained office through favor were to be dismissed, restraining the greedy and rapacious; treacherous factions were to be executed, eliminating the wicked and sycophantic. Those deserving punishment were punished. How could even the rewards and punishments of the ancient emperors and kings surpass these? Yet in governing, carrying things through to the end is always difficult, and human resolve may slacken over time. Rewards serve to encourage meritorious achievement. If those with merit go unrewarded, or rewards are bestowed where there is no merit, the proper administration of rewards is not sustained. Punishments serve to chastise wrongdoing. If the guilty go unpunished, or punishment is imposed where there is no guilt, the proper administration of punishments is not sustained. Rewards and punishments are the impartial laws of all under Heaven: how could any departure from them be permissible? Now is a time of Great Possession. In administering all rewards and punishments, surely we must follow Heaven’s gracious mandate! Surely we must exercise firmness, vigor, and enlightened discernment! Thus rewards must correspond to merit, as the Book of Documents says: “Chariots and robes are bestowed for service”; “For outstanding merit, give outstanding rewards”; and “Let rank not extend to those of evil character.” Only then are rewards impartial. Punishments must correspond to offenses, as the Book of Documents says: “Those who persist obstinately are to be put to death…

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
刑具嚴天威德威惟畏而後為罰之公猶
恐其或偏也有公心焉如周人所謂不賞
私勞不罰私怨是也猶恐其弗協也有公
典焉如禮所謂爵人於朝與士共之刑人
於市與衆棄之是也又恐其弗中也有懼
心焉如蔡聲子所謂懼及淫人懼及善人
是也又恐其或蔽也臨事而思焉如魏徵
所謂行爵賞則思因喜而僭施刑罰則思
因怒而濫是也如此則賞一人而天下莫
不勸罰一人而天下莫不懲大有之治永
保於無疆矣區區芻蕘之見不識可裨
===
聖治否邪敢僭著於篇用附傳言之義
第三問
同考試官訓導黄　批　士子於儒道類能言之
要其所當為與其所當用漫不知旨此作熟於
典故精於討論而且加以潤色之詳蓋有得於
儒道而言之親切者矣
楊縉
punctuated:
刑」、「具嚴天威」、「德威惟畏」，而後為罰之公。猶恐其或偏也，有公心焉，如周人所謂「不賞私勞，不罰私怨」是也。猶恐其弗協也，有公典焉，如禮所謂「爵人於朝，與士共之；刑人於市，與衆棄之」是也。又恐其弗中也，有懼心焉，如蔡聲子所謂「懼及淫人，懼及善人」是也。又恐其或蔽也，臨事而思焉，如魏徵所謂「行爵賞，則思因喜而僭；施刑罰，則思因怒而濫」是也。如此，則賞一人而天下莫不勸，罰一人而天下莫不懲，大有之治永保於無疆矣。區區芻蕘之見，不識可裨聖治否邪？敢僭著於篇，用附傳言之義。
第三問
同考試官訓導黄批：士子於儒道，類能言之。要其所當為與其所當用，漫不知旨。此作熟於典故，精於討論，而且加以潤色之詳，蓋有得於儒道而言之親切者矣。
楊縉
translation_en:
…punishment,” “all stand in awe of Heaven’s majesty” [?], and “the majesty of virtue alone is to be feared.” Only then are punishments impartial. Still fearing that there may be partiality, one maintains an impartial mind, as in the Zhou saying: “Do not reward private services or punish private grudges.” Still fearing that decisions may not accord with proper standards, one has impartial statutes, as the Book of Rites says: “Confer rank upon a man at court, sharing the decision with the officers; punish a man in the marketplace, joining the multitude in rejecting him.” Further fearing that decisions may miss the mark, one maintains a fearful vigilance, as Shengzi of Cai said: “Fear that rewards may reach the wicked; fear that punishments may reach the good.” Further fearing that one’s judgment may be clouded, one reflects when matters arise, as Wei Zheng said: “When conferring ranks and rewards, consider whether joy might lead to excessive grants; when imposing penalties and punishments, consider whether anger might lead to excess.” In this way, rewarding one person encourages everyone under Heaven, and punishing one person admonishes everyone under Heaven. The flourishing rule of Great Possession will thus be preserved forever without limit. These humble views are those of a mere gatherer of grass and firewood; I do not know whether they can benefit Your Majesty’s sagely government. I venture to set them down here, in keeping with the principle of transmitting the words of the lowly to those above.
Third Question
Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, Assistant Instructor: Scholars can generally speak about the Confucian Way. Yet when it comes to what they ought to do and how they ought to be employed, they scarcely understand its purport. This composition shows familiarity with historical precedents and precision in discussion, further enhanced by thorough literary polishing. Its author has evidently gained an understanding of the Confucian Way and speaks of it with intimate insight.
Yang Jin

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
同考試官訓導劉　批〔别白諸儒優劣用儒是否歷歷可信且詞氣雅健良是筭手〕
考試官教諭安　批〔說儒道意出盖必有見者〕
考試官教諭白　批〔議論醇正非徒口耳之為〕
對業儒者當造其至用儒者貴識其真知
業矣而不求其至則道有所未盡知用矣
而不識其真則道有所不行求之必欲其
===
至則道全於我而後達之可施用之必得
其真則道見於治而後用無不顯是儒一
也修己者當審從違之途用人者當澄真
偽之鑑而後兩得之矣執事發策以儒道
為問盖以為學者分内事也惜淺見不足
以窺此始舉其所聞而復之且儒之道大
矣其理無所不該而其用無所不有帝王
之所以授受六經之所以傳述皆是也自
孔子以其行對哀公而其說始詳以其學
punctuated:
同考試官訓導劉，批〔别白諸儒優劣、用儒是否，歷歷可信，且詞氣雅健，良是筭手。〕
考試官教諭安，批〔說儒道意出，盖必有見者。〕
考試官教諭白，批〔議論醇正，非徒口耳之為。〕
對：業儒者當造其至，用儒者貴識其真。知業矣，而不求其至，則道有所未盡；知用矣，而不識其真，則道有所不行。求之必欲其至，則道全於我，而後達之可施；用之必得其真，則道見於治，而後用無不顯。是儒一也，修己者當審從違之途，用人者當澄真偽之鑑，而後兩得之矣。執事發策，以儒道為問，盖以為學者分内事也。惜淺見不足以窺此，始舉其所聞而復之。且儒之道大矣，其理無所不該，而其用無所不有，帝王之所以授受、六經之所以傳述，皆是也。自孔子以其行對哀公，而其說始詳；以其學
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Liu, an Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔The distinctions among the merits and shortcomings of Confucian scholars, and the rightness or wrongness of employing them, are clearly drawn and convincing. Moreover, the diction and tone are elegant and vigorous. Truly a skilled hand.〕
Examiner An, an Instructor, comments: 〔The discussion of the Confucian Way brings out its meaning [?]; surely the writer has insight.〕
Examiner Bai, an Instructor, comments: 〔The argument is sound and correct, not merely a matter of repeating what one has heard.〕
In reply: Those who pursue Confucian learning should attain its utmost excellence; those who employ Confucian scholars must discern the genuine among them. If one knows to pursue this learning but does not seek its utmost excellence, the Way remains incompletely realized. If one knows to employ its scholars but cannot discern the genuine, the Way remains incompletely practiced. If one seeks it with the determination to reach its utmost excellence, the Way becomes complete within oneself, and can then be extended and put into practice. If, in employing scholars, one invariably secures the genuine, the Way manifests itself in government, and its efficacy is evident in every application. Thus, Confucian learning is one: those cultivating themselves must carefully judge which paths to follow and which to reject; those employing others must keep clear the mirror by which they distinguish the genuine from the false. Only then can both achieve their ends.
You gentlemen have issued a policy question concerning the Confucian Way, presumably because you regard it as a matter within a student's proper sphere. Regrettably, my shallow understanding is insufficient to fathom it; I therefore begin by offering what I have heard in reply. Great indeed is the Confucian Way! Its principles embrace everything, and its applications encompass everything. What the sage emperors and kings handed down and received, and what the Six Classics transmitted and expounded, are all this Way. Only when Confucius answered Duke Ai concerning its conduct did its exposition begin to become detailed; through its learning …

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
教子夏而其名始定柰何慕其美者多僞
爲喜其名者無眞見而脩己用人之間誠
有不得不辯者焉故自夫業儒者言之豎
儒之敗事如漢高之所叱俗儒之不達如
宣帝之所譏是雖有其名而無望乎儒之
道矣宿儒以處翰林如宋祖之所擇大儒
以名當世如李固之所造是各有所得而
近似乎儒之實矣若夫儒者高蹈如程顥
深致夫温公之稱大醇小疵如荀楊均得
===
夫韓子之贊其亦儒之表表者與統一後
學爲群儒首如仲舒之在漢朝風流儒雅
爲世所宗如顧榮賀循之在江左其亦儒
之錚錚者與夫爲儒而至於豎與俗固可
醜矣然而李固之明哲不足榮循之清虛
未脱荀子之喜爲異說楊子之尚夫艱深
皆非儒之所當法也必也仲舒程顥其庶
幾焉若論其至則道如周公學如孔子而
後無愧由程董而進之其斯有以盡儒者
punctuated: 教子夏而其名始定。柰何慕其美者多僞爲，喜其名者無眞見，而脩己用人之間，誠有不得不辯者焉。故自夫業儒者言之，豎儒之敗事，如漢高之所叱；俗儒之不達，如宣帝之所譏：是雖有其名，而無望乎儒之道矣。宿儒以處翰林，如宋祖之所擇；大儒以名當世，如李固之所造：是各有所得，而近似乎儒之實矣。若夫儒者高蹈，如程顥，深致夫温公之稱；大醇小疵，如荀楊，均得夫韓子之贊：其亦儒之表表者與！統一後學，爲群儒首，如仲舒之在漢朝；風流儒雅，爲世所宗，如顧榮、賀循之在江左：其亦儒之錚錚者與！夫爲儒而至於豎與俗，固可醜矣。然而李固之明哲不足，榮循之清虛未脱，荀子之喜爲異說，楊子之尚夫艱深，皆非儒之所當法也。必也仲舒、程顥，其庶幾焉。若論其至，則道如周公，學如孔子，而後無愧。由程董而進之，其斯有以盡儒者
translation_en:
…taught Zixia this learning, and only then was its name established. Yet why do those who admire its excellence so often put on a false appearance, while those who delight in its name lack true insight? In cultivating oneself and employing others, there are indeed distinctions that must be drawn. Thus, speaking of those who pursue Confucian learning: petty scholars ruin affairs, as did those whom Gaozu of Han rebuked; vulgar scholars lack understanding, as did those whom Emperor Xuan mocked. Though they possess the name, they have no hope of attaining the Confucian Way. Seasoned scholars occupy posts in the Hanlin Academy, like those selected by Taizu of Song; great scholars win renown in their age, like those whom Li Gu visited. Each has attained something and approaches the substance of a true Confucian scholar. As for lofty conduct among Confucians, Cheng Hao earned the profound praise of the Duke of Wen, Sima Guang; for great purity with minor flaws, Xunzi and Yang Xiong both received Master Han Yu’s commendation. Were these not outstanding Confucians? Dong Zhongshu at the Han court brought later scholars together under a unified teaching and stood at the head of the Confucians; Gu Rong and He Xun in Jiangzuo possessed refinement and scholarly elegance and were revered by their contemporaries. Were these not distinguished Confucians?

For a Confucian to descend to pettiness and vulgarity is certainly shameful. Yet Li Gu’s deficiency in discerning wisdom, Gu Rong’s and He Xun’s failure to free themselves from the pursuit of purity and emptiness, Xunzi’s fondness for unconventional doctrines, and Yang Xiong’s esteem for difficulty and obscurity are all things that Confucians should not emulate. Surely it is Dong Zhongshu and Cheng Hao who come close to the ideal. If we speak of its highest attainment, however, only when one’s Way resembles that of the Duke of Zhou and one’s learning resembles that of Confucius can one be worthy of the name without shame. Advancing further from Cheng Hao and Dong Zhongshu, might one thereby fulfill the Confucian scholar’s…

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
之業矣乎自夫用儒者言之漢武之雅尚
儒術而散亡詩書自是表章理宗之褒封
儒先而周程諸賢悉加榮典若可美矣然
所好公孫弘之流所崇惟既往之賢宜無
益於治也溺儒冠而不好如漢高絀儒術
而不任如景帝固可恨矣而寬仁有王者
之度恭儉盡君德之實故不至於損也若
夫擇五更三老之賢明尊師重傅之典見
於漢明帝之時然也然稽古之華雖有可
===
觀而去古則遠矣文涉義理悉見黜落六
經四書為世大禁見於宋寧宗之時然也
然晦庵諸賢尚賴贊襄而國脉猶存矣夫
待儒而至於惡與禁固皆非矣然而武帝
之好名理宗之好古高帝之嫚罵景帝之
絀儒均之不能用也無已則明帝其近似
焉若論其真則湯之用尹文之用望而後
為得由明帝而進之其斯有以盡用儒之
道矣乎雖然為儒固貴於造其極矣然造
punctuated:
之業矣乎？自夫用儒者言之，漢武之雅尚儒術，而散亡詩書自是表章；理宗之褒封儒先，而周程諸賢悉加榮典，若可美矣。然所好公孫弘之流，所崇惟既往之賢，宜無益於治也。溺儒冠而不好，如漢高；絀儒術而不任，如景帝，固可恨矣。而寬仁有王者之度，恭儉盡君德之實，故不至於損也。若夫擇五更三老之賢，明尊師重傅之典，見於漢明帝之時然也。然稽古之華雖有可觀，而去古則遠矣。文涉義理，悉見黜落，六經四書為世大禁，見於宋寧宗之時然也。然晦庵諸賢尚賴贊襄，而國脉猶存矣。夫待儒而至於惡與禁，固皆非矣。然而武帝之好名，理宗之好古，高帝之嫚罵，景帝之絀儒，均之不能用也。無已，則明帝其近似焉。若論其真，則湯之用尹、文之用望，而後為得。由明帝而進之，其斯有以盡用儒之道矣乎？
雖然，為儒固貴於造其極矣，然造
translation_en:
…the vocation of a Confucian scholar, might one not thereby fulfill it? Speaking of employing Confucian scholars, Emperor Wu of Han esteemed Confucian learning, and from his time the scattered and lost texts of the Odes and Documents were brought to prominence. Emperor Lizong bestowed honorific titles upon earlier Confucian masters, and worthies such as Zhou Dunyi and the Cheng brothers all received honors. These actions might seem praiseworthy. Yet the former favored men of Gongsun Hong’s ilk, while the latter revered only worthies who had already passed away: naturally, this brought no benefit to government. To urinate into a scholar’s cap and dislike scholars, as Gaozu of Han did, or to reject Confucian learning and refuse to employ its adherents, as Emperor Jing did, was certainly regrettable. Yet the former’s magnanimity and benevolence displayed the bearing of a true king, while the latter’s reverence and frugality fulfilled the substance of a ruler’s virtue. Thus their conduct did not ultimately cause harm. As for selecting worthy elders for the honorary positions of wugeng and sanlao and giving conspicuous expression to the rites of honoring teachers and respecting tutors, this occurred under Emperor Ming of Han. Yet although the outward splendor of his emulation of antiquity had something worth admiring, he remained far removed from antiquity. Compositions touching upon moral principles were all rejected, and the Six Classics and Four Books became objects of sweeping prohibition: this occurred under Emperor Ningzong of Song. Yet the state still relied on the assistance of worthies such as Hui’an [Zhu Xi], and its lifeblood endured. To treat Confucian scholars with hatred and prohibition was certainly wrong in both cases. Nevertheless, Emperor Wu’s love of renown, Lizong’s love of antiquity, Gaozu’s insulting abuse, and Emperor Jing’s rejection of scholars all amounted equally to an inability to employ them. If one must choose, Emperor Ming came close. As for truly employing scholars, only Tang’s employment of Yi Yin and King Wen’s employment of Lü Wang attained the right way. By advancing beyond Emperor Ming, might one not thereby fulfill the Way of employing Confucian scholars?
Nevertheless, in being a Confucian scholar, what matters is indeed reaching the highest attainment. Yet to reach it…

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
之則本於志用儒固貴於識其真矣然識
之則在於心志不定則將棄於半塗況有
他岐者矣心不正則將惑於小道況有嫉
賢者矣是立志者爲儒之本而正心者用
儒之本也請以是爲爲儒用儒之所先何
如謹對
第四問
王儒
同考試官訓導吴　批〔此篇於齊魯風俗及所以治之者敷荅詳明而才氣充溢其齊魯之良〕
===
也乎
考試官教諭安　批〔核而整雅而當質而可行非識治體者疇克爾耶宜錄以式〕
考試官教諭白　批〔博考故實而斷制允當末復舉子路治蒲之政以爲牧民者告是可與言政矣〕
政不能無弊救之者存乎時俗不能無移
易之者存乎變時者救弊之宜變者易俗
punctuated:
之，則本於志。用儒固貴於識其真矣，然識之則在於心。志不定，則將棄於半塗，況有他岐者矣；心不正，則將惑於小道，況有嫉賢者矣。是立志者爲儒之本，而正心者用儒之本也。請以是爲爲儒、用儒之所先，何如？謹對。

第四問
王儒
同考試官訓導吴　批〔此篇於齊魯風俗及所以治之者，敷荅詳明，而才氣充溢，其齊魯之良〕也乎？
考試官教諭安　批〔核而整，雅而當，質而可行，非識治體者疇克爾耶？宜錄以式。〕
考試官教諭白　批〔博考故實，而斷制允當，末復舉子路治蒲之政，以爲牧民者告，是可與言政矣。〕

政不能無弊，救之者存乎時；俗不能無移，易之者存乎變。時者，救弊之宜；變者，易俗
translation_en:
…attaining it rests upon resolve. In employing Confucian scholars, one must indeed value discerning the genuine among them; yet such discernment depends upon the heart. If resolve is unsettled, one will abandon the undertaking halfway—how much more so when other paths beckon! If the heart is not upright, one will be beguiled by lesser ways—how much more so when one harbors jealousy of the worthy! Thus establishing resolve is the foundation of becoming a Confucian scholar, and rectifying the heart is the foundation of employing Confucian scholars. May I propose that these be given priority in becoming and employing Confucian scholars? I respectfully submit this reply.

Fourth Question
Wang Ru 王儒

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu 吴, Assistant Instructor: “This essay expounds in detail and with clarity the customs of Qi and Lu and the means of governing them, displaying abundant talent and vigor. Is its author perhaps an outstanding man of Qi and Lu?”

Comment by Examiner An 安, Instructor: “Exact and orderly, elegant and apt, substantive and practicable: who could achieve this without understanding the essentials of governance? It should be recorded as a model.”

Comment by Examiner Bai 白, Instructor: “He examines historical precedents widely, and his judgments are thoroughly sound. At the end he further cites Zilu’s administration of Pu to offer counsel to those who shepherd the people. Here is someone with whom one can discuss government.”

Government cannot be free of abuses; remedying them depends upon timing. Customs cannot remain without shifts; transforming them depends upon adaptation. Timing is what makes the remedy for abuses appropriate; adaptation is what, in transforming customs, …

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
之機也救其弊不因其時弊不可得而救
矣易其俗不通其變俗不可得而易矣故
易貴隨時詩美移俗為民牧者可不加之
意乎夫禹別九州海岱惟青州即齊地也
濟河惟兖州即魯地也武王克殷奄有天
下乃辨九州之國正東曰青州其鎮曰沂
山河東曰兖州其鎮曰岱山於是以太公
有大功則封于營丘謂之齊以周公有大
功則封于曲阜謂之魯太公治齊曰舉賢
===
而上功其政固無不善然一於剛嚴故周
公以為後世必有爭奪之禍周公治魯曰
尊尊而親親其政亦無不善然一於寬緩
故太公以為後世必有寖微之憂太公之
齊因其俗簡其禮傳至桓公管仲相焉設
輕重以富國合諸侯以圖伯身在陪臣而
取三歸故其士好經術矜功名其失夸詐
其俗彌侈伯禽之魯變其俗革其禮傳
至定公孔子相焉別五土而物其所生誅
punctuated: 之機也。救其弊不因其時，弊不可得而救矣；易其俗不通其變，俗不可得而易矣。故《易》貴隨時，《詩》美移俗，為民牧者可不加之意乎？夫禹別九州，海岱惟青州，即齊地也；濟河惟兖州，即魯地也。武王克殷，奄有天下，乃辨九州之國：正東曰青州，其鎮曰沂山；河東曰兖州，其鎮曰岱山。於是以太公有大功，則封于營丘，謂之齊；以周公有大功，則封于曲阜，謂之魯。太公治齊，曰：「舉賢而上功。」其政固無不善，然一於剛嚴，故周公以為後世必有爭奪之禍。周公治魯，曰：「尊尊而親親。」其政亦無不善，然一於寬緩，故太公以為後世必有寖微之憂。太公之齊，因其俗，簡其禮。傳至桓公，管仲相焉，設輕重以富國，合諸侯以圖伯，身在陪臣而取三歸。故其士好經術，矜功名，其失夸詐，其俗彌侈。伯禽之魯，變其俗，革其禮。傳至定公，孔子相焉，別五土而物其所生，誅
translation_en:
…is the opportunity for changing customs. If one remedies abuses without regard to the times, those abuses cannot be remedied; if one changes customs without understanding how to adapt, those customs cannot be changed. Thus the Book of Changes values acting in accordance with the times, and the Book of Odes praises the transformation of customs. Can those who shepherd the people fail to give this their attention?

When Yu divided the Nine Provinces, the region between the sea and Mount Dai constituted Qingzhou: this was the territory of Qi. The region between the Ji and He rivers constituted Yanzhou: this was the territory of Lu. King Wu conquered Yin and possessed all under Heaven. He then distinguished the territories of the Nine Provinces: directly east lay Qingzhou, whose guardian mountain was Mount Yi; east of the He River lay Yanzhou, whose guardian mountain was Mount Dai. Because Taigong had rendered great service, he was enfeoffed at Yingqiu, which was called Qi; because Zhougong had rendered great service, he was enfeoffed at Qufu, which was called Lu.

In governing Qi, Taigong declared: “Promote the worthy and esteem achievement.” His government was certainly good in every respect, but it relied exclusively on firmness and severity. Zhougong therefore thought that later generations would inevitably suffer the calamity of contention and usurpation. In governing Lu, Zhougong declared: “Honor those entitled to honor and cherish one’s kin.” His government likewise was good in every respect, but it relied exclusively on leniency and accommodation. Taigong therefore thought that later generations would inevitably face the danger of gradual decline.

When Taigong went to Qi, he followed its customs and simplified its rites. By the time the succession reached Duke Huan, Guan Zhong served as his chief minister. He instituted policies for regulating the relative values of goods to enrich the state and united the feudal lords in pursuit of hegemony. Though himself merely a lord’s minister, he acquired the ‘Three Returns’ estate [?]. Thus Qi’s scholars favored the study of the classics and prided themselves on achievement and reputation; their faults were boastfulness and deceit, and their customs became increasingly extravagant.

When Boqin went to Lu, he changed its customs and reformed its rites. By the time the succession reached Duke Ding, Kongzi served as his chief minister. He distinguished the five types of soil and classified what each produced, and executed…

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
少正卯而除其亂政又脩六經以明王道
故其民上禮義重廉恥其業桑麻其俗儉
嗇夷考其時齊雖强太公之遺法盡變魯
雖弱周公之遺化猶存故孔子曰齊一變
至於魯魯一變至於道此之謂也夫政以
人而異俗以政而移政之行於古者未必
宜於今俗之移於今者未必同於古禮曰
廣谷大川異制民生其間者異俗剛柔輕
重遲速異齊五味異和器械異制衣服異
===
宜脩其教不易其俗齊其政不易其宜顧
為民牧者治之何如耳將治之以寛與然
政寛則民慢慢則至於弛將治之以猛與
然猛則民殘殘則至於刻是故不必一於
猛也不必一於寛也惟隨其時而救之因
其變而易之當猛而猛如王臻之剛嚴決
事可也當寛而寛如宋璟之仁信為政可
也非廉無以勵俗如李恂之清約束下可
也非教無以正俗如李邕之詩書訓士可
punctuated:
少正卯而除其亂政，又脩六經以明王道，故其民上禮義，重廉恥，其業桑麻，其俗儉嗇。夷考其時，齊雖强，太公之遺法盡變；魯雖弱，周公之遺化猶存。故孔子曰：「齊一變，至於魯；魯一變，至於道。」此之謂也。
夫政以人而異，俗以政而移。政之行於古者，未必宜於今；俗之移於今者，未必同於古。《禮》曰：「廣谷大川異制，民生其間者異俗，剛柔輕重遲速異齊，五味異和，器械異制，衣服異宜。脩其教，不易其俗；齊其政，不易其宜。」顧為民牧者治之何如耳。
將治之以寛與？然政寛則民慢，慢則至於弛。將治之以猛與？然猛則民殘，殘則至於刻。是故不必一於猛也，不必一於寛也，惟隨其時而救之，因其變而易之。當猛而猛，如王臻之剛嚴決事可也；當寛而寛，如宋璟之仁信為政可也；非廉無以勵俗，如李恂之清約束下可也；非教無以正俗，如李邕之詩書訓士可
translation_en:
…Shao Zhengmao, thereby eliminating his disruption of government, and also put the Six Classics in order to elucidate the Kingly Way. Thus the people esteemed ritual propriety and righteousness and valued integrity and a sense of shame; their occupations were cultivating mulberry and hemp, and their customs were frugal and sparing. Examining that period, we find that although Qi was strong, the laws bequeathed by Taigong had all been altered; although Lu was weak, the transforming influence bequeathed by the Duke of Zhou still survived. Thus Confucius said: “With one transformation, Qi could attain the level of Lu; with one transformation, Lu could attain the Way.” This is what he meant.
Government differs according to the person administering it, and customs shift with government. Policies practiced in antiquity are not necessarily suitable today; customs as transformed today are not necessarily the same as those of antiquity. The Book of Rites says: “Broad valleys and great rivers differ in configuration, and the people living among them differ in customs. Their firmness and gentleness, gravity and levity, slowness and swiftness differ in degree; the five flavors are blended differently; implements differ in design; and clothing differs according to what is appropriate. Cultivate their instruction without changing their customs; bring order to their government without changing what suits them.” It depends only on how those who shepherd the people govern them.
Should they govern with leniency? Yet when government is lenient, the people grow lax, and laxity leads to a breakdown of discipline. Should they govern with severity? Yet severity leaves the people afflicted, and such affliction leads to harsh oppression. Thus one need not adhere exclusively to severity, nor exclusively to leniency. One should remedy conditions according to the times and adjust one's measures as circumstances change. When severity is called for, be severe: one may follow Wang Zhen in deciding affairs with firmness and strictness. When leniency is called for, be lenient: one may follow Song Jing in governing with benevolence and trustworthiness. Where integrity is indispensable to improving customs, one may follow Li Xun in restraining subordinates through purity and frugality. Where instruction is indispensable to correcting customs, one may follow Li Yong in instructing scholars through the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents…

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
也民或阻饑思以恤之如富弼之賑濟活
民可也民或弄兵思以綏之如李固之恩
信化盜可也抑猶未盡也昔子路治蒲三
年孔子過之入其境曰善哉由也恭敬以
信矣入其邑曰善哉由也忠信以寛矣至
其庭曰善哉由也明察以斷矣此則牧斯
民者之所當法也愚也生斯土育斯庠固
不敢議政然明問及之亦不敢隱焉執事
倘采而告諸牧民者其亦斯民之幸哉
===
第五問
同考試官教諭徐　批〔賦役之法正今時之急務而荅者類不切民此作救弊體民之意鑿鑿〕
〔可行且措詞雅有法度要亦有用之才也他日〕
袁繼
入對
大廷尚亦以平民之政陳之
考試官教諭安　批〔此策可見之行非徒然〕
〔者故錄之〕
punctuated:
也。民或阻饑，思以恤之，如富弼之賑濟活民可也；民或弄兵，思以綏之，如李固之恩信化盜可也。抑猶未盡也。昔子路治蒲三年，孔子過之，入其境曰：「善哉，由也！恭敬以信矣。」入其邑曰：「善哉，由也！忠信以寛矣。」至其庭曰：「善哉，由也！明察以斷矣。」此則牧斯民者之所當法也。愚也生斯土，育斯庠，固不敢議政，然明問及之，亦不敢隱焉。執事倘采而告諸牧民者，其亦斯民之幸哉！

第五問

同考試官教諭徐，批〔賦役之法，正今時之急務，而荅者類不切民。此作救弊體民之意，鑿鑿〕〔可行，且措詞雅有法度，要亦有用之才也。他日〕袁繼入對大廷，尚亦以平民之政陳之。

考試官教諭安，批〔此策可見之行，非徒然〕〔者，故錄之。〕
translation_en:
…would also be appropriate. If the people suffer famine, one should consider how to relieve them: one may follow Fu Bi in distributing relief to keep the people alive. If the people take up arms, one should consider how to pacify them: one may follow Li Gu in reforming bandits through kindness and trustworthiness. Yet this still does not exhaust the matter. In former times, after Zilu had governed Pu for three years, Confucius passed through it. Upon entering its territory, he said, “Excellent indeed is You! He is respectful and trustworthy.” Upon entering its town, he said, “Excellent indeed is You! He is loyal, trustworthy, and generous.” Upon reaching his court, he said, “Excellent indeed is You! He is perceptive and decisive.” This is what those who shepherd these people ought to emulate. I, in my ignorance, was born in this land and educated in its school. Certainly I dare not presume to discuss government; yet, since your discerning question touches upon it, neither dare I conceal my views. Should you accept them and convey them to those who shepherd the people, would this not be a blessing for these people!

Fifth Question

Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor: “The regulations governing taxation and labor service are precisely an urgent concern of our time, yet most respondents fail to address the people’s circumstances. This essay’s proposals for remedying abuses and taking account of the people are concrete and practicable. Moreover, its phrasing is elegant and well ordered. Its author is, in sum, a man of useful talent. When Yuan Ji someday presents his response before the imperial court, may he likewise set forth policies that bring peace to the people.” [The transcription appears to interleave the name Yuan Ji with the conclusion of the comment; its placement is uncertain.]

Comment by Examiner An, Instructor: “This policy essay can be put into practice; it is no mere empty exercise. Accordingly, it has been included.”

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭白 批〔得救時意〕
賦役之法去古者皆非中賦役之論違古
者皆非善甚矣古之法立之善也行者不
合乎此則或增或損均之失中論者不明
乎此則或誕或略悉為未善行之不中則
民無以立論之不明則國無以守此善政
不復於千載而獨有見於我
朝也請以是而復執事平民之問可乎夫治
人者明道術以馭下食人者出財力以供
===
上國未有不取民之財用民之力者故任
土之貢大禹敘之力役之征孟子言之然
財者民之心力者民之命聖人必厚之節
之而有適中之道焉何後世可為而不為
也是故邦國之賦始於堯舜定於周成而
野外國中無慮什一上有以足國下無以
損民信乎中正之道也後世如文景之減
租於漢太宗之輕賦於唐大略取於三十
五十之一較之始皇興作攘夷而收大半
punctuated:
考試官教諭白批〔得救時意〕

賦役之法，去古者皆非中；賦役之論，違古者皆非善。甚矣，古之法立之善也！行者不合乎此，則或增或損，均之失中；論者不明乎此，則或誕或略，悉為未善。行之不中，則民無以立；論之不明，則國無以守。此善政不復於千載，而獨有見於我朝也。請以是而復執事平民之問，可乎？夫治人者，明道術以馭下；食人者，出財力以供上。國未有不取民之財、用民之力者。故任土之貢，大禹敘之；力役之征，孟子言之。然財者民之心，力者民之命，聖人必厚之節之，而有適中之道焉。何後世可為而不為也？是故邦國之賦，始於堯舜，定於周成，而野外國中，無慮什一。上有以足國，下無以損民，信乎中正之道也！後世如文景之減租於漢，太宗之輕賦於唐，大略取於三十五十之一。較之始皇興作攘夷而收大半
translation_en:
Examiner Bai, Instructor, comments: 〔It grasps the intent of remedying the troubles of the age.〕

Methods of taxation and labor service that depart from antiquity all fail to strike the proper balance; discussions of taxation and labor service that contravene antiquity are all unsound. How excellent were the laws established in antiquity! If those administering them do not conform to these standards, they either increase or reduce the burdens, in either case losing the proper balance. If those discussing them do not understand these standards, their arguments are either fanciful or cursory, and all are unsound. When administration fails to strike the proper balance, the people have no means of sustaining themselves; when discussion lacks clarity, the state has no means of preserving itself. Such good government went unrestored for a thousand years and has appeared again only under our dynasty. May I use this to answer your question, honored examiners, concerning bringing peace to the people?

Those who govern others clarify the Way and the methods of government to direct those below; those who feed others contribute wealth and labor to support those above. No state has ever failed to draw upon the people's wealth and employ their labor. Thus, Yu the Great set out the tribute assessed according to the land, and Mengzi discussed the levy of labor service. Yet wealth is the people's heart, and labor their lifeblood. The sages therefore ensured that their resources were ample and that demands upon their labor were restrained, establishing a properly balanced course. Why could later generations follow it, yet did not?

State taxation thus began with Yao and Shun and was definitively established under King Cheng of Zhou. In both the outlying countryside and the capital, it amounted generally to one tenth. Above, it sufficed to meet the state's needs; below, it did no harm to the people. Truly, this was the balanced and correct course! In later ages, such measures as the reduction of land taxes by Emperors Wen and Jing of Han and the lightening of taxation by Emperor Taizong of Tang generally took one thirtieth or one fiftieth. Compared with the First Emperor, who undertook construction projects and repelled the barbarians, collecting more than half …

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
之賦揚炎量出制入而作兩税之法雖爲
彼善於此皆非中正之道焉尚何嬴歟之
論哉邦國之役載之王制詳之周禮而歲
用民力不過三日國之事既有以集民之
時亦無以奪信乎經久之規也後世限之
二旬如唐初之制有所免役如惠帝之法
大略出於省事節力之意較之武帝常役
尚多而更有七科之謫昭帝他役既繁而
復有三更之役雖爲差强人意皆非經久
===
之規焉亦何苦樂之遠哉奈何王安石之
對神宗曰古者非特什一之税而已他賦
甚衆盖曲學强辯之說耳公羊所謂什一
行而頌聲作者乃有見矣唐太宗之論百
姓曰亡事則驕逸勞役則易使盖晚年怠
政之故耳王符所謂省民繇役使之愛日
者則近是矣噫行者不善而善者不中
論者不是而是者亦非詳此成周之治千
載不復見也我
punctuated: 之賦，揚炎量出制入而作兩税之法，雖爲彼善於此，皆非中正之道焉，尚何嬴歟之論哉？邦國之役，載之《王制》，詳之《周禮》，而歲用民力不過三日。國之事既有以集，民之時亦無以奪，信乎經久之規也。後世限之二旬，如唐初之制；有所免役，如惠帝之法，大略出於省事節力之意。較之武帝常役尚多，而更有七科之謫；昭帝他役既繁，而復有三更之役，雖爲差强人意，皆非經久之規焉，亦何苦樂之遠哉？奈何王安石之對神宗曰：「古者非特什一之税而已，他賦甚衆。」盖曲學强辯之說耳。《公羊》所謂「什一行而頌聲作」者，乃有見矣。唐太宗之論百姓曰：「亡事則驕逸，勞役則易使。」盖晚年怠政之故耳。王符所謂「省民繇役，使之愛日」者，則近是矣。噫！行者不善，而善者不中；論者不是，而是者亦非詳。此成周之治，千載不復見也。我
translation_en:
…levies, and Yang Yan’s establishment of the Two-Tax system, which determined revenues according to expenditures: although the former measures were better than these, none followed the properly balanced way. What further discussion could there be of a surplus [?]?

The labor services of the realm are recorded in the Royal Regulations and detailed in the Rites of Zhou: the people’s labor was employed for no more than three days annually. The affairs of state could thus be accomplished without encroaching upon the people’s time. This was indeed an enduring rule. Later measures, such as the early Tang regulation limiting service to twenty days and Emperor Hui’s provisions exempting some from service, broadly reflected an intention to reduce demands and conserve the people’s strength. Compare these with Emperor Wu’s numerous regular labor obligations, compounded by punitive service imposed upon seven categories of offenders, or Emperor Zhao’s already burdensome other services, compounded by service in three rotations. Although the former measures were somewhat satisfactory, none constituted an enduring rule. How great, then, was the distance between suffering and contentment?

Why, then, did Wang Anshi say in reply to Emperor Shenzong: “In antiquity there was more than merely the tithe; other levies were exceedingly numerous”? This was merely an argument grounded in distorted learning and strained disputation. The Gongyang Commentary’s statement, “When the tithe is implemented, voices of praise arise,” shows real insight. Emperor Taizong of Tang said of the common people: “Without tasks, they become arrogant and indolent; subjected to labor service, they are easy to command.” This surely arose from his neglect of government in his later years. Wang Fu’s statement, “Reduce the people’s corvée obligations and enable them to cherish their days,” comes close to what is right.

Alas! What was put into practice was not good, and what was good was not properly balanced. The arguments advanced were not correct, and those that were correct were insufficiently thorough. This is why the governance of the Zhou at its height has not been seen again for a thousand years. Our…

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
朝
祖宗立法之善
列聖守法之詳大畧與成周同隨田畝之廣狹
為租稅之多寡而賦無不均計丁糧之多
寡為徭役之重輕而役無不平民享太和
之休久矣比歲以來則有不然者雖屢蒙
蠲租之
詔而未觧至骨之負累布輕徭之政而未蘇剥
膚之困信有如執事所言者此有司不能
===
奉行
德意之咎固非可以歲凶歸也意者去冗食
之員黜貪墨之吏禁奢侈之風恤災患之
苦其或民命庶幾也不然雖有成周輕賦
之政其何能救乎省土木之役嚴私役之
法戒淫巧之作下寛簡之令其或民力庶
幾也不然雖有成周輕役之法亦將何補
乎然其仁民之端則又有所本而願以七
月之詩無逸之書為
punctuated:
朝祖宗立法之善，列聖守法之詳，大畧與成周同。隨田畝之廣狹，為租稅之多寡，而賦無不均；計丁糧之多寡，為徭役之重輕，而役無不平。民享太和之休久矣。比歲以來，則有不然者。雖屢蒙蠲租之詔，而未觧至骨之負累；布輕徭之政，而未蘇剥膚之困。信有如執事所言者，此有司不能奉行德意之咎，固非可以歲凶歸也。
意者，去冗食之員，黜貪墨之吏，禁奢侈之風，恤災患之苦，其或民命庶幾也。不然，雖有成周輕賦之政，其何能救乎？省土木之役，嚴私役之法，戒淫巧之作，下寛簡之令，其或民力庶幾也。不然，雖有成周輕役之法，亦將何補乎？然其仁民之端，則又有所本，而願以《七月》之詩、《無逸》之書為
translation_en:
…dynasty’s founding ancestors established excellent laws, and its succession of sage rulers observed them with meticulous care, broadly matching the achievements of Zhou at its height. Taxes were assessed according to the extent of the fields, so that all taxation was equitable; labor service was apportioned according to the numbers of registered adult males and the grain-tax assessments, so that all service obligations were fairly distributed. The people have long enjoyed the blessings of profound harmony. In recent years, however, matters have been otherwise. Although edicts remitting taxes have repeatedly been granted, burdens that penetrate to the bone remain unrelieved; although policies reducing labor service have been promulgated, distress that strips the skin remains unalleviated. Matters are indeed as you, honored examiner, have said. This is the fault of the responsible officials, who have failed to carry out the benevolent imperial intentions; it certainly cannot be attributed merely to a bad harvest.
I suggest dismissing superfluous officials who consume public resources, removing corrupt officials, prohibiting extravagant customs, and relieving the suffering caused by disasters. Then there might be some hope for the people’s survival. Otherwise, even with the light-taxation policies of Zhou at its height, how could they be saved? Reduce construction labor, enforce strictly the laws against requisitioning labor for private purposes, prohibit the production of excessively elaborate luxuries, and issue lenient and uncomplicated ordinances. Then there might be some hope for the people’s strength to recover. Otherwise, even with the laws of Zhou at its height that lightened labor service, what benefit would there be? Yet the impulse to treat the people humanely has a further foundation, and I would wish to take the poem “Seventh Month” (Qi yue) and the Documents chapter “Against Idleness” (Wu yi) and, for …

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text: 聖天子獻馬不知執事以為是否
punctuated: 聖天子獻馬，不知執事以為是否？
translation_en: …to present to the sagely Son of Heaven [?]. I do not know whether you, the officials in charge, consider this right or wrong.

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
山東鄉試錄後序
山東以海岱雄天下靈秀所
萃昭於人文盖自微子立而
殷禮存於宋伯禽封而周禮
在於魯陳敬仲奔而韶樂傳
於齊迨夫孔子作而三千七
十子羣習於洙泗之間晚以
===
道之弗行又取六經而删定
之以詔萬世其後曾子子思
孟子之傳述左氏之春秋伏
生之尚書梁丘賀之易轅固
之詩雖純駁不同而其人胥
此焉出是故天下之文獻莫
先焉
punctuated:
山東鄉試錄後序

山東以海岱雄天下，靈秀所萃，昭於人文。盖自微子立而殷禮存於宋，伯禽封而周禮在於魯，陳敬仲奔而韶樂傳於齊。迨夫孔子作，而三千七十子羣習於洙泗之間，晚以道之弗行，又取六經而删定之，以詔萬世。其後曾子、子思、孟子之傳述，左氏之春秋，伏生之尚書，梁丘賀之易，轅固之詩，雖純駁不同，而其人胥此焉出。是故天下之文獻莫先焉。
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Shandong Provincial Examination

Shandong stands magnificent among all the lands under Heaven, with its sea and Mount Tai. Here numinous excellence gathers and shines forth in human culture. From the time Weizi was established as ruler, the rites of Yin survived in Song; when Boqin was enfeoffed, the rites of Zhou resided in Lu; and when Chen Jingzhong fled to Qi, the Shao music was transmitted there. Then Confucius arose, and three thousand and seventy disciples studied together between the Zhu and Si rivers. Late in life, because his Way was not being put into practice, he took up the Six Classics and edited and established their texts to instruct all generations to come. Thereafter came the teachings transmitted by Zengzi, Zisi, and Mengzi; Master Zuo’s Spring and Autumn Annals; Fu Sheng’s Book of Documents; Liangqiu He’s Book of Changes; and Yuan Gu’s Book of Odes. Although these differed in their purity or admixture, all these men came from this region. Thus, in cultural records and worthy scholars, no place under Heaven takes precedence over Shandong.

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
今上改元嘉靖越四年乙酉當大
比如例錄成常作而歎曰猗
我濟濟乎皇皇乎士也何以
副厥薦嘗歷覲前輩之校文
於茲類叙吾孔子之鄉以為
東人諭嗟乎孔子豈東人之
所得私哉孔子之道布在方
===
策穹壤所際罔不欽崇趍而
詣之者上也勉强而由之者
次也口誦其言而躬自畔之
民斯下矣是皆存乎其人而
地弗與焉故曰孔子非東人
之所得私也雖然於東人抑
有榮焉子貢曰仲尼日月也
punctuated: 今上改元嘉靖，越四年乙酉，當大比，如例錄成，常作而歎曰：「猗！我濟濟乎、皇皇乎士也，何以副厥薦？嘗歷覲前輩之校文於茲，類叙吾孔子之鄉，以為東人諭。嗟乎！孔子豈東人之所得私哉？孔子之道布在方策，穹壤所際，罔不欽崇。趍而詣之者上也，勉强而由之者次也，口誦其言而躬自畔之，民斯下矣。是皆存乎其人，而地弗與焉。故曰：孔子非東人之所得私也。雖然，於東人抑有榮焉。子貢曰：「仲尼，日月也。」
translation_en: In the fourth year after His Present Majesty adopted the reign title Jiajing, the yiyou year [1525], the triennial Provincial Examination fell due. When the record had been compiled according to precedent, Chang [?] rose and sighed, saying: “Ah! Our scholars, so numerous and distinguished, so splendid! How will they prove worthy of their recommendation? I have seen how our predecessors who assessed examination writings here generally spoke of this as the homeland of our Confucius, to offer instruction to the people of Shandong. Alas! How could Confucius be the exclusive possession of the people of Shandong? The Way of Confucius is set forth in written texts; throughout the expanse of heaven and earth, none fail to revere it. Those who hasten toward it and attain it are the highest; those who exert themselves to follow it come next. Those who recite his words but personally act against them are the lowest among the people. All this depends upon the individual; place has no part in it. Thus I say that Confucius cannot be the exclusive possession of the people of Shandong. Nevertheless, the people of Shandong do have an honor in this. Zigong said, ‘Zhongni [Confucius] is the sun and moon.’ …

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
邵子曰仲尼以萬世為土夫
日月之照臨下土何所不到
而暘谷咸池則日月之所自
出也今夫煕明之景清虚之
輝夫人皆仰之而生於所自
出者獨不能窺其全光焉寧
不為日月之恥哉東藩固孔
===
子之暘谷咸池也為之後者
因言以求其意由曲以會其
全庸不違夫静塞不變於時
天下之人将指而榮之曰是
真孔子之郷人乎常等為
國薦賢之意亦可以少伸矣不
然冐其遺緒以為資身之策
punctuated: 邵子曰：「仲尼以萬世為土。」夫日月之照臨下土，何所不到？而暘谷、咸池，則日月之所自出也。今夫煕明之景、清虚之輝，夫人皆仰之，而生於所自出者，獨不能窺其全光焉，寧不為日月之恥哉？東藩固孔子之暘谷、咸池也。為之後者，因言以求其意，由曲以會其全，庸不違夫静，塞不變於時，天下之人将指而榮之曰：「是真孔子之郷人乎！」常等為國薦賢之意，亦可以少伸矣。不然，冐其遺緒以為資身之策，
translation_en: Master Shao said, “Zhongni takes the myriad generations as his territory [?].” Wherever the sun and moon shine upon the earth below, what place do they fail to reach? Yet Yanggu and Xianchi are the places from which they emerge. Now everyone looks up to their bright radiance and pure light. If those born where they emerge should alone fail to perceive their full brilliance, would this not disgrace the sun and moon? This eastern province is indeed Confucius’s Yanggu and Xianchi. If those who come after him seek his meaning through his words and comprehend the whole through its particulars, do not depart from stillness in their ordinary conduct [?], and remain unchanged by the times even in adversity [?], people throughout the realm will point to them with admiration and say, “These truly are fellow townsmen of Confucius!” The wish of Chang and his colleagues to recommend worthy men for the state may then find some small fulfillment. Otherwise, if they lay claim to his legacy as a means of advancing themselves, …

title: 嘉靖四年山東鄉試錄
text:
孔子恥之〔常〕亦恥之〔常〕不敏
竊有志于孔氏而又幸以試
事入其鄉冀其人之無或負
也於其賓興之始申以告之
直隸鎮江府丹徒縣儒學教
諭安〔常〕謹序
punctuated:
孔子恥之，〔常〕亦恥之。〔常〕不敏，竊有志于孔氏，而又幸以試事入其鄉，冀其人之無或負也。於其賓興之始，申以告之。
直隸鎮江府丹徒縣儒學教諭安〔常〕謹序。
translation_en:
…Confucius would be ashamed of this; I, Chang, would likewise be ashamed. Though I am of little ability, I privately aspire to follow Confucius. Having also had the good fortune to enter his native region on examination duties, I hope that none of its people will betray his legacy. At the outset of the proceedings for honoring and recommending worthy men, I reiterate these words to them.
Preface respectfully written by An Chang, Instructor in the Confucian School of Dantu County, Zhenjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili).
